title: fix: resolve feedback bug round-up (#354, #357, #348, #349, #359)
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Fixes #354
Fixes #357
Fixes #348
Fixes #349
Fixes #359

A round of `[Feedback]` bug fixes from the Aug 18 review:

- **#354** — GlobalSearch crashed with `x.localeCompare is not a function` when a contact's `updatedAt`/`createdAt`/`lastSeen` arrived as a Firestore `Timestamp` (from `serverTimestamp()`). The recency sort now normalizes stamps to ISO strings before comparing.
- **#357** — The Directory "Combine tags" popup (`z-50`) rendered under the sidebar (`z-[70]`), covering its left edge on wide screens. Raised to `z-[100]` to match the other modals.
- **#348 / #349** — To-do assignee lists (Prayer page, Attendance, Coordination Notes) surfaced seed/service accounts. Added `isServiceAccountName` in `src/lib/utils.ts` (excludes `cisa-*` and `reviewer-*`) and applied it to all three team loaders, replacing CoordinationNotes' inline `cisa-`-only check.
- **#359** — The Directory "Group" filter dropdown rendered a blank option for contacts with an empty `role`. Falsy roles are now dropped from the option list.

## Verified

- `npm run typecheck` ✓
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors ✓
- `npm run test` — 1679 passed ✓
- `npm run test:coverage` — thresholds met (Statements 90.9 ≥ 90.5, Branches 79.67 ≥ 79.0, Functions 87.93 ≥ 87.5, Lines 92.65 ≥ 92.0) ✓
- `npm run build` ✓

Ground truth for the service-account and blank-role fixes came from prod Firestore (`users` + `contacts`).

## Tests

Regression tests added/updated in `GlobalSearch.test.tsx`, `CombineTagsModal.test.tsx`, `utils.test.ts`, `PrayerList.test.tsx`, `Directory.test.tsx`.

title: feat: central shortcut registry + expanded command palette (#337)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
Implements #337 — a central shortcut registry where every command declares its scope, description, shortcut, and handler in one place. The same registration both binds the key and populates the ⌘K palette, so shortcuts teach themselves.

## Changes
- **New `src/lib/commands.ts`** — registry with `Command { id, scope, description, shortcut, minRole?, hidden?, when?, available?, handler }`. One `document`-level dispatcher binds keys; scopes rank `overlay > compose > global`, most-recently-registered wins within a scope. `useCommand` hook, `registerCommand`, `subscribeCommands`/`getCommands` (palette listing), `shortcutLabel`.
- **Migrated the five ad-hoc listeners**:
  - `GlobalSearch.tsx` — ⌘K open-search → `search.open` (global, hidden from listing)
  - `LogVisitModal.tsx` — ⌘↵ save → `logvisit.save` (overlay, available only while open); Esc stays inline
  - `TodoComposer.tsx` — ⌘↵ create → `todo.create` (overlay); Esc stays inline
  - `Thread.tsx` — ⌘↵ post + reply → `thread.post` / `thread.reply:{id}` (compose, gated to the focused element via `when`)
  - `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — ⌘↵ send → `feedback.send` (compose)
- **Palette** — role-filtered **Shortcuts** section lists the commands the user can currently take with their key hints; clicking runs the handler.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Every existing shortcut still works (existing tests green: GlobalSearch ⌘K, Thread ⌘↵, TodoComposer Ctrl+Enter)
- [x] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role (`src/test/GlobalSearch.test.tsx`)
- [x] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable (`src/test/commands.test.ts` — 15 tests)

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` ✓
- `npm run lint` ✓ (0 new warnings)
- `npm run test` ✓ (1661 passed)
- `npm run test:coverage` ✓ — lines 92.68% / branches 79.85% (thresholds held, ratcheted up)
- `npm run build` ✓

title: feat: shared date-bucket util adopted in History (#327)
label: CLOSED
body:
Fixes #327

## What
Extracts the app's date-grouping into one shared vocabulary instead of leaving it inline in History (and re-implemented again by the future merged attention feed). Three pure functions in `src/components/landing/dateBuckets.ts`:

- `bucketFor(date)` — maps a date to a bucket key (Today / Yesterday / This week / Last week / Earlier this month / Last month / Longer ago)
- `bucketLabel(key)` — warm label in the app's voice
- `bucketOrder(key)` — 0..6 for sorting

Cut-offs (calendar-day): 0, 1, 2–6, 7–13, 14–30, 31–60, 61+. Calendar-day semantics mean an item from 23:59 yesterday is "Yesterday", not "Today". Built on the existing `parseMs`/`DAY_MS` helpers.

## Adoption
History's `dayInfo` now routes its Today/Yesterday boundary through `bucketFor`/`bucketLabel`, keeping its finer per-day weekday/date markers for older moments — rendering is identical. My Day and the team-inbox feed adoption lands with the merged attention feed (#330), which is blocked on this issue.

## Tests
- New `src/test/dateBuckets.test.ts` (32 tests) covering every boundary (0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 30, 31, 60, 61 days), input types (string/Date/ms/null/invalid), the 23:59-yesterday calendar edge, and label/order tables.
- Full pre-PR gate passes: `typecheck`, `lint` (0 errors), `vitest run --coverage` (lines 92.67 vs 92.0 threshold), `build`.

title: [Macro study] Expand the command palette + central shortcut registry
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Code**

## Problem

Keyboard handling is ad hoc and undiscoverable: `⌘K` in `GlobalSearch.tsx:295`, `⌘Enter` in `Thread.tsx`, `TodoComposer.tsx`, `LogVisitModal.tsx`, and `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — five separate listeners, no registry, nothing listed anywhere. The ⌘K palette offers four quick actions with no way to learn what else exists.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/` — a registry where every command declares its scope, description, condition, and handler, so the same registration both binds the key and populates the command palette. Shortcuts teach themselves.

## Explicitly NOT adopting

Their leader grammar (`c`+letter creates, `g`+letter goes) and vim navigation (`j`/`k`, `gg`, `shift+G`). Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day; this app serves students and Full-timers opening it a few times a week, often on a phone. Also skipping their priority chain and scope inheritance — far more machinery than this needs.

## Scope

- A small registry: id, scope, description, handler
- Both binds the shortcut and populates the ⌘K palette
- Migrate the five existing ad-hoc listeners onto it
- Palette lists available actions with their shortcuts

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every existing shortcut still works
- [ ] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role
- [ ] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable

title: [Macro study] Four new to-do creation entry points
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Code + light design**

## Problem

To-dos can be created from two places: highlighting a line on a Board page, and from an interaction. Macro's argument is that trackers go stale because logging costs a context switch — they made tasks creatable from seven places for exactly this reason.

## Scope — four new entry points

1. **From an attendance absence** — marking someone absent on the Gatherings screen is the exact moment someone thinks "I should check on them." Highest value of the four.
2. **From the visit log form** — `Visit.followUpTaskId` already exists in the data model, so this is wiring, not schema. Makes creating the follow-up part of writing the visit up rather than a separate step.
3. **From a chat message** — hover / long-press → "Make a to-do", carrying the message as source. Mirrors the Board highlight flow already built.
4. **From a prayer** — turn a burden into a concrete follow-up while keeping the prayer linked as source.

## Implementation note

One shared helper over `addTodo` in `src/lib/todos.ts`; each site differs only in which source it links. The existing `sourceDocId` / `sourceInteractionId` pattern extends naturally.

## Design needed

Small — the affordance in four placements. Reuse the existing "Make a to-do" treatment from the Board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four create a to-do linked back to its source
- [ ] The source is visible on the resulting to-do row
- [ ] Available on mobile where the source screen exists

title: [Macro study] Role-aware first-run checklist
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

There is no first-run experience. New trainees arrive every semester, and the four roles (Full-timer / Trainee / Student / Community) see substantially different apps.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/features/getting-started/getting-started-types.ts` — a checklist where each row has an optional `isComplete()` read reactively from **live state**, plus `observe()` for event-driven completion, defaulting to "clicking it completes it". Their comment on why completion is derived rather than remembered:

> never persisted itself, so it stays honest when e.g. a tool is disconnected

## Scope

- Dismissible checklist on Home, rows differing per role
- Completion derived from real state — "logged your first conversation" is true because they did, not because they clicked a button once
- Collapsible sections, persisted per user

## Design needed

Checklist layout, per-role row sets, and copy for four roles in the app's existing voice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each role sees rows relevant to what they can actually do
- [ ] Completion reads live state; deleting the underlying data un-completes the row
- [ ] Dismissible, and stays dismissed

title: [Macro study] Live contact pill with hover preview
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Attaching a contact to a message stores `ChatAttachment { type, id, name, subtitle }` — a display cache written at attach time. It goes stale, and checking one fact about the person means opening `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (2,402 lines).

## What Macro does

Every @mention renders as a live pill carrying its target's *current* metadata — a task pill shows the task's status and priority — and previews on hover. Context without a click, and the pill can't go stale because it reads live.

## Scope

- Contact pill showing stage and last-seen, read live rather than from the cached `subtitle`
- Hover preview card on desktop; tap-to-preview on mobile
- Contacts only for now; the other seven `ChatAttachment` types can follow if this lands well

## Design needed

Pill treatment (including stage colour, which already exists as `StageChip`) and the preview card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pill reflects a stage change without the message being re-sent
- [ ] Preview shows enough to answer "who is this and where are they at" without opening the modal
- [ ] Works on mobile web and in `apps/mobile/`

title: [Macro study] One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · ⚠️ **Has a privacy consequence — read before designing**

## Problem

A conversation about one person can live in three places today:

1. `contacts/{id}/threads` — the walking-together thread (Trainee-visible)
2. The Comments tab in `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (~line 2079) — gated `role === "admin" || isAdmin`, **Full-timers only**
3. Messages, with the contact attached via `ChatAttachment`

Someone asking "what did we say about Sarah?" has to check all three.

## What Macro does

*"Every deal gets its own channel, automatically, pinned right to the deal record."* Their argument: a CRM comment box always loses to where the conversation really happens, because people comment *and then* go ping the channel anyway. So the record's notes ARE the chat system, not a parallel one.

## ⚠️ Blocker — decide before this is designed

The Comments tab is Full-timer-only; the walking-together thread is Trainee-visible. **Merging them changes who can read pastoral oversight notes that were written under a different expectation.** This is a privacy change, not just a data migration. Pick one:

- **(recommended)** Migrated comments carry a visibility flag and the merged thread filters by role — preserves the original audience while still giving one place to look. Costs a `firestore.rules` change.
- Comments migrate into a Full-timer-only section of the merged thread.
- Existing comments stay in place; only *new* conversation goes to the thread.

## Scope

- `contacts/{id}/threads` becomes the single conversation surface
- Comments migrated per the decision above, with a migration script
- Attaching a contact in Messages links into that same thread rather than starting a parallel one
- `firestore.rules` updated and reproduced against the emulator **before** the rule is edited (rules deploys have their own CI gate — budget for it)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visibility decision recorded in this issue before design starts
- [ ] No existing comment becomes readable by someone who could not read it before
- [ ] Emulator-backed rules tests, red before green
- [ ] Migration is reversible or dry-runnable

title: [Macro study] Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Row actions differ per view — the same intent is worded and placed differently on a person, a prayer, a visit, and a gathering. Users learn the app per screen instead of once.

## What Macro does

Defines an action vocabulary once and applies it to every object type — `apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/tokens.ts` has `entity.action.{markDone, markRead, delete, rename, share, favorite, createReminder, assignee, status, ...}`. Same key, same menu, same wording regardless of what the object is. Their keyboard reference has a single "Entity Actions" section covering all types.

## Scope

- Agree one action set — done, follow up later, share, make a to-do, open — and the exact wording, in the app's existing warm voice
- One row/overflow menu component consumed by person, prayer, visit, and gathering rows
- First consumer is the merged attention feed (#330), so co-design with it

## Design needed

The overflow menu, its trigger, and mobile (long-press drawer) treatment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One menu component used by all four row types
- [ ] "Done" means the same thing everywhere
- [ ] Wording reviewed against the existing nav voice ("The Journey", "On our hearts", "Looking back")

title: [Macro study] Notification stacking by target
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Pairs with #330

## Problem

`NotificationCenter.tsx` renders notifications flat. Three people commenting on one contact produces three rows, so the one thing that actually needed attention gets buried. This matters more here than in a workspace tool — notification volume per person is low, so a flat list is mostly noise around a few signals.

## What Macro does

Collapses all notifications about the same entity into a single row showing the most recent, with the rest behind a collapsible list (`DEFAULT_VISIBLE_COUNT = 3`), and lets you mark the whole stack read or done at once. See `apps/web/src/features/entity/extractors-notification/notification-stacks.tsx`.

## Scope

Group rows by target entity, show a count ("3 new on Sarah"), expand on demand, mark-all-done on the stack.

## Design needed

Stacked row treatment, count badge, expanded state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple notifications about one contact render as one row with a count
- [ ] Expanding shows the individual entries
- [ ] Mark-done on the stack clears all of them

title: [Macro study] Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Blocked on #326 (read/done model) and #327 (date bucketing)

## Problem

"What needs my attention" is split across three surfaces:

- My Day's hand-assembled sections (`src/views/MyDay.tsx`, 1,192 lines)
- `FromTraineesInbox` — the Full-timer oversight feed
- `NotificationCenter` — the bell, a separate list entirely

Someone has to check all three to know where they stand. And `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` only tracks *scanned*, which is passive — without a "done", the list only grows, so it stops being a list anyone can finish, and people stop opening it.

## What Macro does

One list holding email, messages, @mentions, task assignments, and agent results. `e` marks done and removes the item. Their framing: *"You can think of the Signal view as your action list."* The stance is that you should check exactly one thing.

**Not adopting:** their AI-sorted Signal/Noise split (volume doesn't justify it, and the failure mode — AI hides something pastoral — is worse than the problem), and Inbox-Zero-as-pressure. A list of people you haven't followed up with is not disposable the way email is; "clearing" a person is a strange verb, and a UI that rewards emptying the list can teach people to dismiss rather than follow up. Take *"done is distinct from seen"*; leave the pressure to reach zero.

## Scope

- One attention feed on My Day carrying team activity, to-do assignments, thread questions, and notifications
- Explicit per-row "done" that removes it, built on #326
- Date-group headers from #327
- Bell becomes push delivery only, not a second list

## Design needed

Row anatomy per item kind, the done affordance, group headers, empty state. Desktop, `MyDayMobile.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/`.

## Watch

The feed reads contacts, interactions, a `collectionGroup` over threads, notifications, and to-dos. My Day already does several of these — measure read volume before adding more, and check whether new composite indexes are needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One feed replaces the three surfaces; the bell no longer maintains a parallel list
- [ ] Marking done removes the row and persists per-user
- [ ] Each of the four roles sees an appropriate feed
- [ ] Firestore read count per load measured and recorded

title: [Macro study] Audit and derive Contact activity fields
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only**

## Problem

`Contact` carries `lastSeen`, `lastContactedDate`, `lastContactedBy`, `lastContactedById`, and `hasNewActivity`. All of these look derivable from interactions, visits, and attendance — but if any is hand-entered, or written at only some of the call sites, it goes stale silently. A stale `lastContactedDate` breaks exactly the question the app exists to answer: who have we not seen in a while.

## What Macro does

From their CRM docs: *"records create themselves … stages are all manual: Macro doesn't yet know where a company lies in your pipeline and relies on you."* A clean line between what the system can observe and what only a person knows. Their "Last Interaction" is a sortable column precisely because it is never typed.

Stage stays manual here too — that is judgment, and correctly a human's.

## Scope

1. Map every write of the five fields across web (`src/lib/`, `src/views/`, `src/components/modals/`) and `apps/mobile/`
2. Route them through one derived update triggered by logging an interaction, a visit, or an attendance mark
3. Remove any path that accepts them as direct user input

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Logging an interaction, a visit, and an attendance mark each update the fields identically
- [ ] No UI writes these fields directly
- [ ] Tests cover all three event types
- [ ] Audit findings recorded in the issue before the fix lands, so the size of the drift is known

title: [Macro study] Frecency ranking in Global Search
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Highest value-per-line item in the study

## Problem

`src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` does substring filtering, caps each group at `GS_MAX = 4`, and applies **no ranking**. With no query, "recent people" sorts by `updatedAt` — which is *someone else's* edit, not your usage. So the people you open every day are not the people you are shown.

## What Macro does

`crates/frecency` computes, per user per entity:

```
frequency = log2(event_count + 2)
recency   = Σ over last 10 events of  exp(-0.1 × hours_ago) × weight
score     = 0.7 × frequency + 0.3 × recency

weights:  open = +2.0,  ping = 0.0,  close = -1.0
```

The negative close weight is the interesting part: opening something and immediately closing it is evidence it was the *wrong* result, so it demotes itself.

Their own client ships a much cheaper version for the command palette — `apps/web/src/features/command/recency.ts` is ~20 lines, a persisted `Record<commandId, timestamp>`. **That is the version to copy**, not the Rust service.

## Scope

- Track opens in a per-uid localStorage store, reusing the pub/sub pattern already in `src/lib/inboxReads.ts`
- Rank results by score; keep the substring filter as the gate (frecency only orders what already matched)
- Consider whether `GS_MAX = 4` should rise once ordering is meaningful

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a contact repeatedly floats it to the top of the no-query list
- [ ] Open-then-immediately-close does not promote a result
- [ ] Scoring is a pure function with unit tests; storage is tested separately

title: [Macro study] Shared date bucketing util (Today / Yesterday / This Week / Older)
label: CLOSED
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Feeds the merged attention feed's grouping

## Problem

Date grouping is implemented inline in History, My Day, and the activity feed, each slightly differently. The merged attention feed will want the same grouping, which would make a fourth copy.

## What Macro does

`crates/models_grouping/src/date_buckets.rs` — a fixed vocabulary as three tiny pure functions:

| Bucket | Range | Order |
|---|---|---|
| Today | 0 days | 0 |
| Yesterday | 1 day | 1 |
| This Week | 2–6 days | 2 |
| Last Week | 7–13 days | 3 |
| This Month | 14–30 days | 4 |
| Last Month | 31–60 days | 5 |
| Older | 61+ days | 6 |

Their docs frame it as a product feature, not formatting: it "keeps a busy list scannable without changing any of your filters or sorting."

## Scope

`bucketFor(date)`, `bucketLabel(key)`, `bucketOrder(key)` in a shared util, built on the existing `daysSince` / `parseMs` in `src/components/landing/helpers.ts`. Adopt in History, My Day, and the activity feed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Three pure functions, no view imports
- [ ] Unit tests at every boundary: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 30, 31, 60, 61 days
- [ ] Existing groupings in History / My Day / activity render identically or better
- [ ] Warm labels agreed — the app says "Looking back", not "This Month", so copy should match the app's voice rather than Macro's

title: [Macro study] Unify read/done state into one per-user model
label: OPEN
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · **Prerequisite for the merged attention feed**

## Problem

Five mechanisms currently answer fragments of one question — "has this person seen / dealt with this?":

- `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` — localStorage, per-uid, ids like `contact:<id>` (already an entity ref)
- `src/lib/convHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden conversations
- `src/lib/messageHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden messages
- `Notification.readBy` / `dismissedBy` — Firestore arrays
- `Contact.reviewed` — a boolean on the shared domain object

Three storage strategies, no shared vocabulary. `Contact.reviewed` is the worst of them: it puts a per-user workflow state onto a shared record, so when two Full-timers walk with the same trainee it is ambiguous who reviewed it.

## What Macro does

Separates two orthogonal axes and applies both uniformly to any entity: **read** (I have seen it) and **done** (I have dealt with it). `inboxReads` today only models "scanned", which is passive — there is no way to clear something off your list.

## Scope

- One per-user store keyed by entity ref (`contact:<id>`, `interaction:<id>`, `thread:<id>` — the shape `inboxReads.ts` already uses), with `read` and `done` as separate axes.
- Migrate `inboxReads`, `convHides`, `messageHides` behind it.
- Leave `Notification.readBy` alone for now — it is genuinely shared state, not a per-device preference.
- Plan the `Contact.reviewed` migration but do not remove the field in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing inbox-read and hide behaviour is unchanged from the user's point of view
- [ ] A `done` axis exists and is independently settable from `read`
- [ ] Unit tests cover set/clear/subscribe on both axes and the migration from each legacy store

title: [Macro study] Adopt product patterns from the Macro codebase (tracking)
label: OPEN
body:
Tracking issue for work adopting product patterns from a read-only study of [macro-inc/macro](https://github.com/macro-inc/macro) (AGPLv3, SolidJS + Rust all-in-one workspace).

## Why

Macro's CRM, tasks, docs, and channels map closely onto People/The Journey, to-dos, Coordination Notes, and Messages. Their product decisions are stances rather than infrastructure, so they port even though none of their code does. Their core arguments:

- **Trackers go stale** because logging costs a context switch — so make creating an entry possible from wherever the decision is actually made.
- **Records should build themselves**; only judgment (stage) is manual.
- **You should check one thing** to know what needs your attention, and "done" must be a real verb distinct from "seen."
- **A record's notes ARE the chat system** — a separate comments box always loses to where the conversation really happens.

## Scaled down deliberately

Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day. This app serves four roles who open it a few times a week, often on a phone. Keyboard-first navigation (vim keys, `c`/`g` leader grammar) was evaluated and **declined**; splits/window management, the filter AST, the properties system, and AI Signal/Noise sorting were also declined as poor fits.

## Scope multiplier

Every design-touching item lands in up to three places: the desktop view, its `*Mobile.tsx` twin (7 such pairs exist), and the React Native app in `apps/mobile/`. This is the main reason the code-only foundation goes first — it is written once and shared.

## Phase 1 — foundation, code only, unblocked

Nothing here needs design input; all four can proceed in parallel.

- [ ] #326 — Unify read/done state into one per-user model **(prerequisite for the merged feed)**
- [ ] #327 — Shared date bucketing util **(feeds the merged feed's grouping)**
- [ ] #328 — Frecency ranking in Global Search
- [ ] #329 — Audit and derive Contact activity fields

## Phase 2 — design assets

Merged attention feed · shared row action menu · contact pill + hover preview · merged thread tab · role-aware first-run checklist · four "Make a to-do" affordances.

## Phase 3 — build against the designs

- [ ] #330 — Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
- [ ] #331 — Notification stacking by target
- [ ] #332 — Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
- [ ] #333 — One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab ⚠️ **has a privacy decision to make first**
- [ ] #334 — Live contact pill with hover preview
- [ ] #335 — Role-aware first-run checklist
- [ ] #336 — Four to-do creation entry points
- [ ] #337 — Expand the ⌘K palette + central shortcut registry

## Testing

Per `CLAUDE.md` §6 all of this is logic/data/permissions code, so TDD is mandatory — failing test first. Coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts` ratchet up only.

title: fix(mobile): QA Google sign-in + welcome form link cleanup
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
Two mobile QA fixes:

### 1. QA Android Google Sign-In `developer_error` (root cause + console fix)
EAS Android builds are signed with the EAS-managed keystore (SHA-1 `4787e74fa43b0c8ea2502545d348a29fd8f95fc4`, SHA-256 `c77456bc…`, created 2026-08-14), but Firebase/Google OAuth for `com.cisa.campus` only had the local debug keystore (`078c…`) and an older key (`5e8f…`) registered. Android Google Sign-In matches the app's signing certificate by package + SHA-1, so QA/release builds failed with the native SDK's `developer_error` while debug builds worked.

**Fix (applied via Firebase Management API, no code change needed):** registered the EAS keystore's SHA-1 and SHA-256 on the Firebase Android app — same path used previously for the debug keystore. Verified present via `GET .../sha`. iOS QA is unaffected (client ID, bundle ID, and reversed-client URL scheme all match).

> Note: if Play App Signing is enabled in Play Console, Play re-signs installed APKs with its own app-signing key — that key's SHA-1/SHA-256 may also need registering (values are in Play Console → Setup → App signing). The registered fingerprints cover sideloaded/upload-key-signed installs.

### 2. Welcome form link removed from mobile sign-in screen
The "New here? Fill out our welcome form" link is outward-facing, not an in-app sign-up, so it was removed from `apps/mobile/app/login.tsx` (with the now-unused `Pressable` import). The `/signup` route stays reachable via shared links for phone-based intake.

title: fix(mobile): register push token on the real auth uid, not the impersonated persona
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem

Firestore error when signing in with an account that has a persisted "owner view" role (or while impersonating):

```
ERROR  Firestore Error: {"error":"Missing or insufficient permissions.","operationType":"update","path":"users/cisa-student", ...}
```

`usePushRegistration` wrote the Expo push token to `useAuth().uid` — the **effective** userId (`AuthProvider.tsx:124-132`). With an owner-view role of `operator`, that resolves to `cisa-student`, so the token was written to `users/cisa-student`. `firestore.rules:82-92` denies it: the doc isn't the authenticated user's own (`isOwner` compares against the real auth uid), and the account isn't a manager.

## Fix

`usePushRegistration` now targets the real Firebase `user.uid`, so the device token lands on the actual signed-in account's doc. A push token is a device-level registration — it belongs to the real account, never a persona.

## Tests

- Added `apps/mobile/src/lib/usePushRegistration.test.ts` (4 cases, written Red → Green): registers on the real uid while `uid` reports an impersonated persona, registers on the real uid with no override, skips when signed out, skips when no token is minted.
- All 119 mobile tests pass, mobile + root typecheck clean, root lint 0 errors, root coverage above thresholds (lines 89.04 / branches 76.4 / functions 83.2 / statements 87.02), root build passes.

title: fix: end the "See it as they do" stale-content flash on mobile and desktop
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Two remaining paths let switching to/from **"See it as they do"** flash the previous user's content (admin's message groups when switching to a student; the trainee/student home when switching back).

### Mobile
The render-phase identity reset (#305) left two gaps:

1. `ImpersonateLayer.goHome()` deferred the role-home navigation by only `setTimeout(0)` — on a device that can run **before the identity-change frame (the skeleton) is presented**, so the back/pop transition animates the previously drawn frame. It now waits for `InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions` plus a frame callback, so the transition reveals the skeleton, not the last user's frame (and waits out the picker sheet's dismiss animation).
2. Cached Firestore snapshots resolve a reload within a frame or two, so even the skeleton flickered. All 12 identity-keyed hooks now run their `loading` through a shared `useMinLoading` hold (`MIN_SKELETON_MS` = 500ms), with the clock restarting when an identity switch happens mid-hold.

### Desktop
Views clear/refresh identity-keyed state in effects (after paint), so switching impersonation left the previous viewer's content on screen for at least a frame (and on `/messages`, until the new snapshot landed). `DashboardLayout` now **keys the routed view by `effectiveIdentityKey`**, so the view remounts in the same commit as the identity change — the first frame is already the new viewer's loading skeleton — and an open person detail (which reads the previous viewer's scope) is dropped on identity change, matching the existing #257 navigation behavior. One fix covers every view uniformly, so no per-view reset churn.

## Tests

- New `useMinLoading.test.ts` (min hold, early-data, mid-hold restart), `useChatThreadData`/`useMessagesData` tests updated for fake timers.
- New `App.test.tsx` cases: routed view remounts on identity change (and again switching back); open person detail closes on identity change.
- Mobile: jest 25/25 suites (115 tests), typecheck, eslint clean. Web: vitest 117 files/1443 tests, coverage thresholds met, typecheck, lint (0 errors), build.

## Notes

- Mobile QA: switch to a student → no admin groups flash; back to me → no trainee/student home flash; skeletons hold ≥500ms.
- Desktop: on `/messages`, pick a target from the eye icon → instant skeleton, no stale rooms.

title: feat(mobile): skeleton loaders for every v2 screen + impersonation flash fix
label: CLOSED
body:
## What & why

Every major v2 screen replaced its bare `ActivityIndicator` with a skeleton loader shaped like the content that's loading — and fixed the bug that motivated it: on "See it as they do" (impersonation), switching identities flashed the previous viewer's content before it vanished.

## Root cause of the flash

The tab navigator stays mounted across impersonation switches, and every identity-keyed data hook kept rendering the previous viewer's state until the new subscription's first snapshot landed. The first frame after a switch showed stale content, then it was replaced.

**Fix:** a shared `useIdentityReset(identity, reset)` helper (render-phase state adjustment, keyed on `uid` / `roomId`) applied to all 13 identity-keyed hooks — `useChatThreadData`, `useMessagesData`, `useFtHomeData`, `useMemberHomeData`, `useTraineeLandingData`, `usePeopleData`, `useJourneyData`, `useAttendanceData`, `useContactDetailData`, `useBoardListData`, `useBoardDocData`, `useMemberPrayerData`. On identity change the hooks drop their data and set `loading` back to true synchronously, so the first frame is already the skeleton — no stale flash.

## Skeletons added

- `Skeleton` — reusable pulsing block (reanimated), colour/shape from the caller's layer
- `SkeletonList` — card rows (People, Journey, Gatherings, prayer log, Board, outreach, contact sections)
- `SkeletonSection` — label + widget-card rows (member/FT home sections)
- `QueueSkeleton` — trainee Today: chrome meta + focus card
- `MemberHomeSkeleton` — member Today/Prayer/Messages via the shared `MemberScreen` shell
- `FtHomeSkeleton` — full-timer Today: greeting + quick tiles + sections
- `ContactSkeleton` — person screen hero + rows
- `DocSkeleton` — Board page body
- `ThreadSkeleton` / `MessagesListSkeleton` — messages (previous PR scope, now on the shared helper)

## Tests

14 new tests: skeleton components, `useIdentityReset`, the hook reset behavior, and loading-branch tests for `FtHomeScreen`, `QueueScreen`, `MemberScreen`, `ChatThreadScreen`.

- `apps/mobile`: 24 suites / 112 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean
- root: `eslint .` 0 errors, `npm run build` passes

One trap worth noting for future tests: `jest.mock('mod', () => () => null)` returns the function *as the module*, so a named import from it is `undefined` → "Element type is invalid". Must be `() => ({ LogSheet: () => null })`.

Chat reactions / pins / take-back-for-everyone are silently denied in `prod` and `qa-db`.

The `chatRooms/{roomId}/messages` `allow update` rule reads `resource.data.deleted` with dot-access. In Firestore rules v2, dot-access on a missing map key throws an evaluation error (`Property deleted is undefined on object.`) instead of returning null — and `deleted` is only present on a message **after** it has been tombstoned. So the rule crashed to `false` for every normal message, denying all three field-level acts.

The same crash has kept `deploy-firestore-rules.yml`'s emulator gate red since 2026-08-11 (MSG1/MSG3 fail), so no rules change has deployed via CI since 2026-08-09 — the Aug 14 rules were pushed by hand.

## Fix

`firestore.rules:675-681` — replace `resource.data.deleted` / `request.resource.data.deleted` dot-access with the `resource.data.get('deleted', null)` / `request.resource.data.get('deleted', null)` accessor (null-safe default), matching the `existing().get('type', 'group')` pattern already used for rooms.

## Verification

- Emulator-backed rules suite: MSG1/MSG3 red → green, **102/102 pass** (`firebase emulators:exec --only firestore --project demo-campus-hub "npx vitest run src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts"`).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Merging to `main` triggers `deploy-firestore-rules.yml`, which will finally deploy rules to `prod` and `qa-db` via CI again.
- The reviewer's chatRooms denial is a **stale app build** (pre-#290): that build lists all rooms unfiltered for admins, which the member-only read rule denies. A fresh build from current source fixes it — no code change needed.

title: fix(mobile): scope chat room list to membership for all roles
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem

The App Store reviewer account (`reviewer-appstore@yourdomain.com`, an **admin** / Full-timer) could see another admin's private messages (`yilongwang05@gmail.com`) on the native mobile app — even after clearing storage or signing out and back in.

`#289` fixed this on **web** (`src/views/Messages.tsx`) and tightened `firestore.rules`, but it missed the shared data layer the mobile app uses: `packages/core/src/data/chat.ts`. That module still had the old role branch:

```ts
const roomsQuery = isAdmin
  ? query(collection(db, "chatRooms"), orderBy("createdAt", "desc"))   // admin → every room
  : query(collection(db, "chatRooms"), where("memberIds", "array-contains", uid));
```

So any admin on mobile listed **every** `chatRooms` document. Verified live: the reviewer is a member of **0** chat rooms while the owner has "New message" notification history with several users — the leak was purely that admin see-all query. After `#289` tightened the rules, the unfiltered admin query was also denied outright.

## Fix

`subscribeChatRooms` now always scopes by membership for every role and drops the now-meaningless `isAdmin` parameter:

- `packages/core/src/data/chat.ts` — query is always `where('memberIds', 'array-contains', uid)`
- `apps/mobile/src/lib/data/chat.ts` — wrapper signature updated
- `apps/mobile/src/lib/useMessagesData.ts` — caller updated (dropped `isAdmin`)
- `apps/mobile/src/lib/useMemberHomeData.ts` — caller updated

## Tests

- Added `packages/core/test/chatData.test.ts` — regression tests asserting the room query is `memberIds array-contains` scoped and never `orderBy`-unfiltered.
- Fixed the pre-existing broken `deleteChatMessage` test in `packages/core/test/chat.test.ts` (it called real Firestore with a mock `db`), moving it into `chatData.test.ts` where Firestore is properly mocked.

`packages/core`: 44/44 chat tests pass. `apps/mobile` typecheck passes.

## Notes

- The reviewer account credentials were added to the gitignored `e2e/.test-credentials.json` (not part of this PR).
- Separate data observation (not addressed here): the reviewer's `userPreferences` doc contains `personalContactIds: ["Karen"]` (an owner-created contact), so My Day shows "Karen" as the reviewer's contact. That's server-side data, not a code bug.

title: fix(messages): prevent unauthorized message history access and isolate user sessions
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

Fixes a permission breach where users logging in with a non-admin account (such as a Reviewer / Viewer) could view private message history belonging to a previously logged-in Full-timer / Admin.

### Root Causes & Key Changes

1. **Authentication & Impersonation Isolation (`AuthProvider.tsx`)**:
   - Gated `effectiveUserId` and `effectiveIdentityKey` to only adopt `impersonateTarget` when `isOwner` (`canSimulateRole`) is `true`. For all standard/unauthorized accounts, `effectiveUserId` is strictly guaranteed to be `user.uid`.
   - Updated `logOut()` and `onAuthStateChanged` to purge stale `impersonateTarget`, `ownerViewRole`, and `localStorage` keys (`cisa.impersonate.v1`, `cisa_owner_view_role`) on logout and unauthorized auth changes.

2. **Client Messaging Room Query Restriction (`Messages.tsx`)**:
   - Replaced unrestricted queries (`collection('chatRooms'), orderBy('createdAt')`) with `where('memberIds', 'array-contains', effectiveUid)` across all roles so users only receive conversations they participate in.
   - Added an effect to reset `activeRoomId` if the active room is not in the loaded room membership list.

3. **Firestore Security Rules Hardening (`firestore.rules`)**:
   - Restricted `allow read` on `chatRooms/{roomId}` and `chatRooms/{roomId}/messages/{messageId}` to strictly require room membership (`isRoomMember()` / `memberIds.hasAny([request.auth.uid])`), removing `|| isAdmin()` so non-member admins cannot read private direct chats at the database rule level.

4. **Testing & Validation**:
   - Added unit test suites in `src/test/AuthProvider.test.tsx` and `src/test/Messages.test.tsx`.
   - Added security test cases (`AN8`, `MSG6`) in `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts`.
   - All CI gates passed: typecheck, lint, coverage (1,345 unit tests passed), and production build.

title: fix(visits): conform the page to the design project's views/visits.jsx
label: CLOSED
body: Conforms `/visits` to the design project's `views/visits.jsx`. The original port (see the Visits entry in `CHANGELOG.md`) was already faithful in structure, copy, grouping and the figures footer, so this closes the remaining gaps — all of them places where the app showed **less** than the design does. ## What changed **1. The prayer reads back in its own words.** The design resolves `visit.prayerId` and shows the prayer's text both in the collapsed card's mark tooltip (`Prayer: …`) and in the expanded outcome row. The app only ever said "A prayer came out of this visit." The text is now denormalised onto the visit as `prayerBurden` — the same reasoning already carried by `contactNames`/`wentNames`, and it's already in hand in `LogVisitModal`, so the card costs no extra read. The alternative (a fourth `onSnapshot` on the `prayers` collection) would read the whole collection to render a label on a few cards. Visits logged before this change keep the generic line rather than rendering an empty row. **2. Photo thumbnails in the log/edit modal.** Was a row of filename pills — you couldn't see what you'd attached. Now thumbnails with a corner remove button, as the design has. Existing photos render from their download URL, newly picked files from an object URL that is **revoked** when the set changes or the modal closes. The design never revokes; this version does. **3. Missing-photo fallback.** A photo whose Storage blob has gone rendered as a broken ``. The design guards this, and the card now shows a placeholder tile carrying the filename. **4. Nudge rows match the design's `.reach`.** From a flat wrapping flex row with no affordance to the design's `1fr auto` grid at 14px radius, `18px 20px` padding, card shadow, and the border/lift on hover. ## Notes for review - **`firestore.rules`** gains a `prayerBurden` clause in `isValidVisit`. `isValidVisit` uses `hasAll`, not a field allowlist, so the field was *already* permitted — this is validation (≤500 chars) for consistency with the neighbouring fields, not a permission change. It will trigger the rules-deploy workflow on merge. - **Deliberately not touched**, because they're house convention rather than drift: the `text-[11px] uppercase` eyebrow (shared with `History.tsx`, `PrayerList.tsx`), `PageContainer variant="wide"`, the empty-state icon, and the mobile nudge/footer stacking that the original port recorded as an intentional improvement over the design's own CSS. - **Still open:** card-level pixel fidelity (`.vst-card`, `.vst-face`, `.vst-mark`, `.vst-date`). The design project's `styles.css` exceeds the design MCP's 256 KiB read cap and the `.vst-*` block sits in the truncated tail, so it could not be read. `VisitCard`'s existing Tailwind already mirrors the design's structure; exact values would need a second pass. ## Testing TDD — 7 assertions written red first, then made green. - `visitWrites.test.ts` — `addVisit` persists (and trims) `prayerBurden`; the default is `null`. - `Visits.test.tsx` — the expanded card reads the prayer's own words; falls back to the generic line without them; a photo with no url renders the placeholder, not an ``. - `LogVisitModal.test.tsx` — the burden is stored alongside `prayerId`; a picked file renders as a thumbnail; a photo already on the visit renders from its URL and disappears when removed. - `src/test/setup.ts` stubs `URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL`, which jsdom does not implement. Full gate green: `typecheck` clean, `lint` 0 errors (382 pre-existing warnings, none new), **1293 tests passed**, `build` succeeds. `/visits` is behind a login wall, so this was not eyeballed in a browser — worth a look at the nudge-row hover and the modal thumbnails on the Cloudflare preview. What was verified instead is the thing tests can't catch: that Tailwind actually emits CSS for the arbitrary-value utilities. It does — `.sm\:grid-cols-\[1fr_auto\]{grid-template-columns:1fr auto}`, `border-radius:14px`, `padding-block:18px`, `gap:18px`, and the three-property transition, matching the design's `.reach` verbatim. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(board): restore the missing bdoc-fs-hold class so full screen works
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Full screen on `/coordination` ("The Board") was **completely inert**. One missing class.

[#260](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/260) added the full-screen CSS block to `src/index.css`, every rule keyed on `.bdoc-fs-hold.is-fs`. But the hold element rendered as:

```jsx
className={cn('flex min-w-0 min-h-0 bg-surface', isFullscreen && 'is-fs')}
```

`bdoc-fs-hold` was **never applied** — it existed only in `index.css` and in two code comments — and there is no bare `.is-fs` rule anywhere. Clicking "Full screen" toggled a class that matched nothing: the page never pinned, the gutters and type never changed, the scroll lock was inert. The only visible effect was the button relabelling to "Back to Board".

## Why it shipped

The tests asserted `is-fs` — the class that *was* applied — rather than `bdoc-fs-hold`, the class the CSS actually keys on. So they passed against a dead feature.

## Changes

- **`src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`** — apply `bdoc-fs-hold`. Dropped the duplicated `flex min-w-0 min-h-0`, which `.bdoc-fs-hold` already supplies; keeping both is what invited the drift.
- **`src/index.css`** — `body.bdoc-fs-on { overflow: hidden }` was a no-op: the design project scrolls on `body`, this app scrolls inside the shell's `<main>`. One rule so the lock reaches it.
- **`src/test/CoordinationNotes.test.tsx`** — assert `bdoc-fs-hold` on the hold.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — `[Unreleased]`.

The one-line class fix reinstates the whole block: fixed `inset: 0` at z-220, `bdocFsIn` scale-in, sticky 16/40px head, 40px serif title, 56px (88px ≥1500px) gutters, 17px/1.75 body with h1/h2/h3 bumps — plus `flex: 1` on `.bdoc-fs-doc`, which was missing in **normal** mode too.

## Verification

TDD: the assertion was written first and confirmed red — `Received: flex min-w-0 min-h-0 bg-surface` — then green.

The local app needs a password to sign in, so rather than skip it I verified the CSS contract directly against the app's real compiled stylesheet, which is exactly what was broken. Adding `is-fs` to the fixed className produces every design value:

| | before `is-fs` | after |
|---|---|---|
| hold | `static` / `z-auto` | `fixed` / `inset 0` / **z-220** |
| head | `16px 32px 0`, static | `16px 40px`, **sticky** |
| title | 30px | **40px**, 56px gutter |
| canvas | pad 0, 15px | **`30px 56px 100px`**, 17px / 29.75px (17×1.75) |
| h1 | 27px | **34px** |

Negative control on the pre-fix className with `is-fs` applied: `static` / `z-auto` / title 30px — inert, confirming the diagnosis. Scroll lock: `main` goes `auto` → `hidden` under `body.bdoc-fs-on`.

Full gate green: `typecheck` clean, `lint` 0 errors (382 pre-existing warnings), **1287 tests passed**, `build` OK.

## Reviewer notes

Two things left deliberately unchanged:

- **z-220 sits above this app's overlay tier.** The value is faithful to the design project, whose own top tier is 200 — but this app's is `ContactDetailsModal` 100, flash toast 130, `Toaster` 200, `UndoSnackbar` 250. So clicking a contact chip *inside* a full-screen doc (`CoordinationNotes.tsx:2587`) opens the contact page behind the overlay and appears to do nothing until you leave full screen. Keeping 220 was an explicit call; dropping it to ~90 would sit above all app chrome (max is the sidebar at z-70) and below the overlay tier, if we want to revisit.
- The Escape guard queries `.bdoc-mmenu` (`CoordinationNotes.tsx:701`), a design-project class this app never renders — vestigial but harmless, so left alone under surgical-changes.

Manual pass still worth doing on the preview: confirm `Esc` / "Back to Board" restore the split view **with the caret and unsaved keystrokes intact** (the editor must not remount — `key` is the doc id only, and only a className flips).

## What changed

- **`Messages.tsx`** rewritten to the design's Field Notes inbox:
  - Left rail: "Messages" + New button, `Search messages…`, filter pills All / Unread / Groups / Announcements, conversation rows (cluster icons for groups/announcements or DM avatars, unread dots, relative timestamps).
  - Thread: serif head with pin / search / details actions, a **pinned strip**, bubbles (sender chips in groups, @-mention highlighting, attachment cards), hover tools for **quick-react + pin + a ⋯ menu**, composer with `Write a message…` hint and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to send, and a readonly bar explaining announcement rooms to non-Full-timers.
  - `CreateChatModal` became the design's **NewMessageModal** with Message / Announcement tabs.

- **Schema + rules (reactions / pins / tombstones):**
  - `ChatMessage` gained `reactions: ChatReaction[]`, `pinned: boolean`, `deleted: { by, at }` in both `src/types.ts` and `packages/core/src/types.ts`.
  - `firestore.rules`: messages were immutable (`allow update: if false`). They stay field-level immutable, but updates are now allowed when `diff().affectedKeys().hasOnly(['reactions','pinned','deleted'])` — anyone in the room can react or pin; a tombstone can only be left by the author or a Full-timer, once set it stays, and a gone message can't be reacted to or pinned. Delete stays denied.
  - `src/services/chat.ts`: `reactToMessage` (toggle own reaction), `togglePinMessage`, `removeMessageForEveryone` (tombstone + clears reactions/pin).

- **Hide from my view** — client-only per the design: new `src/lib/messageHides.ts` (per-uid localStorage `cisa.msg.hidden.<uid>`, pub/sub) and a hidden-note with "Bring it back" above the thread.

- **CSS** — `src/index.css` maps the design's Field Notes tokens onto the app's own tokens under `.page.msgs` and adds the scoped `.msgs-*`/`.msgb-*` rules (previously dead CSS referencing undefined tokens); nothing outside the messages page changes.

title: fix(contacts): unblock logging an interaction, denied by the security rules
label: CLOSED
body:
## What's wrong

`LogInteractionModal`'s `writeBatch` is **rejected by the live Firestore rules**. A batch is atomic, so nothing in it lands: no interaction, no contact stamp, no follow-up tasks. Logging an interaction is broken end-to-end.

There are **two independent** rule violations in the one batch — fixing either alone leaves the feature broken.

### 1. The contact update is ghost-field-rejected

The batch stamps `lastContactedBy` / `lastContactedById` / `lastContactedDate` alongside `lastSeen`, but none of the three were in the contacts `allow update` `affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])` allow-list.

Two things worth flagging beyond the original report:

- **It denied every role, not just non-super-admins.** That `hasOnly(...)` conjunct is unconditional — there is no `isSuperAdmin()` escape on the `allow update`.
- **There is a second affected writer.** `ContactDetailsModal.handleAddInteraction` stamps the same trio and was hitting the same denial.

### 2. The interaction document uses a shape no rule (and no reader) accepts

It wrote `date` / `createdById` / `createdByName`, where `isValidInteraction` requires `hasAll(['userId','userName','content','dateTime','createdAt'])` plus `userId == request.auth.uid`.

Independently of the rules, `Interaction` in `src/types.ts` declares `dateTime` as **required** and has **no `date` field at all** — so these docs would have rendered without a date even if they had saved.

## What changed

- **`firestore.rules`** — added the three keys to the contacts allow-list. They are client-stamped display/audit fields, exactly like the `updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`updatedByName` trio already there. Comment updated to name both writers.
- **`src/components/modals/LogInteractionModal.tsx`** — the interaction now writes the canonical `userId` / `userName` / `dateTime` shape already used by `ContactDetailsModal`.
- **`src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts`** — the two reproducing cases.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — `[Unreleased] → Fixed`.

## Why this way

Dropping the trio from the writes was the alternative. It was rejected because `lastContactedBy` is *rendered* in three places in `ContactDetailsModal` (lines 1058, 1111, 1688), so that path meant deleting a live feature from two writers and orphaning three fields on the `Contact` type.

For the interaction shape, loosening `isValidInteraction` to also accept `date`/`createdById`/`createdByName` would have admitted a second schema into one collection, and readers keying off `dateTime` would still have shown no date. Conforming the modal keeps one schema and needs no rule weakened.

## Verification

TDD, emulator-backed. Both tests fail on the parent commit with real denials:

```
contact update    → PERMISSION_DENIED ... evaluation error at L152:24
interaction create → PERMISSION_DENIED ... evaluation error at L173:26
```

Both pass after the fix. Full gate green on the rebased tree:

- **91/91** rules tests (Firestore emulator)
- **1240** tests pass, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, build ok

## Reviewer notes

- ⚠️ **The rules change must be deployed to take effect** — the fix is inert in production until `firestore.rules` ships.
- **Possible stale data.** Any interaction docs this modal wrote before the rules tightened carry `date`/`createdById`/`createdByName` and will read as dateless. Not touched here; worth a look if the modal was ever succeeding.
- **Visits page deliberately untouched** — it already writes only the allowed subset (`lastSeen` + the `updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`updatedByName` trio).
- Running the rules tests locally needs **JDK 21** (`firebase-tools` v15 rejects older):

  ```
  JAVA_HOME="$(brew --prefix openjdk@21)" PATH="$(brew --prefix openjdk@21)/bin:$PATH" \
    firebase emulators:exec --only firestore --project demo-campus-hub \
    "npx vitest run src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts"
  ```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(mobile): "Later" on the only card now says so, plus the queue's first component test
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

Two halves of the same work session:

1. **Fix** — pressing **Later** on the trainee's only remaining card (1 of 1) did nothing visible. The plumbing was live — the card *was* deferred, stamped in AsyncStorage, the queue rebuilt. But `buildQueue` sorts deferred cards to the back of the queue, and with one card the back *is* the front, so the exact same card came back at index 0: no toast, no animation, counter stuck at "1 of 1". `QueueScreen` now shows a **"Moved to later."** toast when the deferred card is the only one in the queue. With 2+ cards the advance is the feedback and the ghost affordance stays quiet (matches the design's intent; mirrors the existing `pushToTomorrow` toast pattern).

2. **Component test harness + regression test** — the mobile app had no test runner at all. This PR stands up the Expo-recommended stack (jest-expo ~54, @testing-library/react-native 13, jest 29) and adds the first screen test, which locks down the fix: render the real `QueueScreen` with the Firestore data hook stubbed, press "Later" on a 1-card queue, assert the toast appears — and assert no toast when Later actually advances. Verified the test goes red without the fix.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/mobile/src/components/queue/QueueScreen.tsx` | "Moved to later." toast when deferring the only card |
| `apps/mobile/jest.config.js` | jest-expo preset; `@cisa/core` → source mapping; transform allowlist extended (firebase, `@firebase/*`, date-fns, `@gorhom`) + `.mjs` transform |
| `apps/mobile/jest.setup.ts` | device-boundary mocks: gesture-handler, reanimated v4 + worklets, safe-area, async-storage, bottom-sheet; vector-icons + expo-router stubbed |
| `apps/mobile/src/components/queue/QueueScreen.test.tsx` | first screen test (2 cases) |
| `apps/mobile/package.json` / `package-lock.json` | `test` script + devDeps |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | new `mobile-test` job (apps/mobile: `npm ci`, typecheck, jest) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Fixed + Added entries |

## Verification

- `npm test` (apps/mobile): 2/2 pass, deterministic across repeated runs
- Regression capability: temporarily disabled the toast line → test fails with `Unable to find an element with text: Moved to later.`; restored → green
- `npm run typecheck` (mobile) and root typecheck: clean
- `npm run lint` (root): 0 errors (only pre-existing warnings)
- Root pipeline unaffected: no root `src` changes; root vitest excludes `apps/**`

## Notes / decisions

- **CI addition**: the repo previously had zero CI coverage of the mobile app, which would make this regression test decorative. The `mobile-test` job is new in this PR — it mirrors the root job (`npm ci`, typecheck, jest) against `apps/mobile`'s own lockfile. Drop it if you'd rather not expand CI scope.
- **Harness design**: device-boundary mocks (native modules, animations, icons, router) live once in `jest.setup.ts`; per-screen data mocks (Firestore hook, auth, firebase writes) live in each test file. Other screens should render under the same harness with just their own data mocks — the queue test is the proof-of-pattern.
- **Stack choice**: `@testing-library/react-native@13` over v14 deliberately — v13 consumes `react-test-renderer@19.1.0`, which jest-expo 54 already pins; v14's new `test-renderer` peer is not yet aligned with the preset.

title: feat(outreach): monthly park outings page — web + mobile
label: CLOSED
body:
Ports the design project's Outreach page (`views/outreach.jsx` + the outreach section of `data.jsx` in the design repo) into the real app as a Firebase-backed feature, on web **and** mobile.

## What it is

Once a month a team goes to a park, hands out Bibles, tracts and booklets, and talks to whoever stops. Logged after the fact — but the record exists for the **names**: anyone who leaves a number becomes a real contact that same moment and sits in "people we met, not yet reached" until someone rings them, usually the next day.

## Access (permission matrix)

| Page | Full-timer (admin) | Community (viewer) | Trainee (manager) | Student (operator) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Outreach** | see · log · take · nudge · edit/remove | **see · log** | — | — |
| **Visits** (not built yet) | full access | — | — | — |

- Outreach is a deliberately **non-ladder** access: `canAccessRoute` special-cases `/outreach` so viewer + admin get it but operator/manager don't.
- Community logs names; because task creation stays operator+ in the rules, a community logger's names become contacts *without* the auto "Ring {first}" to-do — the pending queue still shows them for a full-timer to take.
- Take / Remind / Edit / Remove are admin-only (they write tasks/threads or update the record).
- Visits, when built, will be full-timer-only (`canSeeVisits`/`canLogVisits` are already defined).

## What changed

**Shared core (`@cisa/core`)**
- `outreach.ts` — record/name types, derived `reached`/`pending` (any touch on the contact after the outing date clears the queue), month grouping, stats, UTC date helpers.
- `data/outreach.ts` — `subscribeOutreach`, `addOutreach` (each filled name → real contact via `addContact` + follow-up to-do via `addTodo`), `updateOutreach` (never touches names), `removeOutreach`, `takeOutreachName`.
- `permissions.ts` — `canSeeOutreach`/`canLogOutreach` (admin|viewer), `canSeeVisits`/`canLogVisits` (admin), `/outreach` route + nav entries.
- `firestore.rules` — new `outreach` collection: list/get/create for admin|viewer, update/delete admin-only.

**Web app (`src`)**
- `views/Outreach.tsx` — header + summary, pending queue, expandable This month / Earlier months cards, figures row, Log/Edit modal (when/where/who went/handed/how/name rows).
- Route + sidebar item (`RoleGuard` + `minRole`), admin+viewer only.

**Mobile app (`apps/mobile`)**
- `FT_MORE` entry + `/outreach` route (`canSeeOutreach` guard).
- `OutreachScreen.tsx` in the v2 language (Sheet-based log/edit, take + nudge), wearing the opener's room (navy for full-timers, green for community).
- Community reaches it from the member app's "You" tab.
- `data/outreach.ts` wrapper + `useOutreachData` hook.

## Notes

- Photos are **count-only** in v1 (the design itself strips photo URLs on persist, keeping the count).
- Editing an outreach never touches its names (they're the record's whole point).
- Outreach date math parses dates as UTC — the app stores dates as UTC calendar dates (`toISOString().slice(0,10)`), and parsing them as local time shifted the "reached" boundary a day near midnight.

## Testing

- Core: `outreach.test.ts` (13 tests) + shell/permissions updates → **546 passing**.
- Web: `Outreach.test.tsx` (4 tests) + permissions matrix → **1158 passing**.
- Typechecks: web 0 errors, mobile 0 errors (core has 10 pre-existing test-file errors in `ftHome.test.ts`/`queue.test.ts`, untouched).

title: feat(visits): port the design project's Visits page (#200)
label: CLOSED
body:
Ports the design project's `views/visits.jsx` (issue #200) into the app. The repo had **no** counterpart to it — no visits page, route, type, collection, or test anywhere in `src/`, `packages/core/`, or `apps/mobile/`.

## What a visit is

A record of having gone to where someone lives. Logged after the fact, full-timers only, usually a pair, sometimes several people seen at once. From the design's own header comment:

> Source of truth for a visit lives HERE; the person's card shows it as an interaction and links back.

The page opens on the homes we haven't been round to in three weeks or more, longest-neglected first and capped at four — **people never visited are deliberately excluded**, because the nudge is about letting a relationship lapse, not working through a backlog. Below that the record groups into This week / Last week / Earlier on Monday-start weeks, each visit expanding in place to read back. A quiet footer counts visits, people we've sat with, and how many of us have gone out.

## Files

**New**

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/views/Visits.tsx` | Desktop container — Firestore subscriptions, `useMediaQuery` split, header/nudge/groups/figures |
| `src/views/VisitsMobile.tsx` | Phone layout, props only, no Firestore |
| `src/components/visits/VisitCard.tsx` | `VisitCard` + `VisitGroup`, shared by both |
| `src/components/modals/LogVisitModal.tsx` | Log + edit |
| `src/lib/visits.ts` | Week grouping, overdue selection, and the Firestore writes incl. mirroring |
| `src/lib/visitPhotos.ts` | Browser-side downscale + upload |
| `storage.rules`, `.github/workflows/deploy-storage-rules.yml` | The Storage stack |

**Modified** — `src/App.tsx` (route), `src/lib/permissions.ts` (`ROUTE_MIN_ROLE` / `NAV_ITEMS` / `canSeeVisits`), `src/lib/prayers.ts` (new `addPrayerBurden`), `src/lib/firebase.ts` (`storage` export), `src/types.ts`, `firestore.rules`, `firebase.json`, and `humanize()` in both `src/views/History.tsx` and `packages/core/src/history.ts`.

## Decisions a reviewer should know about

**`src/` is self-contained.** I first put the logic in `packages/core`, then found the web app has no `@cisa/core` alias — only `apps/mobile` resolves it (via metro + its own tsconfig path), and no file under `src/` imports core. Rather than add a build alias, I followed the actual convention and put everything in `src/lib/visits.ts` alongside `src/lib/todos.ts` and `src/lib/prayers.ts`.

**Mirrors use a derived id** (`visit_<visitId>`), so edits and removals need no stored refs — the previous `contactIds` on the doc being edited says which copies to drop. Creates and updates take different code paths on purpose: the interactions **create** rule demands `createdAt == request.time`, and the **update** rule permits only `content`/`dateTime`/`type`/`userName`/`userPhoto`, so an edit must not restate `createdAt` or `userId`. `src/test/visitWrites.test.ts` asserts both key sets directly.

**Storage rules carry no role check.** Storage rules can only reach Firestore through `firestore.get()` on the `(default)` database, and this project uses a *named* one (`ai-studio-43298cca-…`). So the full-timer gate lives on the `visits` doc; a photo without a matching visit doc is an orphan blob nobody can find, and the 8 MB + `image/*` caps bound what can be put there. This is written up in `storage.rules` itself.

**"Where" reuses the existing free-form `location`** rather than adding a `hall`/`residence` field to `Contact` — that would have rippled into `isValidContact` and every contact form for no gain here. It's offered when everyone on the visit shares one place, and asked for when they don't.

**Contact writes stay inside the rules allowlist.** Saving a visit touches only `lastSeen` + the `updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`updatedByName` trio, which is exactly what the contacts update rule permits.

**Follow-up goes through `addTodo`**, assigned to whoever went and due in a week — unlike `LogInteractionModal`, which inlines a self-assigned batch write. Both the follow-up and the prayer are created only on the way in; an edit fixes the record, it doesn't ask the team to carry the same thing twice.

**Web only.** The design keeps Visits out of the mobile bottom nav too, so no `apps/mobile` screen was added. Note the design's own CSS never adapted the nudge rows or the figures footer below `.md-page` — the port stacks them properly rather than reproducing that.

## Access

`/visits` is `admin` in `ROUTE_MIN_ROLE` and the `visits` collection is `isAdmin()` for read *and* write. Worth remembering that `RoleGuard` ignores its own `minRole` prop and defers to `canAccessRoute` → `ROUTE_MIN_ROLE`, so the `ROUTE_MIN_ROLE` entry is what actually gates. `src/test/permissions.test.tsx` was updated with `/visits` in the admin row, and `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts` gained five emulator cases (VS1–VS5) covering the full-timer path, the trainee-and-below denial, empty `contactIds`, an oversized write-up, and a multi-person visit.

## Verification

Full gate green on top of `2efc156`:

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors, and no warnings from any new file
- `npm run test:coverage` — **1224 passed**; 85.02 statements / 74.59 branches / 80.27 functions / 86.90 lines, all above the ratcheted thresholds
- `npm run build` — clean
- `packages/core` — 532 passed

All six new modules were also confirmed to compile through the real Vite pipeline, and both layouts were screenshotted from the running dev server.

**Not verified by me:** the authed end-to-end path (log a visit → confirm it appears on the person's card, the follow-up task, the prayer, and removal) — that needs a Full-timer login, which I don't do. Worth walking on the Cloudflare preview before merge.

## After merge

`gs://sac-campus-hub.firebasestorage.app` already exists and matches the `storageBucket` in `firebase-applet-config.json`, so no config change was needed. The bucket is still on whatever rules it was created with; `deploy-storage-rules.yml` publishes `storage.rules` on this merge, via the same keyless WIF credential the Firestore and RTDB rule deploys use. `firestore.rules` deploys through the existing workflow as usual.

title: fix(mobile): model the v2 palette as the design's three stacked layers
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

`apps/mobile`'s `V2Palette` was one flat object of ~45 colour fields, with `getV2Palette(room, mode, tint)` returning one of six of them. The design project stacks its class list on a **single root element** — the trainee is `m2 deck`, a member `m2 deck mem`, the full-timer `m2 deck mem ft blue` — so three independent token sets land on the same node and disagree. A flat palette can only be right about one at a time.

It's now three layers, and a component reads the layer it *is*:

| layer | source in the design's CSS | varies by |
|---|---|---|
| `c.room` | `.m2.deck`'s bg/ink, `--mb-room`/`--mb-ink*` for the FT's paper; plus `datebox` and `mark`, which sit on the room rather than a card | room × tint × mode |
| `c.card` | `.m2.deck …` — the focus card, the sheets, every pushed `.m2c-*`/`.m2p-*` person screen | **tint × mode only** |
| `c.widget` | `--mb-*` from `.m2.mem` — the furniture the shells that scroll are built from (`.mbr-*`, `.ftw*`, `.ft-tile`, `.ft-gl`, `.ft-chip`) | shell look × tint × mode |

The card layer collapsing to tint × mode is the structural win: all three roots carry `deck`, so it stops being restated per room.

## Why

Two live defects, both of which needed a new room rather than a corrected hex:

1. **Member widgets were white where the design says cream.** `.m2.mem{--mb-card:#f4f1e6}`, but the focus card went white in the design's Jul-26 revision and the member widgets did not — the whole member app was reading the deck's card. Message bubbles also picked up `--mb-mine`/`--mb-minek`, which had no counterpart in the palette at all.
2. **A person screen pushed from the FT shell got the wrong ink.** The FT root carries both `mem` and `deck`, so the widgets take `.m2.mem.ft.blue`'s warm paper ink (`#1b1a18`/`#524d47`/`#8d8880`) while `ContactScreen` keeps `.m2.deck.blue`'s navy (`#17293f`/`#607182`/`#7e8598`). One set of fields couldn't hold both.

## Notes for a reviewer

- **No flat aliases were kept**, so removing a field is a type error at every call site. `tsc` located all **532** of them exhaustively — that's the only safety net this package has (`apps/mobile` has no test runner, and none was added). The bulk of the diff is that mechanical rename.
- **No new `V2Room`.** `mem` adds a *layer* over the trainee's room rather than moving rooms — member and queue resolve to identical room and card layers in all four tint/theme combinations, so a third room would have returned a byte-identical palette. `V2Room` stays `'queue' | 'ft'`, `shellForRole`'s `'member'` folds into `'queue'` on purpose, and `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` now says so by calling `roomForRole` instead of repeating the ternary.
- **Three `--mb-*` tokens that had nowhere to live** came across so no field is dead: `--mb-shadow` (member widgets had a 1px hairline where the design gives a 32px drop), `--mb-warm`/`--mb-deep` (which, unlike the deck's, don't shift at night), and `.ftw.deep` — "Prayers to carry" and the member's "Ask the team to pray" now sit on `--mb-deep` violet with its own `#f2eef8` ink instead of the pale `pray` tone band, so `WidgetRow`/`WidgetEmpty` read their ground from a small tone context.
- **`--mb-prim`/`--mb-onprim` are deliberately not ported.** The design declares them in every `--mb-*` block, but `grep -o "var(--mb-prim"` over `mobile.css` returns zero and `views/mobile/ft.jsx` has no inline use — they're dead declarations.
- **Values corrected in passing**, found independently in #238: the green night ink floor is `--n-ink4` `#8e9a92`, not the navy `#8e97a6`; and `.m2.blue.night` restates neither `.m2-mn`'s chrome tint nor `.m2-b1`'s `#eaf3ec` on-colour. The `sheet`/`grab`/`scrim`/`scrimOpacity` tokens are included in the card layer where they belong, but wiring them into `Sheet.tsx` is left to #238.

### Overlaps with #238

That branch is the immediate predecessor and touches `v2.ts` and `_layout.tsx` too, so whichever lands second will conflict there. I read it rather than rebasing onto it: beyond the palette values it deletes ~5,000 lines (six `app/*.tsx` routes, all of `components/{myday,landing}/`, a dozen `use*Data` hooks). That looks like a coherent removal of the pre-v2 Material screens, but it's a separate decision that shouldn't ride in on a theme refactor.

### Left open (pre-existing, carried verbatim rather than silently changed)

- `card.inverse`/`onInverse` and `room.mark`/`onMark` look inverted in the blue tint — `.m2.deck.blue` restates only the *ink* on `.m2-log`/`.m2-mark`, keeping the cream ground.
- The room-ink mapping keeps `ink2`←`--mb-ink3`, `ink3`←`--mb-ink4` uniformly (#238 chose differently for FT alone, which made FT inconsistent with the green room). `--mb-ink2` still has no slot, which is why `Sech` sits one step light everywhere.
- `apps/mobile/src/components/ft/FtWidget.tsx` is dead — a duplicate of `v2/Widget.tsx` with no importers.

## Testing

Full gate green: `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test:coverage && npm run build` (0 lint errors, 1029 tests passing), plus `apps/mobile`'s own `tsc --noEmit`.

Verified against the design CSS by reading **computed values from the DOM** on the Expo web preview (not screenshots), signed in as student, full-timer and trainee:

| surface | design | measured |
|---|---|---|
| member green light — card / ink / ink3 | `#f4f1e6` `#16332b` `#7d8b7f` | ✅ |
| member widget shadow | `0 14px 32px -18px rgba(0,0,0,.5)` | ✅ `rgba(0,0,0,.28) 0 7px 14px` |
| `.mbr-askbtn` | `--mb-deep` + `#f2eef8` | ✅ `#4a3b63` / `#f2eef8` |
| member blue light — room / card | `#17293f` / `#f4f1e6` | ✅ |
| FT light — room / widget / ink | `#eceae6` / `#ffffff` / `#1b1a18`·`#524d47`·`#8d8880` | ✅ |
| FT light **pushed** ContactScreen | `.m2.deck.blue` navy on white | ✅ `#17293f`·`#7e8598`·`#1f3145` |
| `.ftw.deep` + `.ftw-carry` | `#4a3b63` / `#f2eef8` / `rgba(242,238,248,.28)` | ✅ incl. the `.16` hairline |
| FT night — room / widget / shadow | `--n-room` / `--n-card` / `--n-soft` | ✅ |
| trainee queue night | `--n-room` `--n-card` `--n-prim` `--n-ink4` | ✅ |

That pass earned its keep: moving `Widget tone="deep"` onto `--mb-deep` initially gave the right ground but left the old ink, rendering "Prayers to carry" ink-on-ink with invisible buttons — something `tsc` cannot see.

title: fix(mobile): land impersonation pick/exit on the role home without stale navigation targets
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

Fixes the dev-mode error seen in the mobile app when switching or exiting impersonation:

```
The action 'REPLACE' with payload {"name":"index","params":{}} was not handled by any navigator.
Do you have a route named 'index'?
```

**Root cause (confirmed with live instrumentation of the queued navigation action):** `pick()`/`exit()` in `ImpersonateLayer` changed the impersonation role (`setImpersonateTarget`) and called `router.replace('/')` in the same synchronous tick. The role change re-keys the tab navigator during that render, so the queued REPLACE was built against the *old* navigator key. When the action flushed a moment later, that key no longer existed → React Navigation dropped it as unhandled and the landing navigation silently didn't happen.

Observed in the dispatch logs (web target): at queue time the focused `(tabs)` route had nav key `tab-hvTate2...`; at flush time the same route had `tab-Gl8cxrp...` — the action targeted the old key. Reproduced 3/3 before the fix with: sign in as full-timer → More → "See it as they do" → pick trainee → ☰ → Your app → Switch → pick student → "Back to me".

## Changes

Only `apps/mobile/src/components/impersonate/ImpersonateLayer.tsx`:

- `pick()`/`exit()` now call a `goHome()` helper instead of `router.replace('/')`.
- `goHome()` defers the navigation with `setTimeout(0)` so it runs after the role change commits and targets the current navigator keys, and prefers `router.back()` when there's a stack to pop — `replace('/')` from a pushed root screen (e.g. `/settings`) would stack a **second** `(tabs)` instance on the root stack, leaving the previous role's shell mounted underneath the back button.
- No route/API changes; other `replace('/')` call sites (login, signup, screen back-fallbacks) target the stable root stack and are unaffected.

Also added a `[Unreleased]` → `Fixed` entry to `CHANGELOG.md` per repo convention.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` in `apps/mobile` passes.
- Playwright regression against the web target covering the exact repro flow plus: plain pick from FT More, switch from `/settings` (asserts a single `(tabs)` in the root state — no duplicate), and "Back to me" from both `/` and `/settings`. Result: **0 unhandled REPLACE errors**, lands on the role home, single `(tabs)` throughout.

title: fix(mobile): close five conformance seams against the design project

body:
A fourth pass over `apps/mobile` against the Claude Design project's mobile v2 ([project](https://claude.ai/design/p/019e2501-d939-73e9-8f0f-af68b36b8e64), `mobile.html`), following #234–#237.
