So all five findings are **seams**: places where Field-Notes (Material) code still showed through a v2 shell, or where a v2 file quietly opted out of the design's own rules.

Net **−5,079 lines**.

## What changed

**1. Deleted the unreachable Field-Notes island**
Six routes (`history`, `search`, `notifications`, `answered`, `feedback`, `feedback-admin`), ~30 components (`components/{myday,landing,history,search,notifications,answered,prayer,feedback}`, `people/AddContactSheet`), eight `use*Data` hooks, two orphaned data modules, and the `TeamPrayer` branch of `(tabs)/prayer.tsx`.

Nothing in any v2 shell linked to them — the only inbound edge from outside the island was `login → /signup`. The design's rule is stronger than the note already in `(tabs)/index.tsx`: *"no Field-notes view is mounted inside the mobile app any more."*

Deep-link handlers were checked **before** deleting: `notifications.ts` registers no `addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` and nothing uses `Linking` to route, so push couldn't reach them either.

**2. `ui/Sheet.tsx` got v2 chrome props**
It hard-wired a 16px top radius (`tokens.ts` `radius.lg`), a `colors.outline` grab handle and a `#000`/0.35 scrim underneath all nine v2 sheets. New optional `radius`/`handleColor`/`scrimColor`/`scrimOpacity` — defaults unchanged, so the Field-Notes callers are untouched — supplied by a new `v2SheetChrome()`.

This also fixed a real bug: the v2 sheets passed `backgroundColor={c.card}`, but the focus card went **white** in the design's Jul-26 revision while `.m2-sheet` deliberately stayed cream. `sheet`/`grab`/`scrim` are new palette tokens.

**3. Audited the five non-`lightV2` palettes** against `mobile-night.css` and `mobile-blue.css`
- The green night ink floor was the **navy** one — `#8e97a6` where `.m2.night`'s `--n-ink4` is `#8e9a92` — on `cardInk3`, `roomFaint` and `noteLabel`.
- Bigger: **`lightFt` was the navy-inked blue room, not the design's warm paper room.** `.m2.mem.ft.blue:not(.night)`'s `--mb-*` block is near-black warm ink (`#1b1a18`/`#413c36`/`#6a645c`/`#8d8880`) on `#eceae6` with navy as an *accent* (`--mb-prim:#2b4a6e`), so the full-timer's daylight home had the wrong ink family throughout.
- `darkFt` now derives from `darkBlueQueue` (the design has no `.m2.mem.ft.night` block — it falls through to `.m2.mem.night` over the navy `--n-*`), restating only the three tokens that block re-aims.
- Un-invented two "navy-ised" values the CSS leaves alone (`onPrimary`/`onMark` `#eaf3ec`, `roomChip`).

**4. Tab bar routed through `fs()`** — it was the one v2 surface outside the `--m2-fs` type scale, so its words didn't ease down on a short screen with everything else.

**5. `/signup` got the design's paper backdrop.**

## For the reviewer

**`/signup` is deliberately NOT a v2 screen.** I originally planned to port it — `M2Sub` routes `signup` to `<M2Signup>`, which reads like a v2 component. It isn't: its entire styling in `mobile.css` is two rules that push the **shared** form (`.signup-wrap`, from `styles.css`) full-screen over whichever phone app you were in — *"not an app login, the form you hand to someone new"*. We take only the paper backdrop. There's a changelog note so the next pass doesn't "fix" it.

**No unit test for the palette fix.** `apps/mobile` has no test runner and no test deps at all. The options were new vitest infrastructure, or moving RN-only palette data into the shared `@cisa/core` bundle — both cost more than the bug they'd guard, and `expect(cardInk3).toBe('#8e9a92')` is the hollow kind CLAUDE.md §6 warns against. Verified against live computed DOM values instead (below). Happy to add the runner as a follow-up.

**Two structural gaps found and deliberately left open** (recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`) — both need a new room rather than a corrected hex, so they were out of scope here:
- The member shell renders `c.card` white where `.m2.mem`'s `--mb-card` is cream `#f4f1e6`; students and community members share the trainee's palette, but the design gives them their own `--mb-*` block.
- `V2Palette` conflates the deck's card tokens with the member/FT widget tokens, which is why a person screen pushed from the FT shell inherits paper ink instead of `.m2.deck.blue`'s.

## Verification

Full gate green: `typecheck` ✓ · `lint` 0 errors (369 pre-existing warnings) · **1029** web tests + **530** core tests passed · `build` ✓.

Checked in the running Expo web preview using computed DOM values rather than screenshots alone:
- FT paper room — all seven `--mb-*` values exact: room `#eceae6`, ink `#1b1a18`/`#413c36`/`#6a645c`, card ink floor `#8d8880`, widget `#ffffff`, primary `#2b4a6e`
- Log sheet — handle `#d6cfba` at 40×4 (`.m2-grab`), scrim `#09121f` @ 0.55 (`.m2-sheetwrap` in the navy room), cream surface with 26px corners
- `/signup` renders the shared form on `#eceae6`
- `/history` returns Expo Router's unmatched route
- Metro bundles clean; no new console errors

title: fix(mobile): make "Later" work and stop the impersonation strip covering the queue
label: CLOSED
body:
A third reconciliation pass of `apps/mobile`'s trainee queue against the Claude Design project (`views/mobile/{m2,cards,queue}.jsx`, `views/impersonate.jsx`), closing the two reported defects plus three gaps found alongside them.

## The two reported defects

### 1. "Later" did nothing

`useQueueState` handed back the `handled`/`later` maps that `QueueState` mutated **in place**, and [`useTraineeLandingData.ts:157`](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/blob/claude/mobile-design-fixes-811b44/apps/mobile/src/lib/useTraineeLandingData.ts#L157) memoizes `buildQueue` on those exact identities. They never changed, so the memo never recomputed — the press re-rendered the screen without ever reordering the queue.

Same root cause silently disabled **swipe-to-defer on all five card kinds** and **"I prayed just now"** (the one `handle()` call with no companion Firestore write to invalidate the memo). Every action that *appeared* to work was riding on a second state change.

The day-state reducers now live in `packages/core/src/queueDay.ts` and **replace** the state instead of editing it; `queueState.ts` is storage and pub/sub only. This is the same fix already applied one file over in `apps/mobile/src/lib/data/inboxReads.ts`, which names the bug class in a comment. The design warns about it too — its `M2App` rebuilds the queue every render *"on purpose … so memoising it goes stale immediately."*

### 2. The "Seeing as X" strip covered the content

`ImpersonatePill` (added in #236) floated at `insets.top + 6` with no z-index and no content offset, landing squarely on the queue's own chrome row — the ☰ drawer button and the `Today · N to look after` / `P of N` counter both start at `insets.top + 10`.

It now takes real space at the top, and `ImpersonateLayer` zeroes the top inset for the screens below so their `SafeAreaView edges={['top']}` doesn't double-pad. This matches the design's *other* impersonation strip: the in-flow web `.imp-bar`, which has never had this problem. The design never has to make this call on mobile — its `.imp-pill` renders in the outer preview shell, over the phone *frame*, and the app inside carries no banner at all.

## Three more gaps found while diffing

- **`Open The Board` was ungated on the due card.** `canAccessRoute('manager', '/coordination')` is `false`, so a trainee was being handed a door onto a locked screen. Hidden now (`api.canBoard`, as the design does), along with the "It came from {page}" line; `openBoardDoc` refuses with the design's copy, "That page lives with the team."
- **Stale `logCard`.** `QueueScreen` set it when opening a card's log sheet but never cleared it, so dismissing that sheet and then logging anything via the ＋ FAB marked the **wrong** card handled.
- **Raw keys on screen.** "Look back at your week" printed `small-group` / `meet` / `phone`; new `interactionKindLabel` names them, legacy keys included.

Plus: `Snackbar` restyled onto `theme/v2.ts`. It was the last Material component floating over the v2 room, ignoring the navy tint and the night layer, on all seven screens that use it.

## Two things that are *not* divergences

Worth a reviewer's attention, because the spec prose says otherwise and this cost a planning round:

- **Queue chrome shape.** `MOBILE-V2.md`'s "Chrome — floating (Jul 2026)" section (floating ☰/＋ fabs, one centred counter inside the card) is **stale relative to its own code**. `views/mobile/m2.jsx` renders an in-flow `.m2-top` (☰ + a *two*-label meta) and `.m2-bot` (up-next faces + ＋), commenting *"the meta label and the ☰/＋ fabs live in the air above and below it."* `apps/mobile` already matches. The doc also carries a block headed "Older note (superseded above)" whose claims read as current out of context.
- **Due-card swipe.** The design swipes *every* kind, `due` included, to `later` while the ghost button pushes the due date. We match.

Both are noted in the changelog so the next pass doesn't "fix" them.

## Verification

The `useQueueState` fix was confirmed **both ways** against a running build, with a temporary console probe inside the memo:

- With the fix, pressing Later logs `buildQueue recomputed; later = {"ftmsg:…":…}`.
- With the old mutating write restored, the same press logs **nothing** — the memo never re-ran.

Probe removed before commit. Also verified on screen: the strip is in flow with ☰ and the counter fully visible below it, and the toast now renders in the room palette (cream `inverse` pill, Manrope, dark-green ink) instead of the Material near-black.

Gate, all green:

- `packages/core` — 530 tests (new: `queueDay.test.ts`, `interactionKindLabel` in `quickCapture.test.ts`)
- root — 1029 tests, `typecheck`, `lint` (0 errors), `build`
- `apps/mobile` — `typecheck`

### Reviewer notes

- The identity contract in `queueDay.ts` is load-bearing, not stylistic — the tests assert that each reducer returns a *new* `handled`/`later` object and leaves its input untouched. Anything that reintroduces an in-place write brings the bug straight back.
- `apps/mobile` still has no test runner, so the layout, `logCard` and toast changes are covered by the manual verification above rather than by unit tests. Standing one up is a reasonable follow-up — the absence is why this shipped unnoticed.

title: docs: refine CLAUDE.md for Opus 5
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
- §1 (Think Before Coding → **Think Before Acting**): make routine judgment calls yourself and proceed with the assumption stated inline; ask only when different readings would produce materially different work or the action is irreversible. Cuts unnecessary round-trips vs. the old ask-first bias.
- §5 (Changelog): pre-read is now scoped — targeted `head`/`grep` of `[Unreleased]` and recent entries, only when the change touches an area with recent churn, instead of reading the full (600+ line) file every time. The post-change `[Unreleased]` update stays mandatory.
- §6 (Testing Policy): TDD stays mandatory for logic/data/permissions and all bug fixes; UI-only changes are exempted from hollow snapshot tests; multi-step features should invoke the `tdd` skill so the loop is followed consistently.
- New §7 (Cost Discipline): subagent delegation rules (only for large, genuinely independent/parallelizable work; never to double-check your own output; keep spawn counts low), tool-call batching guidance, and a scoped verification gate (skip checks a doc-only change can't break; run the full gate — mirroring `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — once before pushing).
- Closing "working if" line updated to include fewer redundant tool calls/subagent spawns as a success signal.

## Why
`CLAUDE.md` is loaded into every session, so its instructions are a recurring cost. It predated Opus 5 and actively worked against the model's built-in judgment (ask-first bias, no cost discipline, unscoped changelog reads). Goal was to keep the existing quality bar (TDD, surgical diffs, simplicity — §2–4 untouched) while cutting recurring token cost and unnecessary confirmation round-trips.

## Note for reviewers
`AGENTS.md` is a near-duplicate of `CLAUDE.md` that had already drifted before this PR (it has a "no design mock data" rule and a Pre-PR Gate section `CLAUDE.md` lacked). This PR deliberately does **not** touch `AGENTS.md` — it's now further out of sync. Flagged in the CHANGELOG entry; reconciling the two files was left out of scope by request.

body:
## Summary

Add a **Smart Import** feature that lets users paste unstructured text (roster notes, emails, chat logs, meeting notes) and have Gemini AI parse it into structured **contacts**, **interactions**, and **discussions** — with a full dry-run preview before committing anything to Firestore.

## What's new

### Backend
- **`POST /api/smart-import/parse`** endpoint in `server.ts`
  - Authenticates via Firebase ID token
  - Passes existing contacts to Gemini (`gemini-3.5-flash`) for deduplication/matching
  - Enforces structured JSON output via `responseSchema` for `contacts`, `interactions`, and `discussions`

### Frontend
- **`SmartImportModal.tsx`** — multi-step modal:
  1. **Text Input** — paste area with sample text presets
  2. **AI Parsing** — loading state with Sparkles animation
  3. **Dry Run Preview** — tabbed view (All / Contacts / Interactions / Discussions) with:
     - Per-item checkboxes to include/exclude

title: fix(proxy): strip transport and content-encoding headers to fix Safari EOF error
label: CLOSED
body:
### Summary of Fix

Fixed the Safari `Fetch API cannot load ... unexpected EOF` bug when fetching through the Cloudflare Pages API proxy.

#### Cause
When `functions/api/[[path]].ts` forwarded requests to the GCP Cloud Run backend via Cloudflare Pages Functions, `fetch()` automatically decompressed the backend response stream. However, the proxy copied all backend headers verbatim into `responseHeaders`, retaining stale `content-length`, `content-encoding` (e.g. `gzip`), `transfer-encoding` (e.g. `chunked`), and `connection` headers.

Safari strictly validates HTTP response byte lengths and encodings against response headers. Receiving raw decompressed body bytes alongside compressed `content-length` or `content-encoding` headers caused Safari to terminate the response stream prematurely with an EOF error.

#### Changes Made
1. **Cloudflare Proxy Header Sanitization**: Updated `functions/api/[[path]].ts` to delete transport and content transformation headers (`content-length`, `content-encoding`, `transfer-encoding`, `connection`) before returning the proxied `Response` stream to the browser.
2. **Unit Tests**: Added unit tests in `src/test/cfProxy.test.ts` validating header stripping and preflight handling.
3. **Changelog**: Updated the `[Unreleased]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`.

#### Verification
- Ran vitest unit test suite `src/test/cfProxy.test.ts` (2 tests passing).
- Ran full vitest suite (82 test files, 973 tests passing).

title: fix(coordination): fix raw HTML task list rendering leak when linking to-dos
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue in `/coordination` Board docs where adding or linking a to-do/note from text selection inserted raw HTML `<ul class="contains-task-list" data-type="taskList">...` strings into the TipTap editor.

## Root Cause
The creation callbacks in `CoordinationNotes.tsx` wrapped formatted Markdown lines in `editorMdToHtml(editor, replacement)` before passing them into `editor.chain().insertContent(...)`. Because TipTap's `Markdown` extension is configured with `html: false`, passing HTML strings to `insertContent` caused TipTap's Markdown parser to treat the HTML tags as raw text, leaking `<ul class="contains-task-list" data-type="taskList"><li class="task-list-item"...` directly into the document text.

## Solution
- Passed the clean Markdown strings directly to `insertContent(...)` without `editorMdToHtml` in `handleAssignDirectly`, `TodoComposer.onCreated`, and `NoteComposer.onCreated`.
- Added unit test in `src/test/coordinationTaskSync.test.ts` verifying task Markdown insertion into a TipTap editor.
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`.

title: fix(mobile): Room tint now applies immediately (missing `tint` memo dependency)
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

One-token fix in [`apps/mobile/src/theme/v2.ts`](../blob/claude/elastic-hopper-6630be/apps/mobile/src/theme/v2.ts): the `useMemo` in `useV2Theme` goes from `[mode, room]` to `[mode, room, tint]`.

## Why

`useV2Theme` computes its palette with `getV2Palette(room, mode, tint)` but omitted `tint` from the dependency array — ESLint flagged it as `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. The consequence is a real bug in the room-tint feature from #190 (`RoomTintStore` / `useRoomTint`, picked under **Settings → How it looks → Room tint**): changing the tint updated the context value, but the memo kept returning the previously-computed palette, so the room stayed on its old colour until `mode` or `room` happened to change and invalidate the memo for some other reason.

The bug is pre-existing — it dates from when the tint parameter was threaded through, not from any later change to this hook.

## Verification

Ran the app (`mobile-web`, port 8091) signed in as `cisa-trainee@hub.com` and toggled Room tint, reading the room background back from computed styles at each step:

| | Green | Navy |
|---|---|---|
| **Dark** | `#0b1611` | `#0a1220` |
| **Daylight** | `#16332b` | `#17293f` |

All four match the palettes declared in `v2.ts` exactly (`darkV2` / `darkBlueQueue` / `lightV2` / `lightBlueQueue`), and the cards tracked along with them (`#1b2a23` → `#1a2433` in dark, white in light).

The decisive case is the **light-mode Green↔Navy toggle**, where `mode` and `room` both stay fixed and only `tint` moves — the one combination the stale memo could never invalidate. It now repaints on the click. The change also propagates past Settings: navigating back to the queue showed it in the navy room.

`npx eslint src/theme/v2.ts` and `npx tsc --noEmit` are both clean, and no new console errors appeared (only pre-existing `findDOMNode` deprecation warnings from expo-router).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **No unit test, contrary to CLAUDE.md §6.** `apps/mobile` has no test runner, no test script and no test files, and root `vitest.config.ts:16` explicitly excludes `apps/**`. Covering a hook's memo invalidation would mean standing up a jest-expo + `@testing-library/react-native` harness from scratch, which is well beyond this fix — happy to do that as separate work if wanted.
- **This branch was cut one commit behind `origin/main`.** If the type-scale work that adds `scale` to this same dependency array is on main, the merge needs to end up with **both** `scale` and `tint` in the array.

title: feat(mobile): the log sheet's second beat, the fuller person, and the design's type scale
label: CLOSED
body:
Continues mobile v2 against the Claude Design project (`mobile.html` → `views/mobile/m2.jsx`). Commits #185–#190 ported the role shells, the queue chrome and every drawer screen; re-reading `MOBILE-V2.md` against the repo, the design had moved on three times since the log sheet landed in #189, and those revisions are what's here.

Two commits, so the mechanical pass reviews separately from the feature work.

## 1. The log sheet's "saved" step

Saving no longer just toasts and closes. It lands on the design's quiet second beat: **Come back to {first}** (editable line + Tomorrow / In a few days / Next week), **Something to pray for**, then Done / Log another / Open {first}'s page.

**This closes a regression #189 recorded in its own CHANGELOG entry.** A trainee had *no way to create a follow-up to-do from the phone*, so the queue's own "You said you'd follow up" card could only come from a to-do made on the desktop site. The new to-do carries `contactId`/`contactName` — **not** `source`, which is the Board-doc link and would render an empty doc chip — which is exactly what `buildQueue` reads to raise that card again.

Setting a reminder also schedules the OS notification, so *"your phone will nudge you that morning"* is true rather than a promise the app can't keep. `REMINDER_PRESETS`, `reminderDueDate`, `scheduleTodoDueNotification` and `ensureNotificationPermission` were all recorded in #189 as left on disk unreferenced; they have callers again.

Behavioural wiring the design is explicit about, and worth a reviewer's eye:
- `onSaved` + the queue's card-handling are deferred to `finish()` — on the way **out**, not at save time — with the card id held in a `useRef` so *Log another* can't hand the same card back twice.
- A scrim tap on this step **finishes** (keeps the save, fires the toast) rather than discarding.
- New optional `onOpenContact`, passed by the queue, the full-timer's home and People, and **omitted** by the person screen — you're already there, so the link hides.
- The queue now passes `cardId` and handles the card on save. This is what answers a **gone quiet** card, which has no to-do to complete.

## 2. "Fill in the rest"

*Someone new* still opens with the 20-second three (name · where you met · one note); a disclosure folds out phone · email · year · studying · part of · where they're at · faith so far · first met. Nothing is required. `Part of` and `Faith, so far` render as rows on the person screen.

## 3. The design's type scale

Every font size in the design is `calc(var(--m2-fs) * R)` against `--m2-fs: clamp(11px, 1.6vh, 13px)`. React Native has no `vh` and no `clamp()`, so it's a pure `v2FontScale(windowHeight)` in `@cisa/core`, exposed as `fs()` from `useV2Theme()`, with **421 literal sizes across 51 v2 components** routed through it.

- Line heights scale by the same factor or the rhythm breaks.
- `PersonMark` scales its own mark **once** — its size arrives as a drawn-unit prop, so scaling at the call sites too would double it.
- Material screens are deliberately untouched: the `useV2Theme` call list is exactly the boundary between the two palettes.
- **New v2 styling must use `fs()`** — a plain `px` size will not scale with the rest of the app.

## Substitutions taken (all also in the CHANGELOG)

The design's mock data has fields this schema doesn't:

| Design | Taken as |
|---|---|
| separate **"Lives"** beside "Where you met" | dropped — one dual-purpose `location`, whose own form labels it "FIRST MET / RESIDENCE", so "where you met" keeps it rather than have the two fight over one field |
| **"Bring it to team prayer"** toggle | dropped — `PrayerRecord` has no team flag and `addPrayer` already writes `prayerPage: true`, so every contact prayer is already on the team's page; the done-line says so instead |
| the design's own **year / faith** word lists | the existing `SIGNUP_YEARS` / `SIGNUP_SPIRITUAL_BACKGROUNDS`, so a person added on the phone speaks the same vocabulary as the sign-up form and the web profile rather than opening a second, incompatible one |
| **"Part of"** from a fellowships list | free text into `Contact.role`, which this app's own form already labels "CONTACT GROUP" |
| **"First met"** `<input type="date">` | Today / This week / Earlier presets — no date-picker dependency exists and one optional field is no reason to add a native one; feeds a new optional `createdAt` on `NewContactInput` that genuinely backdates the contact |
| `HeadsUps.add` FYI to another owner | unported — no such store here |

## Verification

- **481 core tests pass** (35 new, covering every new pure helper), **830 root tests pass**. The 4 failing root test *files* are pre-existing and identical on a clean tree: a stale `node_modules` in the dev worktree, not a repo problem — `chrono-node` is declared in `package.json` and Cloudflare's clean install built this branch successfully.
- The widened core contact API (`createdAt` and the fuller fields on `NewContactInput`) is **mobile-only** — the web app has no `addContact` / `NewContactInput` call sites, so nothing in `src/` changes behaviour.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` clean (0 errors).
- **Type scale confirmed live** in the running app: the queue card's name renders **29.83px** at an 812pt window and **25.26px** at 667pt (31 × 11/13.5 exactly), with line-height tracking the identical ratio.

### Not verified interactively — please check on a simulator or device

> **Note:** the Cloudflare Pages preview on this PR builds the *desktop* app (root Vite / `src/`), **not** `apps/mobile` (Expo) — the log sheet below will not be there. Run the mobile app locally (`.claude/launch.json` → `mobile-web`, or `npm run ios` in `apps/mobile`).

The saved step's own taps. Real clicks open the sheet in the browser preview, but the bottom-sheet backdrop swallows clicks *inside* it on web — the pointer-events stall already documented at `apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Sheet.tsx:78`. Synthetic pointer events don't reach RN-web's responder system either. So the saved step's writes (the to-do, the prayer, the card-id ref guard) are covered by unit tests and types, **not** by an end-to-end tap. Worth walking through before merge:

1. ＋ → *A conversation* → pick someone → Save it — the sheet should stay open on the saved step.
2. *Come back to …* → **Remind me** → row collapses; close the sheet and confirm a **"You said you'd follow up"** card is now in the queue for that person.
3. *Something to pray for* → **Start praying** → confirm it on the person's Prayers tab.
4. **Log another** → log a second conversation → confirm the first card wasn't handled twice.
5. People → **＋ New** → *Fill in the rest* → confirm **Part of** / **Faith, so far** rows and a non-zero "Known … days" for a backdated *First met*.

## Noted, not fixed

`useV2Theme`'s memo omits `tint` from its deps, so a room-tint change can render a stale palette. It predates this work, so it's split out rather than folded in.

title: feat(mobile): port the log sheet into the v2 language
label: CLOSED
body:
The last Material surface still mounted **inside** all three v2 shells — and the one screen mobile v2 exists for: *"log fast — a conversation in about twenty seconds."* `MIGRATION.md` has named it as the open item since #188.

I checked the design project against the port first: `M2App`'s current chrome, the Jul-26 revision (white full-height card, the full-timer's paper room, *At a glance*, *The week ahead*), swipe-to-Later and dark mode are all already built. The sheets were the one thing left.

## What changed

`apps/mobile/src/components/log/LogSheet.tsx` is the design's `M2LogSheet` (`views/mobile/m2.jsx`), three modes and no more:

| mode | what it is |
|---|---|
| **palette** | "Log as you go" · two tiles (*Someone new* / *A conversation*) · a *You saw them today* row of one-tap avatar chips · a foot naming the real on-campus window |
| **new** | their name · where you met · one line to remember → **Add {First}** in terracotta |
| **convo** | who, then what it was and what you'll want to remember → **Save it** |

It saves, toasts and closes. Built on the existing v2 kit (`Sheet` with the `backgroundColor` override that exists for this, `V2Input` / `V2TextArea` / `Kicker`, `PrimaryButton` / `SecondaryButton` / `PersonMark`) — the only genuinely new pieces are the two tiles, the chip row and the pickable `.m2-chip`. Tile icons are **drawn as `View`s**, never typed, per the design's own hard-won note that a literal `+` or `…` on a tinted block renders near-invisible.

All four entry points swapped: the queue's ＋ and on-campus strip, the full-timer's *Log a moment*, a person page's **Log**, and People's **＋ New** — which the design points at *Someone new*, so `AddContactSheet` is no longer mounted there (it stays on disk for the unlinked `/search` route, the same call `/coordination/trash` got). `QuickCaptureSheet` is deleted.

`QueueScreen` now carries `card.task?.id` into the sheet, so logging a **You said you'd follow up** completes the to-do behind it — the design's `init.taskId`, which this app was silently dropping.

New pure `logSheetFootLine` / `logSavedLine` / `contactAddedLine` / `newContactFromLog` in `@cisa/core`, reusing `quickCaptureRecents`, `quickCaptureSearchMatches` and `onCampusSummary` rather than restating them, plus `useLogSheetData`, which holds its three Firestore listeners only while the sheet is open — three screens mount it at once.

## What strict fidelity costs

The Material sheet had a fourth "Saved" screen. That shape lives only in the design's **pre-v2** `views/quick-capture.jsx`, which the v2 shell does not mount, so it goes:

- the **follow-up reminder** (a `tasks` doc *and* a scheduled OS notification) — **this leaves a trainee no way to create a follow-up to-do from the phone at all**, so the queue's own `follow` card can now only come from a to-do made elsewhere. The full-timer keeps `FtTodoSheet`'s *Hand something over*.
- the **inline prayer**, **Log another**, **Open {First}'s page**, and the **Today/Yesterday** toggle
- People's **＋ New** stops capturing email, phone, pipeline stage, tags, contact group and spiritual background

All of it still works on the desktop site, which is what the v2 Settings foot already promises. Orphaned and left on disk per CLAUDE.md §3: `REMINDER_PRESETS`, `reminderDueDate`, `reminderNotificationTrigger`, `reminderNotificationContent` (no web callers either — checked `src/`) and `ensureNotificationPermission`. `scheduleReminderNotification` keeps its caller.

**One substitution.** The design tags a new person with where you met; a `Contact` here has a `location` field the app's own new-contact form labels "FIRST MET / RESIDENCE", so that is its home and `tags` stays the active-season tag. Found on the way: the person screen's detail row read **"Lives"**, which mislabelled half of what already lands there — now "First met / lives".

## For the reviewer

- **The reset is done during render, not in an effect** (`LogSheet.tsx`, `wasVisible`) — React's own recipe for adjusting state when a prop changes. Doing it in an effect trips `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, and it resets **only on the way open**, so a closing sheet keeps its words under the dismiss animation.
- **Conversation kinds are the app's own** `QUICK_CAPTURE_KINDS`, not the design's seven — the stored `type` stays a value the desktop site reads back.
- `ContactScreen` and `PeopleScreen` gained a `Snackbar`; neither had one, and without it ＋ New confirms nothing.

## Verification

- `packages/core`: **465 tests green** (was 458).
- Typecheck clean for `apps/mobile`; ESLint clean on every new and changed file.
- Driven live against real Firestore at 375px dark and 360px light:
  - palette renders both tiles and the chip row with **no horizontal overflow at 360** (`scrollWidth === clientWidth`)
  - *A conversation* → picked a person → switched the kind chip → saved: toast `Logged — Aldair.`, and his page shows the note under **TODAY** with "You connected today"
  - *＋ New* → name · where · note: button tracked live to **Add Marisol**, toast `Marisol is in. You can add the rest tonight.`, and she lands in *In your care* with the note as FIRST IMPRESSION and the season tag intact
  - a person page's **Log** opens straight on the conversation, skipping the palette
  - reopening starts clean

title: feat(mobile): port contact detail into the v2 language
label: CLOSED
body:
The design's own `M2Contact` (`MOBILE-V2.md`; `views/mobile/contact.jsx`) — and the last screen in the phone app that still dropped into a Field-notes view mid-flight. Tap someone from People, from a queue card, from a DM's *"Open {First}'s page →"*, and the app left the room it was in.

`app/contact/[contactId].tsx` is now params plus the `canAccessRoute` guard over `components/contact/ContactScreen.tsx`, standing in `roomForRole(role)`.

## What it is

A back row naming who's looking after them, a white hero (avatar · name · year · major · stage dot + "You connected …" · "Last time: …"), **Text / Call / Log**, then segmented **Story · Prayers · Alongside**.

| Tab | What's in it |
|---|---|
| **Story** | The logged conversations, newest first, each expanding into its own thread ("Alongside · N" / "Think this through together"), then one read-only *"Details, notes, how to reach them"* disclosure |
| **Prayers** | *"Pray for {First}"* opens a v2 sheet; open prayers carry "I prayed just now" and "Answered", then a quiet *Looking back* group |
| **Alongside** | Every message on the person — contact-level **and** conversation-level, merged by time — under a compose whose kinds shift by who's writing |

Copy and derivations live in `@cisa/core` with tests (430 → **458**): `contactCareLine`, `contactConnectedLine`, `interactionSnippet`, `lastTimeLine`, `storyRowLine`, `splitContactPrayers`, `prayerCardKicker`, `mergedContactThread`, `composeKindsFor`, and a `v2Label` on `THREAD_KINDS` that sits beside the terser Material one. The v2 kit gained `V2Seg` (the design's `.m2c-seg` — nothing segmented existed) and `V2TextArea`.

## Two bugs found while verifying against real data

- **`PrayerRecord.answeredAt` is display text, not a timestamp.** The web app writes `toLocaleDateString("en-US", {month:"short", day:"numeric"})` — `"Jul 13"` — and prints it straight back (`src/components/landing/PrayerRows.tsx`). Dating a card by it lands in the year 2001; a live prayer rendered **"1307 weeks ago"**. `prayerCardKicker` now only ever *shows* it, and `markPrayerAnswered` writes the same short format rather than the ISO string I'd first coded, which would have surfaced as one on the desktop site. **The format is matched, not fixed** — fixing it is a web-app change.
- **On the trainee's green room the chosen compose chip was the room's own colour**, so it vanished. The design's person screen stands on paper; ours stands in the role's room, so a composer sitting on the room inverts the pair the way `V2Seg` above it does. Same class of fix for `V2Input`, which was invisible on a sheet whose surface is already `card`.

## What this costs — please read before approving

Per the user's call this follows the design strictly for the fourth time, and here it costs the most working capability yet. The design has three tabs; this screen had six plus an admin edit form. **Gone from the phone:**

- **Discussion** — threaded team comments on a contact (`addComment` had no other caller)
- the per-contact **History** timeline
- admin **Edit / Delete contact**
- **editing or deleting a logged conversation** — so the undo-delete window from #160/#161 goes with it
- **tag add/remove**

All of it still works on the desktop site, which is what the design's own Settings foot says of the roster and everything admin. Logging moved to where the design puts it — the hero's **Log** — so `useContactDetailData` dropped the `comments` and `activities` subscriptions and the writes that went with them: two fewer live listeners per open profile. Their thin wrappers are left on disk unreferenced by mobile, as `LandingTrainee` and `components/myday/*` were.

**Four substitutions**, each documented at its call site: no `tags` on a prayer, so the sheet's "Part of life" chips are dropped; no `prayedBy`, so "I prayed just now" is device-local off `useQueueState` + `prayerCardId` exactly as the full-timer's home already is (which also means "{Name} is carrying this too" can't be built); no `owner` on a `Contact`, so "In your care" is `personalContactIdsOf` and the other branch says "{First} added them", matching People's own line; and one `content` field where the design splits `title` from `body`, so the hero quotes the first sentence **as written** rather than lowercasing the names inside it.

**Still Material: the log sheet.** The hero's Log opens `QuickCaptureSheet` with `initialContact`, which is exactly what the design's `M2LogSheet init={{contact}}` does — in Material chrome. Restyling the sheets is the next open item in `MIGRATION.md`, alongside the navy-tint picker.

## Verification

- `packages/core`: **458 tests** green (430 → 458).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in `packages/core` and `apps/mobile`. Core's nine `process` errors in `test/{ftHome,queue}.test.ts` are pre-existing (confirmed by stashing); so is the one `preserve-manual-memoization` warning in `useContactDetailData`.
- **Live on Expo web against real Firestore, all four e2e roles:** trainee → green room, kinds *Note · A question*; full-timer → navy/paper, *Wrote back · Encouragement · Follow-up*, no Edit anywhere; student → every compose surface writable; community → fully read-only across all three tabs. Posted a thread message and toggled a reaction (both round-tripped), "I prayed just now" survived a reload, deep links `?tab=thread` → Alongside and `?tab=prayer` → Prayers both land. Light and dark checked in both rooms; no console errors beyond the bottom-sheet library's pre-existing `findDOMNode` warning.
- **Not clicked live:** `?interactionId=` → Story with that card unfolded. Verified by construction only (a one-line `useState`) — I had no interaction id to hand.

## Note for the reviewer

Verifying against real data left a test message on **Edgar Flores**'s Alongside thread — *"Checking the v2 person screen posts through."* with a 🙏 from the Full-timer account. Neither app has a delete path for thread messages, so removing it needs a Firestore edit.

title: feat(mobile): port The Board, Messages and Settings into the v2 language

body:
The design's own `views/mobile/screens2.jsx` trio — the last three screens the trainee's ☰ drawer and the full-timer's More list reach that still dropped into a Material screen mid-app. After this, only **Contact detail** does.

Continues [#185](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/185) (role shells + FT prayer log) and [#186](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/186) (People · The Journey · Gatherings). Closes the first three of `MIGRATION.md`'s four-screen open item; the remaining one is split out as its own entry.

## What changed

**The Board** — pages grouped as `useBoardListData` already groups them, each row a date block · title · "time · place · *who's leading*" · audience pill, opening onto the page and a foot naming who keeps it. `facilitatorId` has been written on create since Session 3 and rendered nowhere; a new `useFullTimerNames` resolves it (falling back to `createdByName`).

**Messages** — the conversations you're part of, newest first, three lines a row; the thread adds a group sender chip, read-only attachment chips, and "Open {First}'s page →" in a DM.

**Settings** — one screen again, as the design has it. `/queue-settings` folded back in: it only ever existed because the Material `/settings` owned "How it looks" and identity. Queue blocks render only when `shellForRole(role) === 'queue'`, so a full-timer gets the me block, the care line, *How it looks* and the foot.

Five new components, five route files reduced to thin member/staff forks, and 17 Material files deleted.

## Core

Copy and derivation decisions pushed down into `@cisa/core` with tests, **412 → 430**: `boardRowLine`, `boardKeeperFoot`, `boardCountNote`, `AUDIENCE_TONE_KEY`, `chatRowPreview`, `chatKindNote`, `messagesScreenNote`, `settingsCareLine`, `settingsFoot`, `caredForBy`, `onCampusNowLine`, `contactIdForEmail`.

## ⚠️ Strict design fidelity costs working capability here

This was the explicit call, for the third pass running, but these are sharper than the previous passes' losses and reviewers should weigh them:

| Removed | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Board: WebView editor, pin, Trash entry point | Pages are read-only on the phone. The `/coordination/trash` route stays on disk **unlinked**, matching what #185 did for Search, Answered and Looking back. |
| Messages: New conversation, chat details, invite, leave, search | **A trainee can no longer open a conversation** — only reply in one. A full-timer can still start one from a hospitality offer. |
| Settings: team management, roles reference, notifications card | **A new signup can now only be approved from the desktop site.** `firestore.rules:45` locks unapproved users out of everything; the web app's `src/views/Settings.tsx` is the only other approval UI. |

No notification opt-out was lost — the deleted card only offered "Enable" and "Open Settings", `usePushRegistration` is wired independently at `app/_layout.tsx`, and Quick Capture still asks in context.

**Two affordances are blocked, not descoped.** Per-message reactions (🙏❤️🙌) and the "kept" pin need fields `ChatMessage` doesn't carry, and `firestore.rules:601` makes a sent message immutable (`allow update, delete: if false`) — both need a schema change *and* a rules deploy.

**One substitution.** The design reads a `contactId` off the conversation; here a room is user-to-user and a `Contact` has no uid, so the join is the address they signed up with (`contactIdForEmail`, tested), and the contacts listener is only paid for on a direct room.

## Verification

- `cd packages/core && npm test` → **28 files, 430 tests** passing.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in `packages/core` and `apps/mobile` (the 17 deletions were the real check). The repo root has one **pre-existing** error — `chrono-node` isn't installed — confirmed by stashing.
- All three screens driven on Expo web per role: trainee (green room, back row on Messages, all six Settings blocks, "cisa-ft cares for you", "Right now: you're outside the window."), full-timer (navy/paper room, Messages as a tab with no back row, four Settings blocks), student (member forks pixel-unchanged). Rooms checked in all four combinations — green/dark, green/light, navy/dark, paper/light.

## Noted in passing, not touched

- `logOut` in `AuthProvider.tsx:87` has no caller anywhere — the app has had no sign-out UI, before this change too.
- `react-native-webview` is now an unused dependency (its only consumer was the deleted Board editor); left in place rather than churn the native build.
- Web-side `/embed/coordination/:docId` and `/api/mint-custom-token` lost their only mobile caller; both left alone as outside this change.

title: feat(mobile): port People, The Journey and Gatherings into the v2 language
label: CLOSED
body:
The design project (`MOBILE-V2.md`; `views/mobile/screens.jsx`) mounts **no Field-notes view inside the mobile app at all**. #185 put every role behind the right shell, but the screens those shells reach still dropped into a Material screen mid-app — which is `MIGRATION.md`'s last large v2 item.

This takes the design's own trio, grouped that way because they share one shell (`M2Screen` / `M2PersonRow`, already ported as `V2Screen` / `V2PersonRow` for the Prayer log).

| | Now reads as |
|---|---|
| **People** | search, then *In your care* (longest since you talked, first) and *Everyone else* (alphabetical, with who added them) |
| **The Journey** | the kanban as a horizontal step picker, yours first at each step, a "Move a step" sheet per person |
| **Gatherings** | *Who we've missed* with a text you can send, the sessions we've had with each roster expanding **in place**, then *Coming up* |

`The Board · Messages · Settings · Contact detail` stay for a later pass, as do the sheets — including the one People's ＋ New opens.

## What's new underneath

**`@cisa/core`** — pure `splitDirectory` and `stageToneKey` in `directory.ts`, `touchWords` in `myday.ts`, and `matchesSearch` widened to the design's field set (name · major · year · hall · tags · notes). **402 → 412 tests.**

**The v2 shell** (`components/v2/Widget.tsx`) grew what `M2Screen` / `M2PersonRow` also carry: an optional back row (People is a *tab* for the full-timer and a *pushed* screen for the trainee, so `isPushedScreen` decides), a right-hand action, and the stage-dot-plus-line right side. Plus `V2RowCard` — the design's `.m2j-row .m2p-row{background:none}` makes the person row and its care action **one** card, which is why `V2PersonRow` gained `flat` — and `V2Input` / `V2Hint` / `V2Empty`. `roomForRole` joins `theme/v2.ts` because all three screens are reachable by more than one role and must stand in that role's room. `.m2-datebox` came out of `EndOfQueue` into `components/v2/DateBox.tsx` now that "Coming up" needs the same block.

## What reviewers should push back on if they disagree

**Strict design fidelity was the call again, and it costs surfaces.** Gone: People's stage-filter pills and its counts hero, The Journey's "Welcome someone new", and Gatherings' hero figures, gathering-type filter and **CSV export** (`lib/exportCsv.ts` with it — attendance was its only caller), plus the `RosterSheet` modal. Stage filtering is The Journey's job in v2, and export is desktop work — but export now has no mobile entry point at all.

**Two substitutions, carried forward rather than re-invented.** The design splits People on `c.owner === me`; a `Contact` has no owner here, so "In your care" is `personalContactIdsOf` — the picker's choice, else created-by-me — exactly as My Day and the full-timer's home read it. And the design's *Who we've missed* is "absent in 3 of the last 4" while core's tested `whoWeMissed` is "missed the last 2+", so the rule stays and the hint copy says what it actually computes rather than repeating the design's line.

**One thing dropped for want of a field**: the design prints each step's description under the picker, and `Stage` carries only `{id, label, color, order}`.

## Verification

`packages/core` 412/412 green · `tsc --noEmit` clean · lint 0 errors.

Walked live on Expo web against all four e2e role users, in light **and** dark:

- **Full-timer** — People as a tab with no back row, paper/navy room; a Journey move persisted through a reload (Unassigned 1→0, First Contact 2→3); roster cycling wrote (3 came → 4 → restored to 3).
- **Trainee** — all three pushed with back rows, green room, no tab bar.
- **Community** — Gatherings green, roster inert with *"Marking the roster is a full-timer or trainee job."*, as `canTakeAttendance` (operator+) intends.

No console errors on any path after exercising step switching and the move sheet.

⚠️ **Test-data drift**: verification moved *Kristin Castro* from Unassigned into First Contact in the e2e Firestore project and she was left there — her original stage was a stale label that couldn't be restored exactly. The attendance change was reverted.

Two structural details were corrected mid-verification by reading the design's own CSS rather than trusting screenshots: the active step pill is a full inversion (`.m2j-step.on{background:var(--n-inv)}`), not a tint — a tint is invisible in the dark rooms — and the row/action share one card.

title: feat(mobile): port the design's three role shells + the full-timer's prayer log
label: CLOSED
body:
## Why

The design project (`MOBILE-V2.md`; `views/mobile/{m2,member,ft}.jsx`) builds mobile as **three apps, each with its own navigation frame**. All four home screens were ported already — none of the shells were. Every role shared one Material six-tab bar, which `MIGRATION.md:1081` records as the last open box.

That had real consequences, not just cosmetic ones:

- a **Student** got a **People** tab onto the staff directory and a **Log** tab, both of which the design explicitly denies members (*"no CRM, no stages, no owners"*)
- **Messages** and **You** sat under a generic "More" list that printed raw hrefs and role labels
- the **full-timer** had no **Prayer log** screen at all

## What changed

### The three shells

| role | shell |
|---|---|
| Trainee | **no bar at all** — the queue fills the screen, ☰ opens a drawer |
| Student | Today · Prayer · Messages · You |
| Community | What's on · Prayer · Messages · You |
| Full-timer | Today · People · Messages · More |

Which route each tab sits on is a pure `tabsForRole` in `@cisa/core`'s new `shell.ts`, so the tab bar and the screens that need a back row *when they aren't a tab* (`isPushedScreen`) read one source rather than repeating role checks. `MEMBER_TABS` — sitting in `memberHome.ts` unused since the member app landed — finally has a consumer.

The bar wears the design's `.mbr-tabs`: **words, not invented icons**, a 5px active dot, and a terracotta unread badge on Messages.

**Messages moved into the tab group** (`app/(tabs)/messages/` with its own nested `Stack`), so a thread opens with the bar still under it, as `.mbr-stage` + `.mbr-tabs` do. Route groups don't affect paths — `/messages` and `/messages/[roomId]` are unchanged and every deep link (a home card's "Write back", a to-do notification) still lands.

### The full-timer's prayer log

`app/prayer-log.tsx` + `components/ft/FtPrayerLog.tsx` — the design's `FtPrayerLog`, which More opens and the home's **Carrying** glance tile now points at. It reads the **same `ftCarryRows`** the "Prayers to carry" widget reads (uncapped here, capped there) so the tile's number and the list's length can't disagree. `FtCarryRow` gains a `contactId` so a row can open the person's page.

### The trainee's queue chrome, caught up with the design

- meta row is now ☰ · `Today · N to look after` · `P of N`, and the counter spans the **whole day** (what's left plus what's already been looked after) instead of only what remains
- the floor names who's coming — `Then Ana, Rio, Kofi +2` / `Last one today` — instead of counting them
- the all-clear reads `That's everything, {name}.`
- "Look back at your week" is a **pushed screen** (`WeekLookBack`) rather than a list unfolding under the all-clear

Also added `V2Screen` / `V2PersonRow` to `components/v2/Widget.tsx` (the design's `M2Screen` / `M2PersonRow`), built for the prayer log and ready for the People/Journey/Gatherings pass.

## ⚠️ What this removes — please sanity-check

This follows the design **strictly**, which was the explicit call, and it costs entry points:

- **The drawer is exactly the design's six rows and More exactly its five.** Search, Notifications, Looking back, Answered, the Welcome form, Leave a note and Notes from the team are **no longer linked from anywhere on the phone**. Their routes and deep links still work; giving them a home is the next pass.
- **Students lose the People and Log tabs** — the design gives members no CRM.
- **The staff team-prayer screen is desktop-only.** Neither staff role has a Prayer tab now; the full-timer's Prayer log is read-mostly, so hold / set-status / update-burden / stop-holding move to the desk.
- **The Log tab is gone for everyone.** Logging keeps both its real entry points — the queue's ＋ FAB and the full-timer's "Log a moment" tile.

## Out of scope

Converting People, The Journey, Gatherings, The Board, Messages, Settings and Contact detail from Material to the v2 language. The design mounts no Field-notes view inside the mobile app at all; these still render the Material screens, now reached through the right shell. Tracked in `MIGRATION.md`.

## Testing

- **32 new cases** in `packages/core/test/shell.test.ts` — core suite 370 → **402 passing**
- `apps/mobile` typecheck clean; root lint 0 errors
- **Verified in Expo web signed in as all four roles**: trainee (no bar; drawer with exactly six rows; People pushes and comes back), student (Today · Prayer · Messages · You, no People/Log), Community (What's on · …), full-timer (More lists exactly the five design rows; Prayer log shows 6 matching the glance tile and "I prayed" sticks; a thread opens inside the Messages tab)

### Pre-existing, unrelated
The root typecheck and 4 web test files fail on a missing `chrono-node` — this worktree's `node_modules` predates that dependency. Confirmed against a clean tree; `npm install` at the root fixes it.

title: fix(coordination): stop the doc editor throwing the caret to the bottom
label: CLOSED
body:
## The bug

On `/coordination`, editing a page threw your caret to the bottom, wiped whatever you had selected, and made Cmd/Ctrl+Z jump to the end of the document.

## Root cause

All three symptoms come from one line in the bi-directional task sync added by #174 (`src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`). The effect serialized the **whole** page to Markdown, diffed it line-by-line against Firestore, and on any difference called `editor.commands.setContent(...)` — a whole-document delete + insert:

- With `Collaboration` active that rewrites the entire `Y.Doc`, so ProseMirror maps the selection to the end of the new document — **caret at the bottom of the page**, selection replaced.
- The Markdown round trip is lossy, so **selected content genuinely disappeared**.
- `StarterKit` runs with `undoRedo: false` (Yjs owns history), so each rewrite became one giant undo entry — **Cmd/Ctrl+Z undid a whole-doc replace and parked the caret at the end**.

It fired constantly while you typed, because `todos`/`team` are fresh arrays on every Firestore snapshot — including the snapshots the editor's own 1.2s save triggers. Worse, comparing serialized Markdown lines against `formatDocTaskMarkdown` output reads as "changed" *forever* for any indented task or any title containing Markdown punctuation, so it could thrash on every snapshot indefinitely.

Only the desktop page was affected — `CoordinationNotesMobile` and `EmbedCoordinationDoc` don't pass `todos`.

## The fix

The sync now works on `taskItem` **nodes**, not serialized text:

- `collectDocTaskNodes` + `planDocTaskEdits` (`src/lib/board.ts`) work out which checklist lines actually went stale.
- The editor patches only those, in **one transaction** marked `addToHistory: false` — so a teammate's change is never something you can undo.
- The line your caret is in is skipped, and re-syncs once you move off it.
- `syncMarkdownWithTasks` is replaced by `formatDocTaskText`/`parseDocTaskText`, so both sync directions share one format. Node-level comparison also removes the indentation/escaping mismatches that made the old string diff fire forever.

Markdown source view had the same whole-doc-replace pattern in five places; they now route through one helper that no-ops when the text is unchanged and restores the caret otherwise.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The riskiest part is the ProseMirror position math** (`pos + 2` into a `taskItem`'s paragraph). title: fix(board): stop the same person appearing several times in live presence
label: CLOSED
body:
## The problem

The live-presence stack on `/coordination` showed the same person three or four times, and repeated their name label as a remote caret inside the editor. The duplicates faded on their own after ~30 seconds, then came back on the next page load.

## What was actually happening

Not a rendering glitch — **dead editing sessions parked in Firebase RTDB.** Reading `board_docs_rtdb/{docId}/awareness` twice, 50s apart, on the F26 TC page:

| clientID | name | changed between samples? |
|---|---|---|
| 2362121536 | Kevin Munga | **yes → live** |
| 840341282 | Kevin Munga | no → ghost |
| 2306455879 | Kevin Munga | no → ghost |
| 2568911289 | Kevin Munga | no → ghost |
| 2637052531 | Kevin Munga | no → ghost |
| 3364200011 | Leonora Banman | no → ghost |

One live editor, five frozen ghosts, four of them the same person. Other Board pages held them too.

Three things stacked up:

1. **Presence nodes leaked and nothing ever reaped them.** `destroy()` called `onDisconnect(...).cancel()` *before* firing its own best-effort `set(null)` — it disarmed the safety net first, so any unmount whose delete didn't land (tab closed right after a page switch, offline, suspended mobile WebView) orphaned the node permanently. Separately, a client whose initial read failed returned from `bootstrap()` without ever arming `onDisconnect`, yet `publishAwareness()` stayed wired and kept writing the node — a guaranteed orphan every time. A fresh `Y.Doc` (so a fresh clientID) is minted per `DocEditor` mount, so one person accumulates one ghost per leaked mount on the same page.
2. **The avatar stack rendered one entry per Yjs clientID.** The awareness payload carried only `{ name, color }` — no uid — so collapsing by person wasn't even possible.
3. **The 30-second fade** was `y-protocols` evicting peers that hadn't heartbeated. That eviction is local-only; the RTDB node survived, which is why they reappeared on reload. The duplicate cursor labels were the same ghosts — two of them carried a non-null `cursor`.

## What changed

**`src/lib/yjsRtdbProvider.ts`**
- Publishing is gated on `onDisconnect` actually being armed, so a degraded client never writes a node it cannot clean up.
- `destroy()` no longer cancels the `onDisconnect` remove — the server-side delete stays as the backstop when the best-effort write doesn't land. The clientID is never reused, so a late remove is a no-op.
- `pagehide` is handled alongside `beforeunload` (the latter never fires in iOS Safari or the mobile WebView).
- New reaper: when `y-protocols` times a peer out at 30s, the peer's RTDB node is deleted too. Any client opening a page clears that page's orphans — **including the five already sitting there**, so no manual purge is needed. A peer that was merely offline republishes on its next 15s heartbeat, so it self-heals.

**`src/lib/presence.ts`** (new, pure) — `peersFromAwareness` collapses awareness to one face per person, keyed by uid, and drops your own other sessions. Falls back to the name as identity for clients still on the older build, and keeps anonymous clients separate rather than merging strangers.

**`src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`** — publishes `uid` in the caret's user payload (inert for the caret renderer, which reads only `name`/`color`) and uses the helper for the stack.

No change to the caret plugin: once the ghosts are gone the duplicate labels go with them, and two carets for one person's two genuinely-live tabs are correct — they sit at different positions.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **No rules change needed.** `database.rules.json` already lets any authed user write under a doc's `awareness`, which is what the cross-client reap relies on.
- **Answered design question:** one avatar per person, and never yourself — matching the existing "N others editing" tooltip.
- `CHANGELOG.md:249` claimed a previous PR "deduplicat[ed] live presence avatars by user name". `git log -L` on that effect shows it never shipped — that commit touched no such code. The entry is corrected in this PR rather than left to mislead the next person who reads it.

## Testing

- `npm test`: **894 passed, 0 failed**. Coverage holds above all four thresholds (85.7 / 75.69 / 81.6 / 87.86 vs. 85.5 / 75.5 / 81 / 87.5).
- 12 new tests across `src/test/presence.test.ts` and `src/test/yjsRtdbProvider.test.ts`, plus 3 in the editor suite — all written red first and confirmed failing for the right reasons before the fix.
- Production build clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean, new files lint clean.
- Dev server boots with no console errors.

**Not yet verified:** the live end-to-end drain. The ghosts are on a production page that had a live editor on it during the investigation, so that check belongs on this PR's Cloudflare preview. To confirm there: open the F26 TC page, leave it ~40s, then re-run

    npx firebase database:get /board_docs_rtdb/RfhXjR16LsZGB6gnvo6D/awareness --shallow

and the five ghost clientIDs should be gone, leaving only live clients.

title: Mobile v2: the member app is a calm scroll, not a dashboard
label: CLOSED
body:
> **Stacked on #171** — base is `claude/announcement-rooms`, so this diff shows only the member work. Merge #171 first and this retargets to `main` on its own.

The last of the design's four role shapes. Students and Community members were still on the Material `LandingStudent` / `LandingCommunity`; they now get `M2Member` (`MOBILE-V2.md`, "the MEMBER app") — a calm single scroll, because **members browse, they don't work a list**. No CRM anywhere: no stages, no owners, no contact ids, no metrics.

| Role | Design | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trainee | focus queue | ✅ #168/#169 | — |
| Full-timer | widgets home | ✅ #170 | — |
| **Student** | member app | `LandingStudent` (66 lines, Material) | **`MemberHomeScreen`** |
| **Community** | member app | `LandingCommunity` (98 lines, Material) | **`MemberHomeScreen`** |

**Home**: date + greeting + one honest line → **the next thing** as the one hero (RSVP; students also get "Bring a friend") → **a note from the team** → **announcements** → **also coming up** → Community's **Open your home** / a student's **Bring someone with you** → foot line. Prayer, Messages and "You" are v2 too.

## Three decisions worth reviewing

**The tab bar stays; the fork lives on the route.** As #168 and #170 both did, the design's own nav shell isn't ported — Home and Prayer are the existing tabs, Messages and You are reached through More. Each of the four routes forks on a new `memberRoleOf(role)`. Forking on the *route* rather than in the tab bar is deliberate: a deep link (a home card's "Write back", a notification) then lands on the right screen for whoever opened it.

**No third room in `theme/v2.ts`.** The design puts members in the *same green room as the trainee* (`.m2 deck mem` carries no `blue`; only the FT app forces navy), so member screens declare `Room room="queue"` and reuse `lightV2`/`darkV2` untouched. `components/ft/FtWidget.tsx` moved to **`components/v2/Widget.tsx`** — nothing in it was ever full-timer-specific, and it now has two consumers. That rename is most of the noise in the `components/ft/*` diff.

**One substitution**, documented in `memberHome.ts`'s header: the design's *"a note from the person who cares for you"* reads a `caredById` off a mock persona. There is no student↔full-timer relationship in this schema — no link at all between a user account and a `Contact` — so `noteFromTheTeam` reads the newest direct message from **any** full-timer, and the copy says "A note from {name}", never "who cares for you".

## What members send actually reaches someone

The collections shipped in #171 get their staff-side surfaces here, which is what keeps the member copy honest:

- Open prayer requests join **"Prayers to carry"**. `ftCarryRows` flattens a member's ask and a logged prayer into one list (asks first — someone reached out and is waiting), and `ftCarrying` now reads *those same rows*, so the "At a glance" tile's number and the widget under it can't disagree.
- Hospitality offers fill a new **"Homes open to students"** widget — read-only with a "Message them" that opens the DM, because matching a student to a table is a conversation, not a button.

## Verification

- `packages/core` **369/369** (46 new in `memberHome.test.ts`, plus `ftCarryRows` / `ftHomesOpen` coverage). `apps/mobile` has no tests by convention, so every derivation is pure and lives in core.
- Web **844/844**, coverage above every threshold, typecheck + lint + build clean on both apps.
- **Ran the app signed in as both the student and community e2e users**: home, prayer, messages and You in light and dark; RSVP chips, the hospitality form, the ask sheet. Two fixes came out of that — an account with no display name was greeted *"Hi Someone."*, and the pushed member screens had no back affordance.

### Known, and deliberate

- **The member writes stay `permission-denied` until #171's rules deploy.** Verified live that they fail gracefully through `handleFirestoreError` — nothing crashes — and every new subscription degrades quietly to empty rather than failing its screen.
- `LandingStudent` / `LandingCommunity` are left on disk but no longer routed to, exactly as #168/#170 left `LandingTrainee` and `components/myday/*`.

title: Announcements, and the schema mobile v2's member app needs
label: CLOSED
body:
Two things, both prerequisites for **the member v2 app** in the PR stacked on top of this one. Splitting here because this half touches the web app and ships `firestore.rules`, while the other half is mobile-only UI.

## Announcement conversations

A chat room the whole audience reads and **only Full-timers post to** — the design's "broadcast" (`MOBILE-V2.md`, the member app's "Announcements" block).

- `ChatRoom['type']` gains `'announcement'`.
- `firestore.rules` gates creating one *and* posting into one on `isAdmin()`, and blocks a member flipping the room's `type` to get around the post gate. The type check on `messages` create costs no extra document read — the parent room is already fetched for the membership check.
- `canPostToRoom` in `@cisa/core` is the client-side mirror, so web and mobile both show *"replies go to the team directly"* instead of a composer whose write would come back `permission-denied` with no explanation.
- **Authoring**: an admin-only third tab on the existing Create-chat modal (web) and sheet (mobile). Without it no announcement could ever exist, so the read side would be permanently empty. A group and an announcement take the same two inputs, so they share one form and differ only in which create call runs.

## The two collections the member app writes to

Landing ahead of the screens that use them — shared `@cisa/core` data modules, `firestore.rules` for both, and `hospitality.ts`'s availability vocabulary.

| | Shape | Why this shape |
|---|---|---|
| `prayerRequests/{id}` | asker owns it, staff read all | Deliberately **not** a `Prayer`: that entity hangs off a `contactId`, and a member is a user account, not a contact. Top-level rather than a `users/{uid}` subcollection **precisely so staff can list every open ask in one subscription** — a private subcollection couldn't reach the Full-timer's home. |
| `hospitalityOffers/{uid}` | doc id **is** the uid | One standing offer per household that gets updated, rather than a pile of stale ones — and the owner rule is a plain `isOwner(uid)` with no field check. |

## Verification

- **84/84 firestore rules tests against a real emulator** (19 new, 65 → 84): a member writing their own request/offer, a member denied someone else's, an update that tries to reassign a request, staff reading, only staff listing the open homes, and a non-admin denied both creating an announcement room and posting into one.
- `packages/core` **312/312**; web **844/844** with coverage above every threshold (functions 81.05% ≥ 81%, branches 75.66% ≥ 75.5%); typecheck + lint + build clean on both apps.
- New web tests cover both branches of the composer guard, the admin-only tab, and `createAnnouncementRoom`.

## One thing for reviewers

**The rules only take effect once `deploy-firestore-rules.yml` runs on merge.** Until then the two new collections are unreachable in production — which is fine here, since nothing reads or writes them until the stacked PR lands.

title: Mobile v2: the full-timer's home is a widgets screen, not a dashboard
label: CLOSED
body:
Continues the mobile v2 port from the Claude Design project (`019e2501-…`,
`MOBILE-V2.md`). #168 and #169 gave the **trainee** a focus queue. Full-timers
were still landing on `MyDayScreen` — the desktop-derived dashboard the whole v2
rethink was a reaction to. This PR closes the first of the three items
`MIGRATION.md` was tracking as outstanding.

## What changed

Full-timers now land on an **at-a-glance widgets home** (the design's `M2FT`,
direction 05, plus its Jul 26, 2026 revision item 2): warm paper by day,
near-black navy by night.

Top to bottom — date + greeting + one honest summary line ("3 things need you
today · 2 from the team · 1 person gone quiet") → two quick tiles (Log a moment /
Hand something over) → **At a glance** → **Needs you today** → **From the team** →
**Gone quiet in your care** → **Prayers to carry** → **the week-ahead strip** → a
foot line saying the heavy work waits on the desk.

Powers are **people actions only**: log, encourage, write back, hand a to-do
over, pray. Board pages, gatherings and kinds stay a desktop job — that foot line
is the design's way of saying so.

| | |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/ftHome.ts` | Every derivation as a pure, `now`-injectable function. **45 new tests, core 251 → 296.** |
| `apps/mobile/src/lib/useFtHomeData.ts` | The live data, a sibling of `useTraineeLandingData`. Writes go through the existing `data/todos`, `data/threads`, `data/inboxReads`. |
| `apps/mobile/src/components/ft/` | Ten components, reusing `components/queue/atoms` rather than growing a second primitives file. |
| `apps/mobile/src/theme/v2.ts` | **Two rooms** behind a `V2RoomContext`. |
| `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/index.tsx` | The `default:` arm renders `FtHomeScreen`. |

### Two rooms, one set of tokens

`theme/v2.ts` now holds the trainee's green room **and** the full-timer's
paper/navy one. Every green→navy value is `mobile-blue.css`'s own mapping
(`16332b`→`17293f`, `5f7a68`→`607182`, …); the cream paper, terracotta, violet,
amber and semantic green are unchanged, so the interior tints #169 tuned for the
white card carry straight over.

A **context**, not a `useV2Theme(room)` argument — the shared v2 atoms
(`Kicker`, `PersonMark`, `PrimaryButton`, …) then work in either room without
knowing which one they're in. **`lightV2` / `darkV2` are untouched byte for
byte**; worth confirming in review, since it's the "did the trainee queue move?"
gate.

The v2 hard-rules comment is re-scoped in the same commit: 44px targets, the ink
floor and the non-scrolling foot stay universal, but *"no metrics, no KPI tiles"*
now belongs to the trainee's room alone. The full-timer's "At a glance" tiles and
week strip **are** direction 05; an unscoped rule would read as a violation to
whoever comes next.

## Three substitutions the mock data allowed and this schema doesn't

Each is documented at its definition in `ftHome.ts`, and each is a judgement call
worth a second opinion:

1. **The glance's second tile is "Next gathering", not the design's "Team
   prayer".** There is no huddle entity in this schema, and `Event` carries no
   time of day — the design's tile, whose big value *is* a time, cannot be built.
   It shows the day word, the gathering's name and its location, off the next
   upcoming `Event`.
2. **"weighs heavy" is `status === "ongoing"`.** `PrayerRecord` has no priority
   field; `ongoing` is the schema's own "still being carried" signal.
3. **"I prayed just now" is device-local**, sharing `queueState`'s per-day
   `handled` map exactly as the trainee queue's identical button already does,
   rather than widening `firestore.rules` for a shared "who prayed today". Safe
   while the roles are disjoint (`manager` → the queue, `admin` → this screen),
   and noted at the call site.

## Deliberately not ported

The design's **four-tab FT shell** (Today · People · Messages · More) and its
separate **Prayer log** screen — the same call #168 made about the ☰ drawer. The
bottom tab bar already carries navigation, so every widget link routes into the
app's own screens (`/prayer`, `/people`, `/journey`, `/attendance`,
`/contact/[id]`).

## Notes for the reviewer

- **`useFtHomeData` duplicates several of `useMyDayData`'s subscriptions** rather
  than extending it, because `MyDayScreen` still reads that hook and this change
  leaves it alone. Recorded in `MIGRATION.md` so it doesn't read as an accident —
  the same call #168 made with `useTraineeLandingData`.
- **`MyDayScreen` and all of `components/myday` are left on disk, unrouted**, as
  #168 did with `LandingTrainee`. Rollback is a one-line route change.
- **Known gap, recorded:** orphaning `MyDayScreen` also orphans
  `ContactsPickerSheet`, so the "who are my people" picker is unreachable on
  mobile. The new home still *honours* the preference — `personalContactIdsOf`
  falls back to created-by-me when unset — so a full-timer who picked their
  people on the web keeps them; picking a new one is a desktop job for now.
- **An admin who isn't in `FT_TRAINEES`** gets the home with "From the team"
  absent and that clause dropped from the summary line. `inboxItemsFor` already
  returns `[]` outside that map, so the widget self-hides — no extra gate.
- **No automated component tests**, per the standing convention for
  `apps/mobile` (`MIGRATION.md`): pure logic is tested in `packages/core`, the
  screens are checked by hand. That's policy here, not an oversight.

## Bug fixed along the way — shared `components/ui/Sheet.tsx`

**A sheet that mounted already-visible never opened.** `present()` is silently
dropped when it lands in the modal's own mount commit — the ref is live, but
`BottomSheetModal` hasn't finished registering with the root provider, and since
`visible` never transitions again nothing retries. Every sheet **keyed by the
person it's about** hits this, because changing that person remounts the sheet in
the very render that opens it.

Deferred one macrotask. `setTimeout`, not `requestAnimationFrame` — rAF never
fires while the tab is backgrounded, which is the same stall the backdrop above
it is already written to survive. This is a shared component: all 12 sheets are
in its blast radius, so it deserves a careful look.

## Verification

- `packages/core` — **296/296** (24 files), up from 251.
- Root `npm run typecheck` — clean. `apps/mobile` `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.

title: Mobile v2: the focus card goes white and fills the room, and the queue is the trainee's own
label: CLOSED
body:
Continues the native mobile v2 (M2) port. Two things, both from the Claude Design project (`019e2501-…`, `MOBILE-V2.md`).

## 1. The Jul 26, 2026 design revision, item 1 — the card is WHITE and fills the room

The focus card was a cream (`#f4f1e6`) content-sized sheet, so a short card floated as a stub in the middle of the room. It is now white and `flex: 1` with a `minHeight: 0` body — direction 02, "One at a Time" — so it spans the height between the meta row and the floor, with the actions resting on the floor.

The light palette's interior tints are retuned for the white ground (hairlines `#e6e3dc`, notes/about `#f4f2ee`, outline `#dcd8d0`), plus a new `react` token (`#fbfaf8`): `card2` was doing double duty for the "about" chip and the reaction chips, which the revision tints differently. **Ink and the entire night palette are untouched**, exactly as the revision specifies. `AllTodayList` rows and `EndOfQueue` share `c.card`, so they go white too — intended, one card surface.

Revision items 2 (the FT hybrid home) and 3 (one type voice) concern member/FT v2 screens that don't exist natively yet; items 4–6 are prototype-only.

## 2. The prefs #168 deferred — the queue is the trainee's own call

`buildQueue` and `isOnCampus` already took a `QueuePrefs` / `OnCampusWindow`, but nothing on the phone could change either, which left the day-cap note ("N more are waiting for tomorrow — a day only holds so much") with no way to act on it.

- **`packages/core/src/queue.ts`** gains `normalizeQueuePrefs`, `normalizeOnCampusWindow`, `hourLabel` and `onCampusSummary`. Everything read back off a device is clamped per field, and a window that could never open (no days, or `from >= to`) falls back whole. **15 new tests — packages/core 236 → 251.**
- **`apps/mobile/src/lib/queuePrefs.ts`** — the AsyncStorage store (`cisa.m2.prefs.<uid>`, the design's own key), a direct sibling of `queueState.ts`.
- **`apps/mobile/app/queue-settings.tsx`** — the v2-styled "Your queue" screen: the on-campus window (days + from/until), when to nudge you (quiet-after days, quiet people at a time, prayers to carry, how much a day holds), and "Bring back today's queue". Reachable from *Everything today → How today is built* and from a trainee-only row on Settings.
- `OnCampusStrip`'s local `hour()` is now core's `hourLabel`, so the strip and the settings screen can't disagree about when the window ends.

### Two deliberate departures from the prototype's `M2Settings`

1. **The prefs are device-local, not Firestore.** Putting them in `UserPreferences` would mean widening `firestore.rules` and deploying it before the screen could save anything, and the design treats them as phone settings.
2. **"How it looks" is not duplicated onto the v2 screen.** Settings' `AppearancePicker` already owns light/dark app-wide for every role; two controls over one piece of state is a bug waiting to happen.

## Verification

- `packages/core`: **251/251** (`npm test`). The three pre-existing `process`-type errors in that package's `tsc --noEmit` are unchanged — confirmed identical on a clean tree.
- `apps/mobile`: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean.
- **iOS Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro), signed in as the e2e Trainee**: a short card spans the full height with its actions on the floor; a long card still scrolls its body while the foot stays put; dark mode is unchanged; and every control on "Your queue" reflects and writes its pref, with the header line reading "Tue & Wed, 12pm–3pm" off `onCampusSummary`.

**One caveat, stated plainly:** the card geometry was checked against a *temporary local fixture*, since that account's queue is empty — its 17 directory people aren't `createdBy` it, so `traineeMyPeople` returns nothing, and lowering "quiet after" to 1 day changed nothing. Every route to a real card meant writing test data into the team's live Firestore, so I didn't. The fixture was reverted; the pref→queue effect is proven by the core unit tests rather than on-device.

One fix found during that pass: the hour strips opened scrolled to 7am with the selected hour off-screen, so they now scroll the selection into view (the `scrollLeft` approach the design uses for The Journey's step picker).

## Not in this pass

The full-timer widgets home (revision item 2), the member v2 app for student/community, the ☰ drawer, and the blue-room tint — all tracked in the new `MIGRATION.md` section.
