title: Mobile v2: the trainee's home is a focus queue, not a dashboard
label: CLOSED
body:
Ports the Claude Design project's **mobile v2** direction ([`MOBILE-V2.md`](https://claude.ai/design/p/019e2501-d939-73e9-8f0f-af68b36b8e64?file=MOBILE-V2.md), direction 02 "One at a Time") into the native app.

## Why

Mobile had been designed desktop-first and then framed into a phone — functional, but still a **dashboard**. v2 rebuilds the trainee's home around one idea: a full-screen **focus queue**. One actionable card at a time, whole screen, "Later" advances, and the queue **ends**. No metrics, no infinite scroll, no recurring gatherings.

Trainees previously landed on `LandingTrainee.tsx` — a scrolling dashboard (greeting · "What's waiting on you" · "Your people" · "Prayers you're holding"). That's the shape v2 exists to replace.

## What changed

**Five card kinds**, each wired to the data modules the rest of the app already writes with, so the desktop screens agree:

| Card | Wired to |
|---|---|
| A to-do due now | `setTodoDone` / `updateTodo`, deep-links the Board page |
| A message from the full-timer who cares for you | `toggleReaction`, `addThreadMessage`, `InboxReads` |
| A follow-up you promised | `sms:`, Quick Capture |
| Someone gone quiet | `sms:`, Quick Capture |
| A prayer to carry | see caveat below |

- **`packages/core/src/queue.ts`** — `buildQueue()` as a pure function: group ordering (due → full-timer message → follow-ups/quiet → prayers), "later" re-queue by defer time, and a day cap that **never** holds back a to-do that is actually due (a promise isn't held back). 18 new tests; core is 236/236.
- **`apps/mobile/src/theme/v2.ts`** — the v2 palette as its own layer: light green room `#16332b` + cream sheet `#f4f1e6`, the `mobile-night.css` dark room, the five card-kind tones, radii, shadows. Kept **separate from `tokens.ts`** — every other screen still depends on the Material set. Manrope 500–800 + Instrument Serif loaded alongside the existing fonts.
- **`apps/mobile/src/components/queue/`** — `QueueScreen`, `FocusCard` (swipe-to-later via gesture-handler + Reanimated), `QueueCard`, `EndOfQueue`, `AllTodayList`, `ReplySheet`, `OnCampusStrip`, `atoms`.
- **`apps/mobile/src/lib/queueState.ts`** — per-day handled/later state on AsyncStorage, reset at midnight.

## Reviewer notes

**Four things worth a look:**

1. **"I prayed just now" only marks the card done for the day.** `PrayerRecord` has no `prayedBy` field and there's no team prayer log — adding one is a Firestore-rules change I kept out of scope. The button's copy doesn't claim more than it does, but this is the one place the port is deliberately shallower than the design.

2. **Nobody has yet seen the queue against real Firestore data.** The mobile app has no `__e2eSignIn` helper (only the web app does), so I verified the rendering through a temporary fixture route — since deleted, along with its `PUBLIC_ROUTES` entry. The data plumbing is covered by the core tests, but the live pass is still owed.

3. **A latent bug fix rides along in `useInboxReads`** (`src/lib/data/inboxReads.ts`). It returned a module singleton whose identity never changed, so any `useMemo` depending on it went stale — the re-render fired but derived values didn't recompute. It now returns a fresh wrapper per emission. This also silently fixes `waitingUnread` in the trainee landing and the inbox derivation in `useMyDayData`.

4. **`LandingTrainee.tsx` is still on disk**, just no longer routed to (CLAUDE.md §3 — pre-existing code isn't deleted as a side effect). It's the only place a trainee sees "Your people" and the shared prayer rows, so it's worth deciding deliberately whether the drawer-level People screen covers that before removing it.

**Small additive changes to shared components**, all backward-compatible: `Sheet` gained an optional `backgroundColor`; `QuickCaptureSheet` gained an optional `initialContact` (the Log tab's call site is untouched); `app/contact/[contactId].tsx` now honours `?tab=prayer`, not just `?tab=thread`.

**Out of scope for this pass**, per the agreed plan: the ☰ drawer (bottom tabs stay), the v2 Settings screen and its editable prefs (the queue reads the defaults — quiet 2 days, 2 quiet people, 3 prayers, a day holds 8), and the blue-room tint.

## Verification

- `packages/core` — **236/236** across 23 files (18 new in `test/queue.test.ts`).
- Root `tsc --noEmit` and `apps/mobile` `tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npm run lint` — **322 warnings, 0 errors, unchanged from baseline**; every file this PR touches lints clean.
- Root `test:coverage` — above all four thresholds (web is untouched).
- Rendered every card kind, the "Everything today" list, and the end-of-queue in the mobile-web preview at **390 and 360px**, light and dark. Swipe-to-later confirmed (translate + rotate + fade). Two issues the screenshots caught and I fixed: the all-clear mark was `primary`-on-room (invisible in light — it needs the cream inverse), and the tone badge needed the wrap it now has, confirmed on the 360px `follow` card whose label overflows a single row.
- **Not done:** the iOS Simulator pass. Web proves the gesture pipeline, but shadows and fonts do diverge on native.

title: fix(mobile): patch @gorhom/bottom-sheet window-collision crash on native iOS
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

- Opening any bottom sheet (all 12 share `apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Sheet.tsx`) crashed with `ReanimatedError: Property 'window' doesn't exist` on a real native iOS build — never reproducible on Expo web, so it went unnoticed until a live Simulator build.
- Root cause is upstream, not this repo: `@gorhom/bottom-sheet@5.2.14`'s `useAnimatedLayout.ts` destructures `Dimensions.addEventListener('change', ({ window }) => ...)`, and `react-native-reanimated` ≥3.15's Babel plugin added `window` to its "not captured" identifier list — treating that variable as the (nonexistent, on the UI-thread worklet runtime) global object instead of capturing it as a closure. This is a regression introduced in the exact installed version (5.2.14) — [gorhom/react-native-bottom-sheet#2678](https://github.com/gorhom/react-native-bottom-sheet/issues/2678) — with an open, unmerged fix PR ([#2679](https://github.com/gorhom/react-native-bottom-sheet/pull/2679)).
- Patched locally via `patch-package` (renames the colliding variable, adds the missing listener cleanup — matching the upstream fix PR) across `src`, `lib/module`, and `lib/commonjs`. Added `patch-package` as a devDependency + a `postinstall` script to `apps/mobile/package.json` so the patch reapplies on every fresh install.
- Updated `CHANGELOG.md` and `MIGRATION.md` with the root-cause writeup and verification status.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `patch-package`'s generated patch reapplies correctly on a clean `npm install` (deleted `node_modules/@gorhom/bottom-sheet` and reinstalled).
- [x] Built and ran the app on the iPhone 16e Simulator (real native build, not Expo web).
- [x] Verified 11 of the 12 sheets sharing this primitive open/close with **zero crashes**: `InviteSheet`, `EditRoleSheet`, `RemoveAccessSheet`, `AddContactSheet`, `HoldPrayerSheet`, `MoveSheet`, `QuickCaptureSheet`, `RosterSheet`, `CreateChatSheet`, `ChatDetailsSheet`, `HistoryFilterSheet`.

## Summary

- **30-day Trash auto-purge**: no scheduled server-side job exists in this repo, so this is a lazy sweep — whenever a Trash view loads (mobile or the new web one), anything trashed 30+ days ago is permanently deleted. Added `purgeExpiredTrash`/`isExpiredTrash` to `packages/core/src/data/board.ts` and the new `src/lib/data/board.ts`.
- **New web Trash view** (`/coordination/trash`, admin-only): Trash previously only existed on mobile — deleting a page from the web editor had no web-side recovery path. Mirrors mobile's Trash screen (Restore, "Delete Forever" behind a confirm).
- **Pin to top**: `pinned?: boolean` on `BoardDoc` + a `docSortOrder` comparator (pinned-first, then newest-first), with an admin-only pin toggle on both web's `DocRow` and mobile's `DocCard`.
- **Insert link with custom display text**: the TipTap `Link` mark was already active but had no UI. Added a toolbar button and a selection pill-menu option, both opening a new `LinkComposer` popover (modeled on the existing `NoteComposer`).
- **Fixed the live-collaboration cursor label pushing page content down**: `@tiptap/extension-collaboration-caret` renamed its generated classes to `collaboration-carets__*` (plural), which `src/index.css` never picked up after an earlier rename — added the missing selectors.

label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
- Adds `"build:web": "expo export -p web"` to `apps/mobile/package.json` — the missing production web build (only a dev-server script existed before). A route-by-route comparison of the web app's routes against `apps/mobile/app/` confirmed screen-level parity already existed; the real Phase 6 gap was the missing production export.
- **Fixes a real production-only bug found during verification**: the exported static bundle threw `Firebase: Error (auth/invalid-api-key)` on load. `apps/mobile/src/lib/firebase.ts` read `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` env vars through a `const env = process.env; env.EXPO_PUBLIC_X` alias — Expo's babel plugin only statically inlines the literal `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_X` expression shape into production bundles, so the alias defeated it and the value came through as `undefined`. Dev mode never surfaced this, since Metro's dev server injects a live, populated `process.env` at runtime instead of relying on static replacement. Fixed by referencing `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_X` directly for each var.
- Adds a `mobile-web-dist` launch config (`.claude/launch.json`) for locally serving the static export.
- Documents remaining Phase 6 scope in `MIGRATION.md`/`SETUP.md`: retiring the old web app is blocked on an operational decision (three competing, non-automated deployment docs, no CI deploy workflow for either app), and reconciling React versions (web 19 vs Expo's pinned 18.3) is deliberately deferred as a separate, higher-risk Expo SDK bump touching ~15 pinned native deps.

## Verification
- `cd apps/mobile && npm run build:web` exits 0, no errors.

label: CLOSED

## Summary
- `OnTheHorizon.tsx`'s pending-task row rendered `Due: {date}` via `format(new Date(task.dueDate), 'MMM d')`. `task.dueDate` is a bare `yyyy-MM-dd` string, which the JS spec parses as UTC midnight — in any behind-UTC timezone (confirmed live: `America/Los_Angeles`, UTC-7) this lands on the previous day, so a task due "tomorrow" displayed as due today.

- Exported `toLocalDate` from `myday.ts` and switched both mobile components to use it instead of raw `new Date(...)`.

## Why
The stored due dates were always correct — this was purely a display bug caused by UTC-midnight parsing of a timezone-naive date string, matching a bug class the codebase had already solved once (`dueChip`) but not applied consistently.

title: Mobile: fix stuck bottom-sheet backdrop blocking clicks on web
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug in the shared `Sheet` primitive (`apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Sheet.tsx`) where closing any bottom sheet on Expo web could leave a full-viewport, nearly-invisible click-blocker over the entire app.

**Root cause:** `@gorhom/bottom-sheet`'s default `BottomSheetBackdrop` only flips `pointer-events` to `none` once its Reanimated-driven close animation crosses a threshold index. On web, that animation is scheduled entirely via `requestAnimationFrame` (confirmed in Reanimated's `JSReanimated.scheduleOnUI` — no fallback), which can stall indefinitely (a backgrounded/hidden tab, a dropped frame) and never complete. When that happens, the backdrop is left stuck mid-fade with `pointer-events: auto`, silently swallowing every click behind it — even though it's barely visible.

**Fix:**
- Added a custom `SheetBackdrop` that gates `pointerEvents` on the `visible` prop directly — a synchronous React state flip that never depends on any animation finishing. The Reanimated-driven opacity fade is now purely decorative (`pointerEvents="none"`), so it's harmless even if it never settles.
- Forced a duration-bound timing animation on web only (`useBottomSheetTimingConfigs`, matching the library's existing Android default) instead of the default spring, as defense-in-depth against throttled-but-not-fully-dead `requestAnimationFrame` in real user tabs.
- Also bumped the local `mobile-web` dev port in `.claude/launch.json` (8081 → 8091), since 8081 was occupied by an unrelated process from another worktree during verification.

This is the one shared `Sheet` component used by all 12 bottom sheets in the app (My Day, People, Journey, Settings, Messages, History, Attendance, Prayer), so the fix applies uniformly without touching any individual call site.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes clean in `apps/mobile`
- [x] Reproduced the bug live on Expo web: opened a sheet, triggered close, confirmed the backdrop DOM node stayed at `pointer-events: auto` / non-zero opacity indefinitely (probed via direct `getComputedStyle` checks)
- [x] Confirmed the fix live: after the change, the same close action flips the backdrop to `pointer-events: none` immediately, with zero dependency on animation completion
- [x] Confirmed via code audit that all 12 sheet call sites use the identical `visible`/`onClose` API with no way to bypass the backdrop, so the fix applies to every sheet
- [ ] Native (iOS/Android) drag-to-dismiss / backdrop tap-to-close not re-verified on a simulator in this pass — the change preserves the existing spring animation on native and uses the same `pointerEvents` RN API, so no behavior change is expected there, but a follow-up device check is worthwhile

title: Fix OpenWiki Update workflow: remove stray AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md inside openwiki/
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

The scheduled `OpenWiki Update` workflow has failed three days running, each on a different cause. #142 and #144 fixed the first two (missing `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, then unconfigured LangSmith tracing). Today's run gets all the way through doc generation and then dies with:

```
/openwiki/AGENTS.md lacks YAML front matter.
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

- `openwiki/AGENTS.md` and `openwiki/CLAUDE.md` are stray files accidentally committed *inside* the wiki output directory back in the original setup commit (`350242c`). Per [OpenWiki's docs](https://github.com/langchain-ai/openwiki), `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` are only ever meant to live at the repo root — they were never meant to also exist inside `openwiki/`.
- Diffing confirms both are exact duplicates of the `<!-- OPENWIKI:START -->…<!-- OPENWIKI:END -->` block already present in the real root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`.
- `openwiki/.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml` is also a stray duplicate — and a stale one (still has the pre-#142/#144 `openrouter`/LangSmith config), confirming it's dead and untouched since the initial commit.

## Summary

Resolves the mobile migration's top technical risk (tracked in `MIGRATION.md`): proving the web app's collaborative TipTap/Yjs document editor can run inside `apps/mobile`'s `react-native-webview`, with live Yjs/RTDB sync working.

- **Design pivot from the original scoping**: rather than extracting `DocEditor` into a standalone JS bundle with new build tooling (none existed in the repo), this reuses the **already-deployed web SPA** as the "bundle." `DocEditor` only needed one `export` keyword added (`src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`) — it already closes over its module-scope helpers lexically, so no real extraction was required.
- New bare, unauthenticated `/embed/coordination/:docId` route (`src/views/EmbedCoordinationDoc.tsx`), wired in `src/App.tsx` next to the existing `/signup` public-route precedent, which authenticates itself via `signInWithCustomToken`.
- New self-service `POST /api/mint-custom-token` endpoint (`server.ts`) that exchanges the caller's own Firebase ID token for a short-lived custom token — no privilege escalation, reuses the existing `authenticateFirebaseUser` helper.
- New mobile host screen (`apps/mobile/app/coordination.tsx`) that fetches the custom token and hosts the WebView, delivering the token via `injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded` (not a post-load `postMessage`) to avoid a listener-not-mounted-yet race.
- `server.ts`'s `admin.initializeApp` now passes an explicit `serviceAccountId` — `createCustomToken` needs a signing credential that this environment's ADC (a user identity) can't provide without it.

## Why

`MIGRATION.md` called this the single biggest architectural unknown in the whole migration — if the collaborative editor couldn't be hosted in a WebView with working real-time sync, the entire "Coordination Notes / The Board" screen would need a different approach. That risk is now resolved and verified.

## Scope

Deliberately narrow, matching the spike's intent — not the full Board screen:
- Hardcoded to one seeded doc (`demo-board-team`), no doc picker
- `contacts`, `onPromote`, `onDelete` stubbed as no-ops in the embed route
- Verified against `http://localhost:3000` only (iOS Simulator reaches the Mac's loopback directly); pointing at a deployed URL needs redeploying the new server endpoint separately

A full Board/doc-browser mobile screen remains separate, unstarted Phase 4 work — see the updated `MIGRATION.md`.

## One-time environment setup (already done, documented for reviewers)

`createCustomToken` requires the calling identity to have `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the `firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc` service account (keyless — matches this project's existing WIF-over-keys convention rather than a downloaded service-account key).

## Summary
This Pull Request addresses several usability and correctness issues on the coordination page and the feedback flows.

### Changes
1. **Feedback Limits & FAB Visibility**:
   - Increased the payload size limit to `50mb` in `server.ts` to handle high-resolution screenshots without causing `413 Payload Too Large` errors.
   - Wrapped the FAB hiding and showing logic in a `try...finally` block to guarantee the icon is restored if screenshot generation fails.
2. **Markdown View & Auto-Indentation**:
   - Made the raw Markdown source textarea editable and added custom keydown handlers to support basic indentation controls (`Tab` to indent 2 spaces, `Shift-Tab` to outdent, and `Enter` to auto-indent/match preceding indentation).
   - Set the wrapper container background to `bg-surface` to clean up the blank bottom gray area.
3. **Hierarchy Preservation**:
   - Debounced syncing the markdown textarea content to the ProseMirror editor (1000ms delay during typing) to prevent ProseMirror from dismantling nested lists and flattening subpoints during intermediate invalid document states.
4. **AI Insights Caching & Manual Refresh**:
   - Side-panel toggling now uses cached `insightsData` without triggering the API every time.
   - Added a manual refresh button in the header of the AI Insights panel to pull new changes.
5. **DatePicker Scroll Fix**:
   - Removed window scroll-blocking inside `TodoComposer`.
   - Set the modal overlay container to `overflow-y-auto` and positioned the anchored popup card using `position: absolute` so that users can naturally scroll down when the DatePicker calendar goes off-screen.

title: fix: mobile cold-sign-in crash back to login screen
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary
- Fixes a pre-existing bug in `apps/mobile` where signing in from a cold/logged-out state could crash the app back to the login screen.
- Root cause: `useMyDayData`'s Firestore subscription effect depended only on `[fixture]`, so on the very first render after sign-in (before `uid`/`auth.currentUser` was set) it queried Firestore anyway, got `permission-denied`, and `handleFirestoreError` unconditionally threw from inside an `onSnapshot` error callback — crashing the `<MyDay>` tree and bouncing the user back to `/login` via the error-boundary remount.
- Fix has two parts:
  1. Gate the team-data subscription effect on `uid` (mirroring the pattern already used by the per-user effect further down in the same file), so it no longer fires while auth isn't ready.
  2. `handleFirestoreError` now accepts an optional `{ rethrow?: boolean }`; the My Day load-error path passes `{ rethrow: false }` since it already sets `error` state itself — the throw was redundant and was what crashed the component tree.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in `apps/mobile` passes.
- [x] Verified live: ran the `mobile-web` Expo dev server, cleared IndexedDB/localStorage for a true cold/logged-out state, signed in with the fulltimer/admin e2e test user in a real Chrome tab — landed cleanly on the My Day cockpit with no crash and no bounce back to `/login`.
- apps/mobile has no test runner configured (root `vitest.config.ts` excludes `apps/**`), so no unit test was added — this fix was verified behaviorally instead.

title: Build native My Day cockpit, live end-to-end
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

- Ports the flagship **My Day** screen to React Native + Expo (`apps/mobile`), building on the Phase 0 foundation from #115.
- Extracts the pure My Day derivations (leaders/stale-leader, task/prayer splits, this-week, due-date presets) into `packages/core/src/myday.ts` with unit tests, so web and mobile share one behavior oracle — `packages/core` is now 49/49 tests.
- Adds a minimal mobile auth context + email/password login (`src/lib/AuthProvider.tsx`, `app/login.tsx`), gated by a `<Redirect>` in `app/_layout.tsx`. No invitation/auto-provisioning logic (e2e/dev users already have `/users/{uid}` docs); native Google Sign-In is left for a later spike.
- Wires a live Firestore data hook (`useMyDayData`) + thin write modules (`src/lib/data/*`) mirroring the web app's `MyDay.tsx` / `lib/*`.
- Builds the full native screen (`src/components/myday/*`): hero, relational nudge, "From the team" inbox (scan/encourage/remind with AsyncStorage-backed read state), tasks (add/edit/complete/delete), your sheep, your week, your prayers (status + answered-testimony composer), figures footer, contacts-picker bottom sheet.
- Re-aligns the bottom tabs to the mobile design's shell (Home · People · Log · Journey · Prayer · More); Journey and Log are placeholder screens for now.
- Adds a dev `console.warn` when the Firebase API key is unset (closes an open review item from #115).

## Why

My Day is the app's home screen and the natural screen to prove out live auth + a live Firestore data layer on mobile — the two prerequisites the migration roadmap (`MIGRATION.md`) already called out as next. Landing it end-to-end (not just a static scaffold) locks in the "screen port" pattern for the screens that follow.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/core`: `npm test` — 49/49 passing; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] `apps/mobile`: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] Verified live on Expo web (`npx expo start --web`): logged in as the e2e Full-timer (`cisa-ft@hub.com`), confirmed real Firestore data rendered (13 real "From the team" inbox items), tested the inbox action sheet + mark-scanned (persisted through a page reload), checked both light and dark themes at mobile viewport, zero console errors.
- [ ] Not yet covered: adding/editing a task or prayer end-to-end on a live device (typechecked + code-reviewed but not click-tested in this pass); native iOS/Android build.

title: Phase 0: React Native + Expo mobile foundation + shared @cisa/core
label: CLOSED
body:
## What & why

Foundation for the **web → mobile pivot to React Native + Expo** (not Flutter — keeps TypeScript/React, reuses business logic and the React-authored design). This PR is **purely additive**: a new native app + a shared logic package, alongside the existing web app.

> **The existing web app + backend are untouched.** The only changed tracked file is `.claude/launch.json` (adds a `mobile-web` run config). No `src/`, `server.ts`, `functions/`, `vite.config.ts`, or root `package.json` changes — desktop and mobile web build/deploy exactly as before.

## What's in here (Phase 0)

- **`packages/core`** — platform-agnostic shared TS (types, `permissions`/`NAV_ITEMS`, `board`, `inbox`, `walking`, `seasons`, `threads`, `utils`) with vitest. This is the "one codebase" win — logic shared by web + mobile.
- **`apps/mobile`** — Expo SDK 52 + `expo-router` shell:
  - Theme (light + dark) ported verbatim from the web Material tokens (warm "Field notes" palette), follows OS color scheme.
  - Primitive library (Screen, AppText, Button, Card, Chip, Avatar, SectionHead, StatusPill).
  - Bottom-tab nav driven by the shared `NAV_ITEMS`.
  - Firebase JS SDK wired for RN (`getAuth` auto-persistence — v12 removed `getReactNativePersistence`; named Firestore db id; opt-in RTDB).
  - Self-contained (own `node_modules`); resolves `@cisa/core` via a Metro alias (no workspace hoist — web is React 19, Expo is 18.3).
- **`MIGRATION.md`** — living status + full remaining-work checklist (Phases 0.5–6) and how to proceed.

## Verification

- `packages/core`: typecheck clean + **27/27 unit tests pass**.
- `apps/mobile`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; runs on **Expo web** — clean build (1405 modules, 0 console errors), both light/dark themes, working tab navigation, shared core consumed live (season label, `NAV_ITEMS`, `roleLabel`).

## Not in scope (next; see MIGRATION.md)

Decision context: **no SEO required** → end state is a single RN/Expo codebase for web + iOS + Android, retiring the web app at parity.

- Phase 0.5 spikes: collab editor in `react-native-webview`, native Google Sign-In, fonts.
- Phase 1: re-home Firestore data modules into `packages/core` behind an injected `db`; RN auth context/role gating.
- Phases 2–4: port screens (read screens → medium → high-risk: Journey/Messages/Board).
- Phase 5: EAS app-store builds. Phase 6: unify web onto Expo Router, retire the old web app.

## How to run

```bash
cd packages/core && npm install && npm test   # 27 tests
cd apps/mobile && npm install && npx expo start   # i / a / w, or Expo Go
```

title: fix(security): gate unauthenticated API endpoints, verify webhooks, wire up ESLint
label: CLOSED
body:
## Summary

A repo-wide security/bug audit found several Express endpoints in `server.ts` running with **no authentication** despite using the Firebase Admin SDK (which bypasses Firestore security rules entirely). This PR closes those gaps and picks up a couple of adjacent bug fixes and infra quick wins found in the same pass.

### Security
- `/api/webhook/logs` and `/api/analyze-notes` now require a verified Firebase ID token belonging to an admin (matching their existing admin-only client-side gating). Previously anyone could pull raw webhook/contact PII, or dump the entire contact + user roster into a Gemini prompt, unauthenticated.
- `/api/quick-add` now derives the attributed user from a verified ID token instead of trusting a client-supplied `userId`/`userName` (which anyone could forge to impersonate a teammate) — falling back to a generic "External Automation" label for legitimate unauthenticated callers (curl / Siri / Android Shortcuts), preserving that documented use case.
- Added Twilio request-signature verification (`TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`) for `/api/webhook/sms` and an optional group allow-list (`GROUPME_GROUP_ID`) for `/api/webhook/groupme`. Both are no-ops until the env var is configured, matching the existing GitHub-webhook convention. New `src/lib/twilioVerify.ts` + unit tests.

### Bug fixes
- Added the missing `activities` composite Firestore index (`targetId` + `createdAt`) so the contact Activity tab's query stops silently depending on an out-of-band index; the rules-deploy CI workflow now also deploys `firestore.indexes.json`.
- The Activity tab now surfaces load errors via `handleFirestoreError`, matching the other tabs, instead of only logging to console.

### Infra
- Wired up ESLint (flat config: TypeScript, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, and the already-installed-but-never-configured `@firebase/eslint-plugin-security-rules` for `firestore.rules`). Split the old `lint` script into `typecheck` (tsc) and `lint` (eslint); CI now runs typecheck, lint, tests, and `build`.
- Fixed a stale `.env.local` reference in the README (actual convention is `.env`).

### Deliberately left alone (verified, not bugs)
- The notifications rule's `ALL_ADMINS` create branch — it's the public sign-up form notifying admins, not an accidental hole.
- `database.rules.json` — RTDB rules can't query Firestore roles, so tightening this risks re-breaking a previously-fixed regression (see CHANGELOG). A real fix needs a custom-claims mirror via a Cloud Function, which is a separate project.
- `vite` appearing in both `dependencies` and `devDependencies` — load-bearing, since the production Docker image runs `npm ci --only=production` and `server.ts` statically imports `vite`.
- The phone-validation "stale value" bug and an "un-normalized Timestamp" bug flagged by an initial pass both turned out to be false positives on closer inspection.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — passes
- [x] `npm run lint` — passes (0 errors, 246 pre-existing warnings surfaced for future cleanup)
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 743 passed, 56 skipped (emulator-gated rules tests)
- [x] `npx vitest run --coverage` — ~87.06% statements, above the 87% ratcheted threshold
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds
- [ ] Deploy `firestore.indexes.json` to the live project (via the rules-deploy workflow on merge to `main`) and confirm the contact Activity tab loads without a "requires an index" error
- [ ] Set `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` / `GROUPME_GROUP_ID` in the deployment environment if SMS/GroupMe quick-add is in active use, to actually enable the new verification

body:
Implements **Sessions 5 & 6** from the design spec (handoff `PLAN.md`), ported into the real TypeScript/Firestore app.

## Session 5 — Gatherings: managed kinds + edit
- **Managed gathering types** are now a team-shared Firestore collection (`gatheringTypes`) instead of hardcoded constants — auto-seeded with the four classic kinds, mirroring the `stages` taxonomy. New `src/lib/gatheringTypes.ts`.
- **"Manage kinds"** modal (`ManageGatheringTypesModal`) — create / rename / remove kinds. Renaming a kind **remaps every past gathering** carrying the old name (batch update of `events`).
- **Edit a gathering** (`EditEventModal`) — name / kind / date / location, with an edit affordance next to the existing delete in `Attendance`.
- The managed list now drives the type pills in `AddEventModal` and the filter pills in `Attendance`.
- **Recurrence already existed** in `AddEventModal` (daily/weekly/monthly + batch series) and is left untouched.

## Session 6 — Club rush + seasons
- A **season** (Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter + year) is auto-derived from today's date, with a team-wide, publicly-readable `settings/season` doc holding the override + club-rush flag. New `src/lib/seasons.ts`.
- A **"Season · '26"** strip under the brand in the sidebar (`SeasonChip`): managers get a popover to override the season / toggle club rush; everyone else sees it read-only.
- New sign-ups from both the **public Sign-up** and **Quick Add** are stamped with the season cohort tag (e.g. `Fall '26`, plus `Club Rush` during intake) via the existing `tags` field — **no contacts-rules change**.

## Firestore rules
- New `gatheringTypes` block — read by approved users, create/update/delete by managers.
- New publicly-readable `settings/{docId}` block — `read: if true` (so the public sign-up reflects the season), write restricted to managers and the `season` doc id.
- Both deploy via the existing Deploy-Firestore-Rules CI job.

## Tests
- New suites: `gatheringTypes`, `seasons`, `ManageGatheringTypesModal`, `EditEventModal`, `SeasonChip`, plus emulator rules tests for both new rule blocks.
- Updated `AddEventModal` / `Attendance` / `SignUp` / `NewContactModal` tests for the managed types + season tagging.
- **734 tests pass**, coverage thresholds hold (~89% lines); `tsc` + `npm run build` clean.

## Reviewer notes
- ⚠️ The `settings/season` and `gatheringTypes` rules are **new**. Until this branch's rules deploy on merge, reading `settings/season` returns a benign `permission-denied`; the UI degrades gracefully (season still derives client-side, override/club-rush fall back to defaults). After deploy it's silent. Verified locally — `/signup` renders "Christian Fellowship · Summer '26" correctly.
- No new `Contact` field — the cohort lives in the existing `tags` array, so no contacts-rules change.

title: fix(rules): unblock Deploy Firestore Rules CI (stale DD11 + contact validation bug)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Why

The **Deploy Firestore Rules** workflow gates its deploy job on emulator-backed rules tests (`needs: test-rules`). Those tests have been **red since #100 (2026-06-25)**, so the deploy job has been skipped — **production Firestore rules have not auto-published in over a month.** Two tests were failing in the latest run.

## What was broken

1. **`lets a full-timer mark a contact reviewed (bool only)` — real rules bug.** `isValidContact` validated optional fields with `data.x == null`, which *errors* (`Property x is undefined`) on an **absent** key in a partial-update merged doc rather than returning false. Result: a full-timer couldn't flip `reviewed` on any contact that lacked a `phone`.

2. **`DD11: Prevents PII Scraping by Viewer` — stale test.** #100/#102 deliberately relaxed `users` reads to `isApprovedUser()` because the app now needs it: the Community landing page lists full-timers (`LandingCommunity.tsx`) and the messaging member-pickers (`CreateChatModal.tsx`) query the `users` collection as plain approved users (incl. viewers). The rule is intentional; the test was asserting the old behavior.

## What changed (`firestore.rules` + `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts`)

- **`isValidContact`**: guard optional fields with `!('x' in data)` first, matching the pattern already used by `isValidPrayer` / `isValidTask`.
- **Contact `update` rule**: fixing the bug above revealed that **`DD3` (ghost-field injection) only ever "passed" by accident** — the same `phone` error was incidentally blocking the write, not real protection. Made it real with a **diff-based allowlist** (`incoming().diff(existing()).affectedKeys().hasOnly([...])`) covering every field the edit paths actually write (traced across SignUp, NewContactModal incl. its non-typed `serverCreatedAt`, ContactDetailsModal, Directory, OutreachBoard, Attendance, LogInteractionModal). Using the *diff* (not the whole merged doc) keeps contacts carrying legacy fields editable; only newly-introduced unknown keys (e.g. `pwned`) are rejected.
- **`DD11`**: rewritten to encode the *actual* intended boundary — approved members (incl. viewers) **may** read peers, unapproved users **may not**, and a viewer **cannot tamper** with another member's profile.

## Verification

- `firebase emulators:exec --only firestore … "vitest run src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts"` → **40/40 pass** (ran with `firebase-tools@14` locally since the local JDK is 17 and CI's `@^15` needs JDK 21 — same emulator, no repo change).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Note for reviewers

The contact `update` rule allows any `isOperator()` (Students) to set `reviewed`, while the "walking together" feature describes review as a **full-timer** action. No app code writes `reviewed` yet (the rule is ahead of the planned Session-2 UI), so this PR keeps the existing `isOperator()` scope — worth deciding whether to tighten to `isAdmin()` when that UI lands.

title: fix: safely access optional/nullable fields in tasks rules
label: CLOSED
body:
This PR fixes the failing Firestore security rules tests in the CI pipeline.

### Root Cause
Directly accessing optional/nullable fields (e.g., `data.contactId`) in Firestore Security Rules throws a runtime evaluation error if the field is missing (undefined) on the document being validated. This caused the recently added rules tests for tasks/team to-dos to fail since they create tasks without specifying all the optional contact/assignee/interaction fields.

### Solution
Modified `isValidTask` in `firestore.rules` to use `data.get('fieldName', null)` for all optional/nullable fields. This returns `null` safely if the key does not exist rather than throwing a runtime error.

title: fix(notifications): render the bell with the app's design tokens
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Fixes the notification bell, which was rendering unstyled — the reported **"notification bell is off."**

`NotificationCenter.tsx` had been ported from the Claude Design but kept the **design's** raw CSS variable names (`--accent`, `--bg-elev`, `--panel`, `--shadow-pop`, `--text-dim`, …). None of those tokens are defined anywhere in the app — it uses the Material/`@theme` tokens in `src/index.css`. So the bell rendered with ~38 undefined `var(--…)` references: **no panel background, an invisible badge, and missing accent / shadow / border colors.** It was the only file in `src/` referencing the design tokens.

## Why this approach

The app's tokens turned out to be the design's tokens **renamed**, with exactly matching light/dark values — so this is a faithful 1:1 remap, not a redesign. Keeping the app's single token system (rather than introducing the design's parallel namespace) matches every other component and honors the handoff guidance ("recreate in the target's tech; match visual output, not the prototype's internals").

Representative mappings:

| design token | → app token / utility |
|---|---|
| `--accent` | `primary` (tone fills `stage-accent`) |
| `--accent-soft` / `--accent-line` | `stage-accent-soft` / `primary/30` |
| `--text` / `--text-dim` / `--text-mute` | `on-surface` / `on-surface-variant` / `outline` |
| `--bg-elev` / `--panel` / `--panel-2` | `surface-container` / `surface` / `surface-container-high` |
| `--border` / `--border-soft` | `outline-variant` |
| `--violet/amber/teal` (+soft) | `stage-violet/amber/teal` (+soft) |
| `--success` / `--success-soft` | `success` / `success/10` |
| `--shadow-pop` | `shadow-xl` (app popover convention) |

No layout, geometry, or logic changes. Also added two small design-fidelity touches: `text-wrap: pretty` on body/empty text and a `focus-visible` ring on notification items.

## Verification

- `NotificationCenter.test.tsx` → **14/14 pass**; `tsc --noEmit` clean; no console errors.
- Computed styles match the design's values in **light and dark** (e.g. badge `rgb(58,90,130)`, panel `rgb(244,246,251)` + `shadow-xl`, dark panel `rgb(27,32,39)`).
- Visually confirmed in the mobile strip, dark mode, and the desktop anchored dropdown.

## Notes for reviewer

- Single-file change: `src/components/layout/NotificationCenter.tsx`.
- The 15° bell-open tilt animation is **kept** (a micro-interaction the static design doesn't specify) — easy to drop if a strict match is preferred.
- The design source lives in-repo at `docs/design/project/` (`views/notifications.jsx`, `styles.css`) for cross-reference.

## What

Fixes the primary, actionable part of #4: the **Log out** control in the sidebar footer could be pushed below the fold on shorter viewports, leaving an admin/manager unable to log out or switch accounts.

Two utility-class additions in `src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx` — no logic changes:
- **Nav-items region**: add `min-h-0` so the existing `flex-1 … overflow-y-auto` container can actually shrink and scroll internally.
- **Footer**: add `shrink-0` so it keeps its intrinsic height and stays pinned.

## Why

PR #75 switched the nav-items container from `overflow-hidden` to `overflow-y-auto` to make it scrollable, but left out `min-h-0`. A flex child defaults to `min-height: auto` and refuses to shrink below its content height, so the scroll never engaged — the region grew past the `h-screen` nav and pushed the footer out of the clipped (`overflow-hidden`) sidebar. PR #75 did not close #4, consistent with the bug persisting.

With `min-h-0`, the `flex-1` region shrinks to `viewport − header − footer` and scrolls internally when items overflow; the footer (`mt-auto shrink-0`) stays pinned and visible. When items fit, behavior is unchanged.

## Scope

Part 1 (layout) only. Part 2 of #4 (intermittent re-login session-persistence race) is intentionally out of scope — the issue marks it low-confidence with no reliable repro.

## Verification

Verified in the browser preview, signed in as Full-timer (all 9 nav items):
- **500px-tall viewport (repro):** nav list scrolls internally (`clientHeight 243 < scrollHeight 412`, `min-h-0` present); **Log out** sits at `bottom: 436`, within the 500px viewport. Clicking it logged out and returned to the sign-in screen.
- **Collapsed icon-rail at 500px:** Log out icon + expand chevron stay pinned and visible — no regression.
- **Tall viewport (1000px):** nav region not scrollable (no double scrollbar), footer pinned.
- No console errors; HMR compiled cleanly.

Closes #4 (Part 1).

title: fix(views): consistent error state across data views (#45)
label: CLOSED
body:
Closes #45.

## Problem

`handleFirestoreError` (`src/lib/firebase.ts`) logs and then **throws**. PR #43 fixed the cases where `setLoading(false)` sat *after* the throw (dead code → skeleton stuck forever), but left a broader gap: there was **no consistent error state** across the data views. On a listener error, users got one of two bad outcomes:

1. **Stuck skeleton** — the listener that owns `setLoading(false)` errors, so loading never clears.
2. **Silent empty/partial list** — a *different* listener errors after loading already cleared, so the user just sees missing data with no signal anything failed.

There was no way to tell "no data yet" / "empty" / "load failed" apart, and no reusable error UI.

## Change

Chosen approach (issue's recommended Option 1): a shared error UI + reload, applied uniformly.

- **New shared component** `src/components/ui/DataLoadError.tsx` — a centered "Couldn't load {label}" card with an icon badge and a **Reload** button (defaults to `window.location.reload`), styled to match the existing `ErrorBoundary` / `FeedbackList` error patterns.
- **Per-view `error` state** in all 7 affected views. Each `onSnapshot` error callback now sets `error` + clears `loading` **before** calling `handleFirestoreError`, preserving the ordering invariant established in PR #43 (state is cleared before the throw). The error card renders with priority over the loading skeleton.
- **PrayerList**: both listeners previously had **no error callback at all** (silent failure) — now fixed.
- The 600/800ms loading delays in Attendance/Directory/OutreachBoard are dropped on the error path so failures surface immediately.
- Inline write-path error handling (UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE) is intentionally left unchanged — out of scope.

| View | Label |
|------|-------|
| Dashboard | the dashboard |
| MyDay | your day |
| History | history |
| Directory | contacts |
| OutreachBoard | the board |
| Attendance | attendance |
| PrayerList | the prayer list |

## Tests

- New `src/test/DataLoadError.test.tsx` (label render, custom `onRetry`, default reload).
- An error-path test in each affected view spec asserting the error card renders when a listener fails.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` (tsc) — clean
- `npm test` — **490 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failures**
- `npm run test:coverage` — thresholds hold: statements 88.18% (≥87), branches 78.08% (≥77), functions 84.23% (≥82), lines 89.81% (≥88); `src/components/ui` at 100%.

## Reviewer notes

Live-browser verification of the error card was skipped deliberately: the error state is only reachable on a real Firestore permission failure, which the local dev preview can't exercise without an authenticated session and broken rules. The normal render paths are unchanged and the error UI is fully unit-tested. The rendered card can be confirmed in this PR's Cloudflare preview.

title: feat(board): collapsible Pages panel, live previews, rich-paste matching (#66, #67, #70)
label: CLOSED
body:
Addresses three pieces of feedback on **The Board** (`/coordination`), all in `src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx` plus a small tested helper in `src/lib/markdown.ts`.

## #70 — Collapsible Pages panel
The Pages list was a fixed `300px` grid column with no way to hide it. It's now collapsible on desktop, persisted to `localStorage` (`board_pages_collapsed`) like the main sidebar. Collapse from a chevron in the **Pages** header; reopen from a button in the editor head. Mobile is unchanged (the list is already a stacked strip there).

## #66 — Live Pages-list preview
The row preview line and "X to do" count read the Firestore-persisted `md`, so the page you were editing showed stale content until the 1200ms debounced save landed. The **active** page's row now updates live (throttled ~300ms) from the editor's current Markdown — type, or check a `[ ]`, and its row reflects it immediately. Other pages still update on save as before.

## #67 — Rich-paste format matching
Pasting rich text (Google Docs, Notion, a webpage, a rendered AI reply) bypassed Markdown and went through ProseMirror's HTML parser, importing foreign markup/inline styles. Pasted HTML is now normalized through Markdown via `transformPastedHTML`: `turndown` → the editor's own Markdown parser → clean schema HTML. Includes `turndown` rules for Google Docs' style-based bold/italic (`font-weight`/`font-style` spans) and its fake-bold selection wrapper (`<b style="font-weight:normal">`). Internal editor copy/paste (`data-pm-slice`) is left to ProseMirror untouched.

**Out of scope:** GFM extras (tables, strikethrough, task-list checkboxes) would need `turndown-plugin-gfm`, not currently a dependency; core turndown covers the common rich-paste cases.

## Tests
- `src/test/markdown.test.ts`: new cases for `htmlToBoardMarkdown` (headings, bold/italic, lists, links, code, blockquote, Google Docs style-based bold/italic + fake-bold wrapper).
- `src/test/CoordinationNotes.test.tsx`: collapse/expand + persisted-preference tests for #70.
- `src/test/CoordinationNotesEditor.test.tsx` (new): a functional-editor seam that exercises the paste normalization (#67) and live-preview (#66) paths.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (482 passing), and `npm run test:coverage` (thresholds met) all green.

UI smoke test on this PR's Cloudflare Pages preview with an admin account (The Board is admin-gated and needs live Firebase, so it can't be exercised locally):
- Collapse the Pages panel → editor fills width; reopen from the editor head; reload → state persists.
- Type / check a task → that page's sidebar row preview + "to do" update live.
- Paste from Google Docs / a webpage → headings, bold, lists, links come through cleanly without foreign styling.

Closes #66
Closes #67
Closes #70

title: fix(board): keep Markdown toolbar visible when scrolling a long page (#65)
label: CLOSED
body:
## What & why

Fixes #65 — on **The Board** (`/coordination`), the Markdown formatting toolbar disappeared when scrolling down a long document.

**Root cause:** the editor workspace grid had no bounded height, so the whole page scrolled at the **window** level, while the toolbar's `sticky top-0` was anchored to a non-scrolling inner container. As the page scrolled, the toolbar scrolled away with it (measured: the toolbar's Bold button moved to `y ≈ -1045`, off-screen).

**Fix** (one line in `src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`): bound the workspace grid height on desktop with `lg:h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]`, and add `lg:grid-rows-1` so the single row resolves to `minmax(0,1fr)` instead of growing to content height. Both grid columns already used the `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` internal-scroll pattern — they just needed a height-bounded parent. Now the page list and document canvas scroll **internally** and the toolbar stays pinned.

## Verification

- **Desktop (1440×900):** scrolled the canvas 2000px → toolbar stays at `y=355` (unchanged, visible); canvas scrolls internally (`clientH=657`, `scrollH=4347`); window stays at 0. (Before: toolbar → `y ≈ -1045`.)
- **Mobile (375px):** unchanged — the new classes are `lg:`-scoped, so the grid keeps its auto height and the page scrolls normally. No console errors.
- **Tests:** added a regression test asserting the workspace carries the bounded-height classes; `tsc --noEmit` clean; full suite **462 passed / 17 skipped**.

## Notes for reviewer

- The `6rem` offset accounts for the `sticky` `h-16` TopBar plus a little breathing room; it's not pixel-critical — any bounded height engages the inner scroll. Floor of `min-h-[560px]` is retained for short viewports.
- Scope is desktop only by design; the mobile board is a single stacked column where a fixed-height editor would be cramped.

title: Auto-create a GitHub issue when feedback is submitted
label: CLOSED
body:
## Context / Problem
Feedback submitted through the in-app feedback module (the "Leave a note" FAB and the `/feedback` page) lands only in the Firestore `feedback` collection and the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`). There is no bridge into our engineering workflow, so actionable feedback has to be manually re-entered as GitHub issues. We want submissions to automatically open a GitHub issue in this repo so they show up in normal triage.

## Proposed behavior
When a user submits feedback, automatically open a GitHub issue in `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`:
- **Trigger on all four kinds** — thought, idea, "something's off", request.
- Map kind → labels: `off` → `bug`; `thought`/`idea`/`request` → `enhancement`; plus a new `feedback` label (needs creating).
- Title: short summary from the kind + first line of the message.
- Body: full message, submitter name/email, kind, and a link to the admin feedback entry.
- **Link back:** store the created issue's number/URL on the feedback doc and show a "View on GitHub" link in the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`).
- **Best-effort:** a GitHub failure must NOT block or revert the in-app success state (mirror the existing `logActivity` / `sendNotification` pattern).

## Suggested implementation
- Feedback is written client-side directly to Firestore today (`addDoc(collection(db, 'feedback'), …)`) in `src/components/FeedbackFAB.tsx` and `src/views/SubmitFeedback.tsx`. Keep that write; add a best-effort backend call afterward.
- Add an endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/feedback/github-issue`) in `server.ts` (Express on Cloud Run, fronted by the Cloudflare proxy in `functions/api/[[path]].ts`) that creates the issue via the GitHub REST API and writes the issue URL/number back onto the feedback doc with the Admin SDK.
- Store a `GITHUB_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with Issues:write on this repo, or a GitHub App token) as a Cloud Run env var — never exposed to the client.
- Create a `feedback` label in the repo.
- Add optional `githubIssueUrl` / `githubIssueNumber` to the `Feedback` type (`src/types.ts`) and render the link in `src/views/FeedbackList.tsx`.

## Acceptance criteria
- Submitting any feedback kind opens a GitHub issue with appropriate labels.
- The issue references the submitter + message; the feedback doc / admin list links to the issue.
- A GitHub outage does not break feedback submission.

---

title: ci(pr-agent): make gemini-2.5-flash the primary model
label: CLOSED
body:
## Why

PR-Agent's `/improve` step has been posting **"Failed to generate code suggestions for PR"** (e.g. on #53). The run logs show why:

- **Primary `gemini-2.5-pro` → HTTP 429:** `Quota exceeded ... limit: 0, model: gemini-2.5-pro` — the AI Studio `GEMINI_API_KEY` is free-tier, and **2.5-pro has zero free-tier quota**, so every call 429s instantly.
- **Fallback `gemini-2.5-flash` → HTTP 503:** `This model is currently experiencing high demand` (transient).

With both exhausted, PR-Agent gives up. Pro-on-a-free-key will *always* 429, so suggestions only ever appeared when the flash fallback happened to be up.

## Change

In [.github/workflows/pr_agent.yml](.github/workflows/pr_agent.yml):

- `CONFIG__MODEL`: `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` → **`gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`** (has free-tier quota).
- `CONFIG__FALLBACK_MODELS`: `["gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"]` → **`["gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite"]`** (lighter model for the transient flash 503s).

No other behavior change — `auto_review`/`auto_describe` stay off, `auto_improve` stays on.

## Notes

- Purely a CI/bot reliability fix; unrelated to any app code.
- Alternative not taken: enabling billing on the Gemini key (would make 2.5-pro usable). Flash-primary is the zero-cost fix.

title: fix(board): degrade editor to Firestore copy when RTDB is denied
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem

On The Board (`/coordination`), the left **Pages list** updated live across windows but the right **editor pane was blank**, with a flood of console errors:

```
[RtdbYjsProvider] initial load failed Error: Permission denied
transaction at /board_docs_rtdb/<id>/seeded failed: permission_denied
set at /board_docs_rtdb/<id>/awareness/<id> failed: permission_denied
```

## Root cause

Two layered issues:

1. **Infra (the live outage — not fixed by this PR):** the `Deploy Database Rules` workflow added in #52 **failed** (`Error: Failed to get details for project: sac-campus-hub`), so `database.rules.json` never reached the live RTDB, which then defaults to `.read/.write: false` and denies everything. The same `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret works for Firestore rules but lacks the IAM role the `--only database` path needs (**`roles/firebasedatabase.admin`** + `roles/firebase.viewer`). This must be granted and the workflow re-run for live collab to work.
2. **App resilience (fixed here):** the editor only seeds content into the Y.Doc for the client that wins the RTDB `seeded` transaction. When RTDB is denied, `claimSeed()` fails for everyone → `seedFromMd()` never runs → blank pane. `RtdbYjsProvider.bootstrap()` also swallowed the load error and still wired up presence, flooding the console.

The asymmetry (left works, right blank) is because the list reads `board_docs` from **Firestore** (rules deployed) while the editor rides on **RTDB/Yjs** (rules not live).

## Changes

- **`src/lib/yjsRtdbProvider.ts`** — `bootstrap()` tracks whether the initial RTDB read threw and surfaces it as a `degraded` flag to `onSynced(degraded)`; on degrade it skips wiring live listeners/presence (no permission_denied flood).
- **`src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx`** — `DocEditor` seeds from the Firestore `d.md` copy + `setLive(false)` when degraded, so a denied/offline RTDB shows the doc single-user instead of a blank pane. Reuses the existing `!rtdb` fallback pattern.
- **`database.rules.json`** — relax `board_docs_rtdb/$docId` read/write from `auth != null && email_verified === true` to **`auth != null`** (matches the admin route + Firestore `board_docs` gating; unverified admin accounts were being denied). Only takes effect once the database-rules deploy succeeds.

## Reviewer notes

- The relaxed rule broadens RTDB access to any *authenticated* user who knows a docId; acceptable for this internal admin tool since the UI route and Firestore already restrict `board_docs` to admins, and the RTDB node only holds Yjs deltas.
- **This PR does not restore live collab on its own** — the IAM grant + database-rules re-deploy (item 1 above) is still required. What it does fix is the blank pane: with the fix, a denied RTDB degrades to single-user Firestore-backed editing.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Test suite: 69 passed. The only failures are two pre-existing `OutreachBoard` suites failing at `getDatabase()` in `src/lib/firebase.ts:24` (jsdom env quirk when `databaseURL` is set) — confirmed they fail identically on `main`; neither touches a file changed here.
- End-to-end: best checked on this PR's Cloudflare Pages preview. Since the live RTDB is currently denying, the preview naturally exercises the fallback — the editor should show content with a "live off" state instead of a blank pane.

title: fix(board): unblock RTDB live-collab + auto-deploy database rules
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Fixes The Board's live-collaboration writes failing with RTDB `permission_denied` on `/board_docs_rtdb/{docId}/updates` and `/awareness`.

- **Broaden the `board_docs_rtdb` rule** in [`database.rules.json`](database.rules.json) to any signed-in, email-verified user (was: `auth.token.admin` custom claim or the hardcoded super-admin email).
- **Add [`deploy-database-rules.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy-database-rules.yml)** — auto-deploys `database.rules.json` on merge to `main`, mirroring `deploy-firestore-rules.yml`.
- **Changelog** entry under `[Unreleased] → Fixed`.

## Why

Two compounding causes:

1. **RTDB rules were never deployed.** Firestore rules auto-deploy on merge (`deploy-firestore-rules.yml`), but there was no equivalent for `database.rules.json`, so the live RTDB kept its default deny-all rules.
2. **The rule was built on a signal the app never populates.** The app establishes admin via a Firestore `users/{uid}.role == 'admin'` lookup (`firestore.rules`, `hasRole`) and **never sets the `admin` custom claim** (the only backend is a Cloudflare→Cloud Run proxy; no Firebase Admin SDK / Cloud Function). RTDB rules can't read Firestore, so Firestore-role admins like `cisa-ft` were denied **even after deploying**.

### Security note (intentional relaxation)

The board **page** stays admin-gated in the UI and durable content stays admin-gated in Firestore (`board_docs`). Only the ephemeral CRDT transport in RTDB is opened to authenticated, verified users — an accepted tradeoff given there's no custom-claim/backend infra to bridge Firestore roles into RTDB.

## Reviewer notes

- ⚠️ **IAM prerequisite for CI:** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` needs `roles/firebasedatabase.admin` on `sac-campus-hub` (in addition to the `firebaserules.admin` it has for Firestore) or the new deploy workflow will 401 — fails loudly, not silently.
- The rule was **already deployed manually** to `sac-campus-hub-default-rtdb` (via `firebase deploy --only database` with Owner credentials), so prod is unblocked ahead of this merge; the workflow keeps it from going stale going forward.

title: fix(firestore): drop fieldOverrides so deploy works on Enterprise edition
label: CLOSED
body:
## Problem

`firebase deploy` against the `sac-campus-hub` project fails during the Firestore **index** step:

```
Error: Request to https://firestore.googleapis.com/v1/projects/sac-campus-hub/databases/ai-studio-43298cca-4d70-4c5d-bada-c10ab66ab897/collectionGroups/comments/fields/createdAt?updateMask=indexConfig had HTTP Error: 400, Enterprise Edition does not support updating field index configuration.
```

## Root cause

The target database (`ai-studio-43298cca-4d70-4c5d-bada-c10ab66ab897`, used by the app via `firestoreDatabaseId` and by deploys via `firebase.json`) is a Firestore **Enterprise edition** database (AI Studio creates these). Enterprise edition does not auto-create single-field indexes and does **not** support the single-field "field index configuration" update API.

The `fieldOverrides` block in `firestore.indexes.json` uses exactly that API, so the deploy 400s on the new `comments/createdAt` override. The sibling `interactions/createdAt` override didn't error only because that index already existed in the DB (no update sent); `comments/createdAt` is new (added alongside The Board rebuild) and the create request is rejected.

## Fix

Remove the entire `fieldOverrides` array (both `interactions` and `comments` entries). The composite `indexes` array is **unchanged** — composite indexes are supported on Enterprise edition and were never the problem.

## Verification

`firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project sac-campus-hub` was run against the live project. The index step now completes with no 400. Verbatim tail of the CLI output:

```
i  firestore: deploying indexes...
✔  firestore: deployed indexes in firestore.indexes.json successfully for ai-studio-43298cca-4d70-4c5d-bada-c10ab66ab897 database

✔  Deploy complete!
```

JSON was also validated with `jq` and confirmed to contain no remaining `fieldOverrides` entries.

## ⚠️ Required manual follow-up (a human must do this after merge)

The app genuinely needs a **collection-group `createdAt` (DESCENDING)** index on the `comments` collection. It is queried via `collectionGroup(db, 'comments')` + `orderBy('createdAt', 'desc')` in:

- `src/views/Dashboard.tsx`
- `src/views/MyDay.tsx`
- `src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx`
- `src/views/Directory.tsx`

On Enterprise edition this index **cannot** be created via `fieldOverrides` / CLI field-config (that's the unsupported API this PR removes). It must be created **out-of-band**, by one of:

- Firebase console → Firestore → Indexes, or
- `gcloud firestore indexes` (against the `ai-studio-...` database), or
- loading one of the views above and following the "create index" link Firestore returns in the runtime error.

**Until that index exists, those views' `comments` queries will fail at runtime with "query requires an index."**

## Scope

Standalone, independent of any bundle-optimization / lazy-loading work.

title: perf(bundle): lazy-load The Board editor view to split it from the initial bundle
label: CLOSED
body:
## What

Lazy-load the admin-only **The Board** view (`/coordination`, `CoordinationNotes`) so the TipTap + Yjs + ProseMirror editor stack is code-split out of the initial JS bundle.

- `src/App.tsx`: static `import CoordinationNotes` → `React.lazy(() => import(...))`, and the `/coordination` route element is wrapped in `<React.Suspense>` with a `Skeleton` fallback.
- `vite.config.ts`: added `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` (path-matching function) that groups `@tiptap/*`, `prosemirror-*`, `tiptap-markdown`, `yjs`, `y-protocols`, `y-prosemirror`, and `lib0` into a single `board-editor` chunk.

## Why

The Board rebuild (#49) pulled in TipTap/Yjs/ProseMirror, all consumed **only** by `CoordinationNotes`. They were shipping in the initial bundle (~2.3 MB / 651 KB gzip), tripping Vite's >500 KB chunk warning and slowing first load for every user — including the majority who never open the admin-only Board.

## Impact (from `npm run build`)

| chunk | raw | gzip | when it loads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `board-editor-*.js` | ~666 KB | ~224 KB | lazily, only with `/coordination` |
| `CoordinationNotes-*.js` | ~34 KB | ~10 KB | lazily, only with `/coordination` |
| `index-*.js` (initial) | ~1,621 KB | **~417 KB** | first load |

Initial bundle gzip drops from ~651 KB → ~417 KB; the ~224 KB gzip of editor code no longer ships up front.

## Verification

- `npm run build` ✅ — editor deps confirmed in their own `board-editor` chunk; the lazy import resolved correctly.
- `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) ✅ clean.
- `npm test` ✅ 74 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failures.
- Dev-server smoke test ✅ — app boots, login renders, zero console errors. `CoordinationNotes` confirmed to use a `default` export (required by `React.lazy`).

## Notes for reviewer

- I used a `manualChunks` **function** (path match) rather than the package-name list, because the real deps don't match a naive list (no direct `@tiptap/core`; several `@tiptap/extension-*`; ProseMirror arrives via `@tiptap/pm`). The regex catches the whole family without future maintenance.
- The >500 KB warning still prints for two chunks: the lazy `board-editor` (expected — it no longer affects initial load) and the main `index` chunk, whose remaining bulk is **Firebase**, not the editor. Fully silencing it would mean splitting Firebase into a vendor chunk — intentionally left out of scope here.
- The authenticated `/coordination` render wasn't exercised locally (it's admin-gated behind Firebase auth); per team convention that UI check is best done on the Cloudflare Pages preview for this PR.

Rebuilds **The Board** (`/coordination` → `CoordinationNotes.tsx`) to match the Claude Design bundle's `BoardFT`. The old *coordination-sessions* model (categorized agenda, delegated tasks, push-to-next-session) is replaced with **a folder of dated Markdown pages — one running document per gathering** — edited in a Google-Docs-style editor, beside the **unchanged** Notes & learnings archive.

> Note: this is the page literally titled "The Board" at `/coordination` — not `/board` "The Journey" (the kanban `OutreachBoard`).

## How it works (Tier 2 — true multiplayer)

```
TipTap editor ⇄ Y.Doc ⇄ RTDB provider ⇄ RTDB /board_docs_rtdb/{id}   (live edits + cursors/presence)
                  │
                  └─(debounced)→ derive markdown → Firestore board_docs/{id}.md   (durable: list, previews, search)
```

- **Live editor** — TipTap (ProseMirror) + Yjs CRDT: formatting toolbar (Title/Heading/Body, bold/italic, bullet/numbered/checklist/quote), clickable checklists, read-only Markdown source toggle, autosave, remote presence + cursors.
- **Transport** — purpose-built Yjs↔Firebase **RTDB** provider (`src/lib/yjsRtdbProvider.ts`): append-only update log + ephemeral awareness that self-cleans on disconnect, single-writer seed guard. No new server (works from the static Cloudflare frontend).
- **Durable store** — new admin-only Firestore **`board_docs`** collection holds the markdown (debounced save); powers the Pages list, previews, "N to do", and Notes search.
- **Graceful degradation** — if RTDB isn't configured, the editor falls back to Firestore-only editing; the page is never broken by realtime issues.

## Changes

- `src/views/CoordinationNotes.tsx` — full rewrite (Pages list + TipTap `DocEditor` + presence + create/delete; Notes & learnings archive kept, restyled to the design's note cards w/ amber learnings + "1 yr" recall badge).
- `src/lib/board.ts` — `BoardDoc` type + group/status/label helpers; `src/lib/markdown.ts` — `mdPreview`/`mdOpenTasks`.
- `src/lib/yjsRtdbProvider.ts` — Yjs↔RTDB provider.
- `src/lib/firebase.ts` — opt-in RTDB init via `VITE_FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL` (+ `.env.example`).
- `firestore.rules` — admin-only `board_docs` rules; `database.rules.json` + `firebase.json` — RTDB rules (gated on the `admin` custom claim).
- `src/index.css` — `.bdoc-prose` editor content styles + collaboration-cursor styles, themed on app tokens (light/dark).
- `src/test/firestore.rules.test.ts` — `board_docs` rules cases.
- `package.json` — TipTap v3, Yjs, y-protocols, tiptap-markdown.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` (tsc) ✅ · `npm run build` ✅ · `npm test` → 74 passed ✅
- Firestore emulator rules tests → **17 passed**, incl. 4 new `board_docs` cases (admin CRUD / minimal doc / viewer denied / malformed rejected).
- Browser, signed in as the admin test user: editor mounts and is fully interactive (typing, toolbar checklist, checkbox toggle, Saved, Markdown toggle) in **light + dark**.

## Follow-ups / reviewer notes

- ⚠️ **Live collab needs infra**: enable **Realtime Database** on the project, set `VITE_FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL`, and `firebase deploy --only database` (RTDB rules do **not** auto-deploy). Until then the page runs Firestore-only (edits save + sync, no live co-cursors).
- Firestore `board_docs` rules deploy automatically on merge to `main` (existing workflow).
- Old `board_sessions` collection/rules left in place but unused by the UI — data migration is a separate follow-up.
- Bundle grew (~2.3 MB / 651 KB gzip) now that TipTap/Yjs are in the main chunk — recommend a follow-up to lazy-load the Board route.

title: Move Firestore-rules deploy to keyless auth (Workload Identity Federation)
label: CLOSED
body:
## Goal
Replace the long-lived service-account **key** used by the Firestore-rules deploy with **keyless auth via Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** — GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for short-lived GCP credentials, so there's no JSON key stored in a GitHub secret.

> Terminology: for CI/workloads this is **Workload Identity Federation** (a *Workload* Identity Pool + OIDC provider). "Workforce pools" are the sibling feature for human users from an external IdP — not what we want here.

## Why
Follow-up to #44 / #46. Today [`.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml) (lines 76–79) authenticates with:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
  with:
    credentials_json: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}
```

That secret holds a **long-lived private key** for `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Downsides:
- A non-expiring credential sits in GitHub secrets; if it leaks, it's valid until manually revoked.
- No rotation story — keys silently age forever (`validBeforeTime: 9999`).
- During #46 we hit exactly the failure mode this invites: the secret was holding the *wrong* SA's key and nobody could tell (secrets are write-only). WIF removes the key entirely.

With WIF: tokens are minted per-run, expire in minutes, and access is scoped by an attribute condition to **this repo only**.

## Current state (already in place)
- Deploy SA `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` exists and holds the 3 roles a rules deploy needs: `roles/firebaserules.admin`, `roles/datastore.indexAdmin`, `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer`.
- Project: `sac-campus-hub` (project number `914549253362`).
- Repo: `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.

## Setup (one-time, GCP side)
```bash
PROJECT_ID=sac-campus-hub
PROJECT_NUMBER=914549253362
POOL=github-actions
PROVIDER=github
REPO=Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker
SA=github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# 1. Workload Identity Pool
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create "$POOL" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --display-name="GitHub Actions"

# 2. OIDC provider, locked to this repo (the attribute-condition is required)
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc "$PROVIDER" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" \
  --display-name="GitHub" \
  --issuer-uri="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository" \
  --attribute-condition="assertion.repository == '${REPO}'"

# 3. Let this repo's tokens impersonate the deploy SA
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \
  --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL}/attribute.repository/${REPO}"
```
Provider resource name for the workflow:
`projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github`

## Workflow change
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write        # required for OIDC

# ...in the deploy job, replace the auth step:
  - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
    uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    with:
      project_id: sac-campus-hub
      workload_identity_provider: projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github
      service_account: github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
The action still exports `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (now a short-lived token file), so the `firebase deploy` step needs no change. Update the file's header comment (lines 6–9) which currently describes the key-based flow.

## Cutover & cleanup (after a green WIF run)
- [ ] Confirm `workflow_dispatch` + a real push both deploy green via WIF.
- [ ] Delete the GitHub secret `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`.
- [ ] Delete `github-action@`'s user-managed key `63fafb9d4edaa333c8060133ed5814a41419b9e9`
      (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete …`) so no long-lived key remains.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WIF pool + OIDC provider created, scoped to `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`.
- [ ] `github-action@` granted `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` for the repo's principalSet.
- [ ] Workflow uses `workload_identity_provider` + `service_account`, with `id-token: write`.
- [ ] Deploy is green with **no** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret present.
- [ ] Old key and secret removed.

_Refs: #44 (auto-deploy), #46 (credential validation + the wrong-key incident)._

title: fix(board): reconcile Journey header count + prefill stage on "Add to {stage}" (#29)
label: CLOSED
body:
Closes #29 — two follow-ups from the Outreach Board reskin (#28), both reskin-only-out-of-scope at the time.

## 1. Header total now reconciles with the per-stage breakdown
The prose header bolds **every** contact on the board (`filteredContacts.length`, which includes unmapped/unassigned people), but the per-stage breakdown only summed the **active** stages — so the numbers didn't add up whenever the "Unassigned" column had anyone (e.g. *"10 people walking it — 2 first contact, 3 second contact, 3 regular"* → sums to 8).

The column footer buttons called `openNewContact()` with no stage, so *"Add to Regular"* landed the new contact in the modal's default stage — the label overpromised. Same for the Unassigned column's *"Add to Unassigned"*.

Fix: thread an optional `initialStage` through `openNewContact` → `NewContactModal` and prefill the stage `<select>`. Calls without a stage (Dashboard / Directory / Global Search "Add someone") keep defaulting to the first stage.

Also wraps two bare `onClick={openNewContact}` handlers (Dashboard, Directory) in arrow functions — now that `openNewContact` takes an arg, passing it directly would feed the click **event** in as `initialStage`. (tsc caught this.)

## Tests
- `OutreachBoardBreakdown.test.tsx` (new) — feeds 2 + 3 + 2-unassigned contacts and asserts the header reads `… 2 first contact, 3 regular, 2 not yet placed.` summing to the bold **7**.
- `NewContactModal.test.tsx` — asserts the stage prefills from `initialStage` ("Unassigned") and falls back to the first stage when none is given.
